fields.name: CLSIZE
fields.text: Cache line size.

fields.name: CSIZE
fields.text: Cache size.

fields.name: LCKDOWN
fields.text: Lock-down support; a 0 turns the lock-down feature off, a 1 turns it on.

fields.name: WAYNUM
fields.text: How the cache is mapped: direct or set associative.

fields.name: RRP
fields.text: Round robin policy; a 1 turns it on, a 0 off.

fields.name: GCLK
fields.text: Dynamic clock gating; a 1 turns it on, a 0 off.

fields.name: CSIZESW
fields.text: Sets the cache size from software.

fields.name: DCDIS
fields.text: A 1 turns data caching off; a 0 turns it on.

fields.name: ICDIS
fields.text: A 1 turns instruction caching off; a 0 turns it on.

fields.name: CEN
fields.text: A 1 turns the CMCC on; a 0 turns it off.

fields.name: CSTS
fields.text: Cache controller status; a write does nothing.

fields.name: LCKWAY
fields.text: One bit per way; a set bit locks that way.

fields.name: INVALL
fields.text: A 1 invalidates every cache entry; a 0 does nothing.

fields.name: WAY
fields.text: Picks the way whose entry at INDEX is invalidated.

fields.name: INDEX
fields.text: The cache index to invalidate.

fields.name: MODE
fields.text: Picks what the monitor counter counts.

fields.name: MENABLE
fields.text: A 1 starts the monitor counter; a 0 stops it.

fields.name: SWRST
fields.text: A 1 clears the monitor event counter; a 0 does nothing.

fields.name: EVENT_CNT
fields.text: The current count of the monitor event counter.

fields.name: CE
fields.text: A 1 starts a chip erase; a 0 does nothing.

fields.name: MBIST
fields.text: A 1 starts the memory built-in self-test; a 0 does nothing.

fields.name: CRC
fields.text: A 1 starts a 32-bit CRC calculation; a 0 does nothing.

fields.name: SWRST
fields.text: A 1 resets the DSU; a 0 does nothing.

fields.name: PERR
fields.text: Set when a command not permitted in the protected state is given; a 1 clears it, a 0 does nothing.

fields.name: FAIL
fields.text: Set when a DSU operation fails; a 1 clears it, a 0 does nothing.

fields.name: BERR
fields.text: Set on a bus error; a 1 clears it, a 0 does nothing.

fields.name: CRSTEXT
fields.text: Set when a debug adapter is cold-plugged, which lengthens the CPU reset phase; a 1 clears it, a 0 does nothing.

fields.name: DONE
fields.text: Set when a DSU operation finishes; a 1 clears it, a 0 does nothing.

fields.name: CELCK
fields.text: Reads 1 while chip erase is locked, 0 when unlocked; writes do nothing.

fields.name: HPE
fields.text: Reads 1 while hot-plugging is on; it clears when the SWCLK pin function changes, and only a power reset or external reset sets it again. Writes do nothing.

fields.name: DCCD
fields.text: One bit per debug communication channel: set when that DCC is written, cleared when it is read. Writes do nothing.

fields.name: DBGPRES
fields.text: Set when a debugger probe is detected and never cleared afterwards. Writes do nothing.

fields.name: PROT
fields.text: Reads 1 from power-up on a protected device (Security Bit set) and 0 from power-up on an unprotected one. Writes do nothing.

fields.name: ADDR
fields.text: Word start address for a memory operation.

fields.name: AMOD
fields.text: Access mode; its meaning depends on the operation, CRC32 or MBIST.

fields.name: LENGTH
fields.text: Length of a memory operation, in words.

fields.name: DATA
fields.text: Starting value for a memory operation, or its result.

fields.name: DATA
fields.text: Debug communication channel data.

fields.name: PROCESSOR
fields.text: Identifies the processor; reads 0x6 on this part, the Arm Cortex-M4F.

fields.name: FAMILY
fields.text: Product family from the ordering code; 0x0 for SAM D5x, 0x3 for SAM E5x.

fields.name: SERIES
fields.text: Product series from the ordering code.

fields.name: DIE
fields.text: Identifies the die family.

fields.name: REVISION
fields.text: Die revision number. It is separate from the device variant, the last letter of the ordering code: the variant marks functional differences, the revision marks changes to the die.

fields.name: DEVSEL
fields.text: Identifies the device within its product family and series; the codes differ per series: SAM D51, SAM E51, SAM E53, SAM E54.

fields.name: ETBRAMEN
fields.text: ETB RAM enable: a 1 sets aside the first 32 KB of RAM as the trace ETB buffer.

fields.name: DCCDMALEVEL
fields.text: Picks when the DCC DMA trigger rises.

fields.name: LQOS
fields.text: Priority of memory accesses.

fields.name: DCFG
fields.text: Device configuration.

registers.name: ENTRY0
registers.title: CoreSight ROM Table Entry x
notes: The register's reset value is also given as 0x9F0FC002.

fields.name: ADDOFF
fields.text: Base address of the component, as an offset from this ROM table's base address.

fields.name: FMT
fields.text: Always reads 1: the ROM table is 32-bit.

fields.name: EPRES
fields.text: Tells whether an entry is present at this ROM table location. On an unprotected device, set at power-up means no entry is present, and cleared at power-up means an entry is present.

fields.name: END
fields.text: Marks the end of the CoreSight ROM table entries.

fields.name: SMEMP
fields.text: Tells whether system memory sits on the bus the ROM table connects to. From power-up it reads 1 on an unprotected device, so a debug adapter can reach system memory, and 0 on a protected one, so it cannot.

fields.name: FKBC
fields.text: Always reads 0: the component takes one 4 KB block.

fields.name: JEPCC
fields.text: Always reads 0.

fields.name: PARTNBL
fields.text: Always reads 0xD0, marking a DSU instance.

fields.name: JEPIDCL
fields.text: Always reads 0xF; the JEP-106 identity code is 0x1F.

fields.name: PARTNBH
fields.text: Always reads 0xC, marking a DSU instance.

fields.name: REVISION
fields.text: Peripheral revision; begins at 0x0 and goes up by one at each major or minor revision.

fields.name: JEPU
fields.text: Always reads 1: a JEP-106 code is used.

fields.name: JEPIDCH
fields.text: Always reads 0x1; the JEP-106 identity code is 0x1F.

fields.name: REVAND
fields.text: Always reads 0x0.

fields.name: CUSMOD
fields.text: Always reads 0x0.

fields.name: PREAMBLEB0
fields.text: Always reads 0x0D.

fields.name: CCLASS
fields.text: Always reads 0x1: this CoreSight component is a ROM table.

fields.name: PREAMBLE
fields.text: Always reads 0x0.

fields.name: PREAMBLEB2
fields.text: Always reads 0x05.

fields.name: PREAMBLEB3
fields.text: Always reads 0xB1.

fields.name: SWRST
fields.text: A 1 returns every GCLK register to its power-reset state, except generic clocks and generators locked by PCHCTRLm.WRTLOCK; a 0 does nothing. The reset is synchronized, and CTRLA.SWRST and SYNCBUSY.SWRST both clear when it is done.

fields.name: GENCTRLn
fields.text: One bit per generator: set while GENCTRLn is synchronizing between clock domains, cleared when that or a clock switch is done.

fields.name: SWRST
fields.text: Set while CTRLA.SWRST is synchronizing between clock domains, cleared when done.

registers.name: GENCTRLn
registers.title: Generator Control
notes: The register's reset value is also given as 0x00000106.
Controls generator n, n = 0 to 11.
After a power reset GENCTRL0 is 0x00000106 and the others 0x00000000. A user reset gives the same values, except a generator feeding a peripheral channel with PCHCTRLm.WRTLOCK=1 keeps its register.

fields.name: DIV
fields.text: Division value for the generator, used as set by DIVSEL. Generators 0 and 2 to 11 use DIV[7:0] (largest factor 512); generator 1 uses DIV[15:0] (largest factor 131072). Bits written outside that range are ignored.

fields.name: RUNSTDBY
fields.text: Keeps the generator running in Standby while it drives its GCLK_IOn pin. With OE at 0 it has no effect, and the generator runs only when a peripheral needs the clock.

values.text: Generator stops in Standby; GCLK_IOn sits at the level set by OOV.
Generator keeps running and driving GCLK_IOn in Standby.

fields.name: DIVSEL
fields.text: Selects how DIV becomes the division factor. To leave the source undivided, DIVSEL must be 0 and DIV must be 0 or 1.

values.text: Source frequency divided by 2^(N+1), N being the generator's number of DIV bits.

fields.name: OE
fields.text: Drives the generator clock out on its GCLK_IOn pin, unless that pin is the generator's SRC.

values.text: Clock on GCLK_IOn, unless GCLK_IOn is the source in SRC.

fields.name: OOV
fields.text: Level on GCLK_IOn while the generator is off or OE is 0, unless that pin is the generator's SRC.

fields.name: IDC
fields.text: Balances the output duty cycle to 50/50 when the division factor is odd.

fields.name: GENEN
fields.text: Turns the generator on or off.

fields.name: SRC
fields.text: Selects the generator's clock source.

registers.name: PCHCTRLm
registers.title: Peripheral Channel Control
notes: Controls peripheral channel m, m = 0 to 47.

Channel map: 0 DFLL48 input; 1 FDPLL0 reference; 2 FDPLL1 reference; 3 FDPLL0 and FDPLL1 32 kHz lock timer clocks, SDHC0 and SDHC1 slow, SERCOM0 to 7 slow; 4 EIC; 5 FREQM measure; 6 FREQM reference; 7 SERCOM0 core; 8 SERCOM1 core; 9 TC0, TC1; 10 USB; 11 to 22 EVSYS0 to 11; 23 SERCOM2 core; 24 SERCOM3 core; 25 TCC0, TCC1; 26 TC2, TC3; 27 CAN0; 28 CAN1; 29 TCC2, TCC3; 30 TC4, TC5; 31 PDEC; 32 AC; 33 CCL; 34 SERCOM4 core; 35 SERCOM5 core; 36 SERCOM6 core; 37 SERCOM7 core; 38 TCC4; 39 TC6, TC7; 40 ADC0; 41 ADC1; 42 DAC; 43 to 44 I2S; 45 SDHC0; 46 SDHC1; 47 CM4 trace.

fields.name: WRTLOCK
fields.text: Once set to 1, later writes to PCHCTRLm are dropped and the GENCTRLn chosen by GEN is locked too; only a power reset unlocks them. Generator 0 cannot be locked.

fields.name: CHEN
fields.text: Turns the peripheral channel on or off.

fields.name: GEN
fields.text: Picks the generator that clocks the peripheral channel. A power reset clears GEN, CHEN and WRTLOCK to 0; a user reset clears them when WRTLOCK is 0 and leaves the register as it is when WRTLOCK is 1.

values.text: No dual bit error since the flag was last cleared.

fields.name: ECCDIS
fields.text: Set from the fuses at startup; with ECC on, each RAM write stores the computed ECC beside the data and reads are checked and corrected.

fields.name: ERRADDR
fields.text: Offset from the RAM start of the address that gave an ECC error; it holds the first error, except that a dual bit error after a single bit error replaces it; reads 0 unless INTFLAG.SINGLEE or INTFLAG.DUALE is 1.

fields.name: ECCELOG

fields.name: ECCDIS

fields.name: BKUP
fields.text: Free for user-defined general purpose data, kept in the Backup domain.

fields.name: CLOCKSYNC
fields.text: Turns on synchronization of CLOCK reads; with it off, CLOCK reads do not return valid values. Not enable-protected.

fields.name: GPTRST
fields.text: When 1, a tamper condition resets the GP registers whose CTRLB.GPnEN bit is set. Writable only while the RTC is disabled; not synchronized.

fields.name: BKTRST
fields.text: When 1, a tamper condition resets every BKUPn register. Writable only while the RTC is disabled; not synchronized.

fields.name: PRESCALER
fields.text: Divides GCLK_RTC down to the counter clock CLK_RTC_CNT. With the prescaler off, periodic events and interrupts are unavailable. Not synchronized.

fields.name: MATCHCLR
fields.text: Clears the counter on a Compare/Alarm 0 match; applies in Mode 0 (COUNT32) and Mode 2 (CLOCK) only. Writable only while the RTC is disabled; not synchronized.

values.text: Counter kept on an Alarm 0 match.
Counter cleared on an Alarm 0 match.

fields.name: CLKREP
fields.text: Picks 24-hour or 12-hour hours in CLOCK; Mode 2 only. Writable only while the RTC is disabled; not synchronized.

fields.name: MODE
fields.text: Selects the RTC operating mode. Not synchronized.

fields.name: ENABLE
fields.text: Turns the RTC on or off. The written value reads back at once and SYNCBUSY.ENABLE sets; the change takes effect after synchronization, and SYNCBUSY.ENABLE clears when it is done.

fields.name: SWRST
fields.text: Writing 1 returns every RTC register except DBGCTRL to its reset value and disables the RTC; other writes in the same access are dropped. Writing 0 does nothing. The bit clears once the synchronized reset finishes.

fields.name: ACTF
fields.text: Divides CLK_RTC to make the OUT clock used for active layer protection.

fields.name: DEBF
fields.text: Divides CLK_RTC to clock the input debouncers.

fields.name: DMAEN
fields.text: Lets the RTC request a DMA transfer when a timestamp is ready in TIMESTAMP.

values.text: No tamper DMA request; reading TIMESTAMP leaves INTFLAG.TAMPER alone.
Tamper DMA request on; reading TIMESTAMP clears INTFLAG.TAMPER.

fields.name: RTCOUT
fields.text: RTC out enable: switches the active layer output.

fields.name: DEBASYNC
fields.text: Debouncer asynchronous enable: runs the tamper input debouncers asynchronously.

fields.name: DEBMAJ
fields.text: Debouncer majority enable: picks how the tamper input debouncers decide.

fields.name: GP2EN
fields.text: General purpose 2 enable: trades the COMP1 compare function for GP2 and GP3.

fields.name: GP0EN
fields.text: General purpose 0 enable: trades the COMP0 compare function for GP0.

fields.name: TAMPEVEI
fields.text: Tamper event input enable.

values.text: Tamper event input off; incoming events ignored.
Tamper event input on; each incoming event captures CLOCK.

fields.name: OVFEO
fields.text: Overflow event output enable.

fields.name: TAMPEREO
fields.text: Tamper event output enable.

values.text: An event on every tamper input.

fields.name: ALARMEOn
fields.text: Alarm n event output enable, one bit per alarm (n = 0..1).

values.text: An alarm n event on every compare match.

fields.name: PEREOn
fields.text: Periodic interval n event output enable, one bit per interval (n = 0..7).

registers.name: INTENCLR
registers.title: Interrupt Enable Clear in Clock/Calendar mode (CTRLA.MODE=2)
notes: Writing 1 to a bit disables that interrupt with no read-modify-write; the change also shows in INTENSET.

fields.name: OVF
fields.text: Writing 1 clears the overflow interrupt enable, turning the overflow interrupt off; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: TAMPER
fields.text: Tamper interrupt enable.

fields.name: ALARMn
fields.text: Writing 1 clears the alarm n interrupt enable, turning the alarm n interrupt off; writing 0 does nothing (n = 0..1).

fields.name: PERn
fields.text: Writing 1 clears the periodic interval n interrupt enable, turning that interrupt off; writing 0 does nothing (n = 0..7).

registers.name: INTENSET
registers.title: Interrupt Enable Set in Clock/Calendar mode (CTRLA.MODE=2)
notes: Writing 1 to a bit enables that interrupt with no read-modify-write; the change also shows in INTENCLR.

fields.name: OVF
fields.text: Writing 1 sets the overflow interrupt enable, turning the overflow interrupt on; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: TAMPER
fields.text: Writing 1 sets the tamper interrupt enable, turning the tamper interrupt on; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: ALARMn
fields.text: Writing 1 sets the alarm n interrupt enable, turning the alarm n interrupt on; writing 0 does nothing (n = 0..1).

fields.name: PERn
fields.text: Writing 1 sets the periodic interval n interrupt enable, turning that interrupt on; writing 0 does nothing (n = 0..7).

registers.name: INTFLAG
registers.title: Interrupt Flag Status and Clear in Clock/Calendar mode (CTRLA.MODE=2)

fields.name: OVF
fields.text: Set one CLK_RTC_CNT cycle after an overflow; raises an interrupt when INTENCLR/SET.OVF is 1. Writing 1 clears it; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: TAMPER
fields.text: Set when a tamper condition occurs; raises an interrupt when INTENCLR/SET.TAMPER is 1. Writing 1 clears it; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: ALARMn
fields.text: Set one CLK_RTC_CNT cycle after alarm n matches; raises an interrupt when INTENCLR/SET.ALARMn is 1. Writing 1 clears it; writing 0 does nothing (n = 0..1).

fields.name: PERn
fields.text: Set when prescaler bit n+2 goes from 0 to 1; raises an interrupt when INTENCLR/SET.PERn is 1. Writing 1 clears it; writing 0 does nothing (n = 0..7).

fields.name: DBGRUN
fields.text: Chooses whether the RTC runs while an external debugger halts the CPU. A software reset leaves it unchanged.

values.text: RTC stops while the CPU is halted.
RTC keeps running while the CPU is halted.

fields.name: GPn
fields.text: Busy while a write to GPn is being synchronized, one bit per register.

fields.name: CLOCKSYNC
fields.text: Busy while a write to CTRLA.CLOCKSYNC is being synchronized.

fields.name: MASKn
fields.text: Busy while a write to MASKn is being synchronized (n = 0..1).

fields.name: ALARMn
fields.text: Busy while a write to ALARMn is being synchronized (n = 0..1).

fields.name: CLOCK
fields.text: Busy while a read or write of CLOCK is being synchronized.

fields.name: FREQCORR
fields.text: Busy while a write to FREQCORR is being synchronized.

fields.name: ENABLE
fields.text: Busy while a write to CTRLA.ENABLE is being synchronized.

fields.name: SWRST
fields.text: Busy while a write to CTRLA.SWRST is being synchronized.

fields.name: SIGN
fields.text: Correction sign.

fields.name: VALUE
fields.text: Size of the correction applied to the RTC prescaler.

values.text: RTC frequency corrected by this amount.

fields.name: YEAR
fields.text: Years past a reference year that software chooses; a year with YEAR[1:0] = 0 counts as a leap year.

fields.name: MONTH
fields.text: Month, 1 for January through 12 for December.

fields.name: DAY
fields.text: Day of the month, from 1 up to 28, 29, 30 or 31 by month and year.

fields.name: HOUR
fields.text: Hour. With CTRLA.CLKREP = 0, 0 to 23; with CTRLA.CLKREP = 1, HOUR[3:0] runs 1 to 12 and HOUR[4] is 0 for AM, 1 for PM.

fields.name: MINUTE
fields.text: Minute, 0 to 59.

fields.name: SECOND
fields.text: Second, 0 to 59.

registers.name: ALARM
registers.title: Alarm n Value in Clock/Calendar mode (CTRLA.MODE=2)
notes: ALARMn is compared all the time with CLOCK, over the fields MASKn.SEL picks. A match sets INTFLAG.ALARMn one counter cycle later, and also clears the counter if CTRLA.MATCHCLR is 1.

fields.name: YEAR
fields.text: Alarm year; compared only when MASKn.SEL is 6.

fields.name: MONTH
fields.text: Alarm month; compared only when MASKn.SEL is above 4.

fields.name: DAY
fields.text: Alarm day; compared only when MASKn.SEL is above 3.

fields.name: HOUR
fields.text: Alarm hour; compared only when MASKn.SEL is above 2.

fields.name: MINUTE
fields.text: Alarm minute; compared only when MASKn.SEL is above 1.

fields.name: SECOND
fields.text: Alarm second; compared only when MASKn.SEL is above 0.

registers.name: MASK
registers.title: Alarm n Mask in Clock/Calendar mode (CTRLA.MODE=2)

fields.name: SEL
fields.text: Chooses which parts of ALARMn take part in the match.

fields.name: GP
fields.text: Free for software use as general purpose storage.

fields.name: DEBNC
fields.text: Turns on debouncing per tamper input INn, one bit per input. Has no effect when TAMPCTRL.INACT is ACTL (active layer protection).

fields.name: TAMLVL
fields.text: Chooses the detected edge per tamper input INn, one bit per input. Has no effect when TAMPCTRL.INACT is ACTL (active layer protection).

fields.name: IN4ACT
fields.text: Action of tamper channel 4. 0x0 OFF: off. 0x1 WAKE: wakes and sets the Tamper flag. 0x2 CAPTURE: captures a timestamp and sets the Tamper flag. 0x3 ACTL: compares the RTC signal routed between IN4 and OUT; on a mismatch, captures a timestamp and sets the Tamper flag.

fields.name: IN3ACT
fields.text: Action of tamper channel 3. 0x0 OFF: off. 0x1 WAKE: wakes and sets the Tamper flag. 0x2 CAPTURE: captures a timestamp and sets the Tamper flag. 0x3 ACTL: compares the RTC signal routed between IN3 and OUT; on a mismatch, captures a timestamp and sets the Tamper flag.

fields.name: IN2ACT
fields.text: Action of tamper channel 2. 0x0 OFF: off. 0x1 WAKE: wakes and sets the Tamper flag. 0x2 CAPTURE: captures a timestamp and sets the Tamper flag. 0x3 ACTL: compares the RTC signal routed between IN2 and OUT; on a mismatch, captures a timestamp and sets the Tamper flag.

fields.name: IN1ACT
fields.text: Action of tamper channel 1. 0x0 OFF: off. 0x1 WAKE: wakes and sets the Tamper flag. 0x2 CAPTURE: captures a timestamp and sets the Tamper flag. 0x3 ACTL: compares the RTC signal routed between IN1 and OUT; on a mismatch, captures a timestamp and sets the Tamper flag.

fields.name: IN0ACT
fields.text: Action of tamper channel 0. 0x0 OFF: off. 0x1 WAKE: wakes and sets the Tamper flag. 0x2 CAPTURE: captures a timestamp and sets the Tamper flag. 0x3 ACTL: compares the RTC signal routed between IN0 and OUT; on a mismatch, captures a timestamp and sets the Tamper flag.

fields.name: YEAR
fields.text: The year captured when a tamper condition occurs.

fields.name: MONTH
fields.text: The month captured when a tamper condition occurs.

fields.name: DAY
fields.text: The day captured when a tamper condition occurs.

fields.name: HOUR
fields.text: The hour captured when a tamper condition occurs.

fields.name: MINUTE
fields.text: The minute captured when a tamper condition occurs.

fields.name: SECOND
fields.text: The second captured when a tamper condition occurs.

fields.name: TAMPEVT
fields.text: Shows that a tamper input event was detected. Writing 1 clears it; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: TAMPID
fields.text: One bit per channel n showing a tamper detected on that channel. Writing 1 clears a bit; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: BKUP
fields.text: Free for software use as general purpose storage in the backup domain.

fields.name: LVLENx
fields.text: One bit per priority level x: when set, requests at that level go to the arbiter; when clear, they are ignored. Not enable-protected.

fields.name: DMAENABLE
fields.text: Writing 1 turns the DMAC on, 0 turns it off. A 0 written during a transfer takes effect only once the internal buffer empties, at the end of the current burst, and the transfer is aborted. Not enable-protected.

fields.name: SWRST
fields.text: Writing 1 while the DMAC is off (DMAENABLE = 0) returns every DMAC register except DBGCTRL to reset; writing 0 does nothing. With the DMAC or CRC module on, the request is ignored and an access error returned.

fields.name: CRCMODE
fields.text: Selects the CRC block transfer mode.

fields.name: CRCSRC
fields.text: Selects the data source the CRC is computed over. It cannot change while a CRC is running: it stays locked, shown by CRCBUSY, until the CRC finishes or the module is disabled. With a DMA channel as source, that channel signals CRC completion.

fields.name: CRCPOLY
fields.text: Selects the CRC polynomial.

fields.name: CRCBEATSIZE
fields.text: Size of each bus access when the CRC is fed from the I/O interface.

fields.name: CRCDATAIN
fields.text: Data to run through the CRC; the new checksum is ready CRCBEAT + 1 clock cycles after a write.

registers.name: CRCCHKSUM
registers.title: CRC Checksum
notes: Resets to 0; writing it directly can set all bits to 1, and it is writable only while the CRC module is off. With CRC-32 and CRCBUSY clear (CRC done or aborted), it reads back bit-reversed (bit 31 with bit 0 and so on) and inverted. With CRC-16, or while CRCBUSY is set, it reads back as is.

fields.name: CRCCHKSUM
fields.text: The CRC result. With CRC-16 the upper 16 bits read as 0.

fields.name: CRCERR
fields.text: Reads 1 when the memory CRC monitor finds corrupted data.

fields.name: CRCZERO
fields.text: Set when a CRC finishes with a zero checksum; cleared when a new CRC source is chosen.

fields.name: CRCBUSY
fields.text: CRC busy. With the I/O interface as source (CRCCTRL.CRCSRC = 0x1): set by a write to CRCDATAIN, cleared by writing 1, writing 0 does nothing. With a DMA channel as source (CRCCTRL.CRCSRC = 0x20 to 0x3F): set when that channel is enabled, cleared when it is disabled, writes do nothing.

fields.name: DBGRUN
fields.text: Chooses whether the DMAC runs while an external debugger halts the CPU. A software reset leaves it unchanged.

values.text: DMAC stops while the CPU is halted.
DMAC keeps running while the CPU is halted.

fields.name: SWTRIG
fields.text: One bit per channel n. Writing 1 starts a software trigger on channel n when its CHSTATUS.PEND is 0; PEND then sets and the bit stays 0. If PEND is already 1, the written 1 stays set. The bit clears when PEND sets or on a write of 0 or 1.

fields.name: RRLVLEN3
fields.text: Round-robin arbitration enable for priority level 3.

fields.name: QOS3
fields.text: Quality of service for priority level 3.

fields.name: LVLPRI3
fields.text: With round-robin on for level 3 (PRICTRL0.RRLVLEN3 = 1), holds the number of the last channel granted access at level 3. With static arbitration (RRLVLEN3 = 0), a nonzero value has no effect on the static order. Turning round-robin off does not reset it.

fields.name: RRLVLEN2
fields.text: Round-robin arbitration enable for priority level 2.

fields.name: QOS2
fields.text: Quality of service for priority level 2.

fields.name: LVLPRI2
fields.text: With round-robin on for level 2 (PRICTRL0.RRLVLEN2 = 1), holds the number of the last channel granted access at level 2. With static arbitration (RRLVLEN2 = 0), a nonzero value has no effect on the static order. Turning round-robin off does not reset it.

fields.name: RRLVLEN1
fields.text: Round-robin arbitration enable for priority level 1.

fields.name: QOS1
fields.text: Quality of service for priority level 1.

fields.name: LVLPRI1
fields.text: With round-robin on for level 1 (PRICTRL0.RRLVLEN1 = 1), holds the number of the last channel granted access at level 1. With static arbitration (RRLVLEN1 = 0), a nonzero value has no effect on the static order. Turning round-robin off does not reset it.

fields.name: RRLVLEN0
fields.text: Round-robin arbitration enable for priority level 0.

fields.name: QOS0
fields.text: Quality of service for priority level 0.

fields.name: LVLPRI0
fields.text: With round-robin on for level 0 (PRICTRL0.RRLVLEN0 = 1), holds the number of the last channel granted access at level 0. With static arbitration (RRLVLEN0 = 0), a nonzero value has no effect on the static order. Turning round-robin off does not reset it.

registers.name: INTPEND
registers.title: Interrupt Pending
notes: Gives the lowest-numbered channel with an interrupt pending. An interrupt handler serving several channels reads it to find which one comes first, skipping channels that have their own interrupt line; a handler for a single channel must not use it.

fields.name: PEND
fields.text: Reads 1 when the channel chosen by ID is pending.

fields.name: BUSY
fields.text: Reads 1 when the channel chosen by ID is busy.

fields.name: FERR
fields.text: Reads 1 when the channel chosen by ID has fetched an invalid descriptor.

fields.name: CRCERR
fields.text: Reads 1 when the channel chosen by ID has its CRC error flag set, which happens when the CRC monitor finds corrupted data. Writing 1 clears it and the matching flag in that channel's CHINTFLAG; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: SUSP
fields.text: Reads 1 when the channel chosen by ID has a suspend interrupt pending. Writing 1 clears it and the matching flag in that channel's CHINTFLAG; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: TCMPL
fields.text: Reads 1 when the channel chosen by ID has a transfer complete interrupt pending. Writing 1 clears it and the matching flag in that channel's CHINTFLAG; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: TERR
fields.text: Reads 1 when the channel chosen by ID has a transfer error interrupt pending. Writing 1 clears it and the matching flag in that channel's CHINTFLAG; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: ID
fields.text: Lowest channel number with an interrupt pending, valid while SUSP, TCMPL or TERR is set; reads 0 when none is pending. Updates when a lower-numbered channel gets a pending interrupt or when the channel's interrupt sources are cleared. Writing it gives indirect access to that channel's interrupt flag register.

fields.name: CHINTn
fields.text: One bit per channel n, set when channel n has an interrupt request pending; cleared when its interrupts are disabled or their sources cleared.

fields.name: BUSYCHn
fields.text: One bit per channel n, set when channel n starts a transfer; cleared when its trigger action completes, on a bus error on that channel, or when it is disabled.

fields.name: PENDCH
fields.text: One bit per channel n, set when a transfer is pending on channel n; cleared when its trigger action starts (per CHCTRLA.TRIGACT), on a bus error on that channel, or when it is disabled.

fields.name: BTCNT
fields.text: Block transfer count of the transfer in progress, held in the active channel and written back to that channel's write-back memory when the arbiter grants another channel. Valid only while ABUSY is set.

fields.name: ABUSY
fields.text: Goes to 1 when the next descriptor's transfer count is read from write-back memory, and to 0 once the active count has been stored back there.

fields.name: ID
fields.text: Number of the channel now held in the active channel registers; updated each time the arbiter grants a channel.

fields.name: LVLEXx
fields.text: One bit per priority level x: 1 while some level-x channel has a trigger request running or waiting, 0 when none does.

fields.name: BASEADDR
fields.text: Base address of the descriptor memory section; must be 64-bit aligned.

fields.name: WRBADDR
fields.text: Base address of the write-back memory section; must be 64-bit aligned.

registers.name: CHCTRLA
registers.title: Channel Control A
notes: The summary places the copies 0x10 apart.

fields.name: THRESHOLD
fields.text: How many beats are read from the source before writing to the destination begins. No effect on single-beat transfers. Not enable-protected.

fields.name: BURSTLEN
fields.text: Number of beats in a burst. Not enable-protected.

fields.name: TRIGACT
fields.text: What one trigger starts. Not enable-protected.

fields.name: TRIGSRC
fields.text: Peripheral trigger that starts this channel. 0x00: none, software or event triggers only. 0x01: RTC timestamp. 0x02, 0x03: DSU DCC0, DCC1. 0x04 to 0x13: SERCOM0 to SERCOM7, RX then TX for each. 0x14, 0x15: CAN0, CAN1 debug. 0x16: TCC0 overflow/underflow/retrigger; 0x17 to 0x1C: TCC0 match/compare. 0x1D: TCC1 overflow; 0x1E to 0x21: TCC1 match/compare. 0x22: TCC2 overflow; 0x23 to 0x25: TCC2 match/compare. 0x26: TCC3 overflow; 0x27, 0x28: TCC3 match/compare. 0x29: TCC4 overflow; 0x2A, 0x2B: TCC4 match/compare. 0x2C: TC0 overflow; 0x2D, 0x2E: TC0 match/compare. 0x2F: TC1 overflow; 0x30, 0x31: TC1 match/compare. 0x32: TC2 overflow; 0x33, 0x34: TC2 match/compare. 0x35: TC3 overflow; 0x36, 0x37: TC3 match/compare. 0x38: TC4 overflow; 0x39, 0x3A: TC4 match/compare. 0x3B: TC5 overflow; 0x3C, 0x3D: TC5 match/compare. 0x3E: TC6 overflow; 0x3F, 0x40: TC6 match/compare. 0x41: TC7 overflow; up to 0x43: TC7 match/compare. 0x44: ADC0 result ready; 0x45: ADC0 sequence. 0x46: ADC1 result ready; 0x47: ADC1 sequence. 0x48, 0x49: DAC empty. 0x4A, 0x4B: DAC result ready. 0x4C, 0x4D: I2S RX. 0x4E, 0x4F: I2S TX. 0x50: PCC RX. 0x51: AES data write. 0x52: AES data read. 0x53: QSPI RX. 0x54: QSPI TX.

fields.name: RUNSTDBY
fields.text: Keeps the channel running in standby. Not enable-protected.

fields.name: ENABLE
fields.text: Writing 1 turns the channel on. A 0 written during a transfer takes effect only once the internal buffer empties, at the end of the current burst, and the transfer is aborted. Not enable-protected.

fields.name: SWRST
fields.text: Writing 1 while the channel is off (ENABLE = 0) returns the channel registers to reset; ignored while ENABLE = 1. Writing 0 does nothing. Clears itself when the reset is done.

fields.name: CMD
fields.text: Software command to the channel: suspend or resume. Not enable-protected.

fields.name: PRILVL
fields.text: Priority level of the channel; a higher level wins over a lower one. Not enable-protected.

fields.name: EVOE
fields.text: Turns on the channel's event output, generated on each condition chosen by CHEVCTRL.EVOMODE.

fields.name: EVIE
fields.text: Channel event input enable.

values.text: Every incoming event starts the event action.

fields.name: EVOMODE
fields.text: Chooses what produces the channel event output.

values.name: DEFAULT
values.text: Block event output, chosen by BTCTRL.EVOSEL.

fields.name: EVACT
fields.text: Action taken on an input event; runs only when CHEVCTRL.EVIE is set, and only on channels that have event input.

values.name: SSKIP
values.text: Skip the next block suspend action.

registers.name: CHINTENCLR
registers.title: Channel Interrupt Enable Clear
notes: Writing 1 to a bit disables that channel interrupt with no read-modify-write; the change also shows in CHINTENSET.

fields.name: SUSP
fields.text: Writing 1 clears the channel suspend interrupt enable, turning that interrupt off; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: TCMPL
fields.text: Writing 1 clears the channel transfer complete interrupt enable, turning that interrupt off; writing 0 does nothing.

values.text: Transfer complete interrupt off; with block action set to none, TCMPL does not set at the end of a block.

fields.name: TERR
fields.text: Writing 1 clears the channel transfer error interrupt enable, turning that interrupt off; writing 0 does nothing.

registers.name: CHINTENSET
registers.title: Channel Interrupt Enable Set
notes: Writing 1 to a bit enables that channel interrupt with no read-modify-write; the change also shows in CHINTENCLR.

fields.name: SUSP
fields.text: Writing 1 sets the channel suspend interrupt enable, turning that interrupt on; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: TCMPL
fields.text: Writing 1 sets the channel transfer complete interrupt enable, turning that interrupt on; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: TERR
fields.text: Writing 1 sets the channel transfer error interrupt enable, turning that interrupt on; writing 0 does nothing.

registers.name: CHINTFLAG
registers.title: Channel Interrupt Flag Status and Clear

fields.name: SUSP
fields.text: Set when a block with the suspend block action (BTCTRL.BLOCKACT) completes, on a software suspend command (CHCTRLB.CMD), on a suspend input event (CHEVCTRL.EVACT), or when an invalid descriptor is fetched. Writing 1 clears it; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: TCMPL
fields.text: Set when a block transfer completes with its interrupt block action enabled. Writing 1 clears it; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: TERR
fields.text: Set on a bus error in a beat transfer, or on an invalid descriptor fetch by the DMAC. Writing 1 clears it; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: CRCERR
fields.text: Set when the CRC monitor finds corrupted data; cleared by writing 1 or by clearing INTPEND.CRCERR.

fields.name: FERR
fields.text: Set when an invalid descriptor is fetched; cleared by a software resume command.

fields.name: BUSY
fields.text: Set when the channel starts a transfer; cleared when its trigger action completes, on a bus error, or when the channel is disabled.

fields.name: PEND
fields.text: Set as soon as a transfer request arrives for the channel; cleared when its trigger action (CHCTRLA.TRIGACT) starts, on a bus error, or when the channel is disabled.

fields.name: STEPSIZE
fields.text: Picks the multiple of the beat size the address moves by after each beat; STEPSEL decides whether it acts on the source or the destination address.

values.name: X1
values.text: Address advances by 1 x beat size in bytes.

values.name: X2
values.text: Address advances by 2 x beat size in bytes.

values.name: X4
values.text: Address advances by 4 x beat size in bytes.

values.name: X8
values.text: Address advances by 8 x beat size in bytes.

values.name: X16
values.text: Address advances by 16 x beat size in bytes.

values.name: X32
values.text: Address advances by 32 x beat size in bytes.

values.name: X64
values.text: Address advances by 64 x beat size in bytes.

values.name: X128
values.text: Address advances by 128 x beat size in bytes.

fields.name: STEPSEL
fields.text: Chooses which address, source or destination, takes the STEPSIZE step.

fields.name: DSTINC
fields.text: 1 makes the destination address advance during the transfer, by 1 by default, or by the STEPSIZE step when STEPSEL = 0; 0 holds it fixed.

fields.name: SRCINC
fields.text: 1 makes the source address advance during the transfer, by 1 by default, or by the STEPSIZE step when STEPSEL = 1; 0 holds it fixed.

fields.name: BEATSIZE
fields.text: Width of one beat, the single bus access the transfer is made of; applies to both reads and writes.

fields.name: BLOCKACT
fields.text: What the DMAC does once a block transfer finishes.

values.name: NOACT
values.text: Channel disabled if this was the transaction's last block.

values.name: INT
values.text: Channel disabled if this was the last block, plus block interrupt.

fields.name: EVOSEL
fields.text: Chooses when the channel puts out an event.

values.name: BLOCK
values.text: Event pulse at the end of each block.

values.name: BEAT
values.text: Event pulse at the end of each beat.

fields.name: VALID
fields.text: Marks the descriptor usable; a 0 in the descriptor or write-back copy suspends the channel when that descriptor is fetched. The write-back copy is cleared by hardware on a channel abort, a block transfer error, or the end of the block.

fields.name: BTCNT
fields.text: 16-bit count of beats in the block; the internal counter drops by one per beat and is saved to the channel's write-back section when the channel loses priority, is suspended or is disabled (by completion, a transfer error or software).

fields.name: SRCADDR
fields.text: Source address of the block. With SRCINC = 0 it is the address of the last beat; with SRCINC = 1 it is the first beat's address plus BTCNT x (BEATSIZE + 1) bytes, further multiplied by 2^STEPSIZE when STEPSEL = 1. BTCNT here is the starting beat count, BEATSIZE the bytes per beat and STEPSIZE the beats per step.

fields.name: DSTADDR
fields.text: Destination address of the block. With DSTINC = 0 it is the address of the last beat; with DSTINC = 1 it is the first beat's address plus BTCNT x (BEATSIZE + 1) bytes, further multiplied by 2^STEPSIZE when STEPSEL = 0. BTCNT here is the starting beat count, BEATSIZE the bytes per beat and STEPSIZE the beats per step.

fields.name: DESCADDR
fields.text: SRAM address of the next descriptor, on a 128-bit boundary; 0x00000000 ends the transaction when the DMAC goes to load the next descriptor.

fields.name: CKSEL
fields.text: Picks the EIC clock: GCLK_EIC where filtering needs more than 32.768 kHz, CLK_ULP32K where low power comes first. Not write-synchronized.

fields.name: ENABLE
fields.text: Turns the EIC on or off. Synchronization delays the change: the written value reads back at once and SYNCBUSY.ENABLE goes to 1, clearing when the EIC is actually on or off. Not enable-protected; write-synchronized.

fields.name: SWRST
fields.text: Writing 1 returns every EIC register to its reset value and disables the EIC, and overrides any other write in the same access; 0 does nothing. CTRLA.SWRST and SYNCBUSY.SWRST both clear once the reset, which is delayed by synchronization, is done. Not enable-protected; write-synchronized.

fields.name: NMIASYNCH
fields.text: Selects whether NMI edge detection runs synchronous or asynchronous to the EIC clock.

fields.name: NMIFILTEN
fields.text: Non-maskable interrupt filter enable.

fields.name: NMISENSE
fields.text: Edge or level that triggers the NMI.

registers.name: NMIFLAG
registers.title: Non-Maskable Interrupt Flag Status and Clear

fields.name: NMI
fields.text: Set when the NMI pin meets the NMISENSE condition, raising an interrupt request; write 1 to clear, 0 has no effect.

fields.name: ENABLE
fields.text: Busy while a write to CTRLA.ENABLE is being synchronized.

fields.name: SWRST
fields.text: Busy while a write to CTRLA.SWRST is being synchronized.

fields.name: EXTINTEO
fields.text: Bit x turns on the event output for pin EXTINTx.

values.text: EXTINTx gives an event when it meets its sense condition.

fields.name: EXTINT
fields.text: Write 1 to bit x to clear the enable of interrupt EXTINTx; 0 has no effect. Reads give the enable state.

fields.name: EXTINT
fields.text: Write 1 to bit x to set the enable of interrupt EXTINTx; 0 has no effect. Reads give the enable state.

fields.name: EXTINT
fields.text: Bit x is set when pin EXTINTx meets its sense condition and requests an interrupt if INTENCLR/SET.EXTINT[x] is 1; write 1 to clear it, 0 has no effect.

fields.name: ASYNCH
fields.text: Bit x selects asynchronous edge detection for EXTINTx.

fields.name: FILTEN7
fields.text: Turns on the input filter for EXTINT[7]; it must be off while asynchronous detection is on.

fields.name: SENSE7
fields.text: Edge or level on EXTINT[7] that produces its interrupt or event.

fields.text: Bit x turns on debouncing for EXTINTx.

fields.name: TICKON
fields.text: Chooses the clock that samples pin bounce while a transition is being detected.

fields.name: STATES1
fields.text: Number of debouncer low-frequency samples a pin must hold to accept a change of state, in synchronous debouncing, for EXTINT[15:8].

fields.name: PRESCALER1
fields.text: Divides the EIC clock to make the debouncer low-frequency clock for EXTINT[15:8].

fields.name: STATES0
fields.text: Number of debouncer low-frequency samples a pin must hold to accept a change of state, in synchronous debouncing, for EXTINT[7:0].

fields.name: PRESCALER0
fields.text: Divides the EIC clock to make the debouncer low-frequency clock for EXTINT[7:0].

fields.name: PINSTATE
fields.text: Bit x reads the debounced, validated state of pin EXTINTx.

fields.name: LPI
fields.text: Set to 1 to turn on low power idle (LPI) transmission, sent at once on txd and tx_er.

fields.name: FNP
fields.text: Set to 1 to drop the next packet held in the external RX DPRAM; it acts only when the DMA is not already copying a stored packet from the DPRAM to memory.

fields.name: TXPBPF
fields.text: Sends a PFC priority-based pause frame built from the values held in TPFCP.

fields.name: ENPBPR
fields.text: Set to 1 to turn on reception of PFC priority-based pause frames: PFC negotiation and recognition of such frames.

values.text: PFC priority-based pause frames are recognised.

fields.name: SRTSM
fields.text: Set to 1 to overwrite the CRC of each received frame with the nanoseconds field of the 1588 timer, as captured when the frame passed the message time stamp point.

values.text: Every received frame's CRC holds a time stamp instead.

fields.name: TXZQPF
fields.text: Write 1 to send a pause frame with a zero quantum; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: TXPF
fields.text: Write 1 to send a pause frame; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: THALT
fields.text: Write 1 to stop transmitting once the frame in progress, if any, has gone out; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: TSTART
fields.text: Write 1 to begin transmitting; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: BP
fields.text: At 1, in 10M or 100M half duplex, a collision is forced on every received frame; gigabit half duplex ignores it.

values.text: Collisions forced in 10M and 100M half duplex.

fields.name: WESTAT
fields.text: Set to 1 so the statistics registers can be written, for functional test.

fields.name: INCSTAT
fields.text: Write 1 to add one to every statistics register, for test; writing 0 does nothing. Always reads 0.

fields.name: CLRSTAT
fields.text: Write 1 to zero the statistics registers; writing 0 does nothing. Always reads 0.

fields.name: MPE
fields.text: 1 turns the management port on. 0 turns it off, puts MDIO in high impedance and drives MDC low impedance.

fields.name: TXEN
fields.text: 1 lets the GMAC transmitter send data. 0 halts transmission at once, clears the transmit pipeline and control registers, and resets the transmit queue pointer to the first transmit descriptor.

fields.name: RXEN
fields.text: 1 lets the GMAC receive data. 0 halts reception at once and clears the receive pipeline; the receive queue pointer is left as it is.

fields.name: LBL
fields.text: 1 ties GTX to GRX and GTXEN to GRXDV and forces full duplex. GRXCK and GTXCK may misbehave while switching into or out of internal loop back; receive and transmit must already be disabled before switching.

fields.name: IRXER
fields.text: At 1, GRXER has no effect on the GMAC while GRXDV is low.

fields.name: RXBP
fields.text: At 1, frames whose preamble is non-standard are kept rather than rejected.

fields.name: IPGSEN
fields.text: At 1, the transmit IPG may grow beyond 96 bit times according to the previous frame's length and IPGS.

fields.name: IRXFCS
fields.text: Keep at 0 for normal operation. At 1, frames with FCS/CRC errors are kept; bad-FCS statistics are still counted and the FCS status still goes into the frame's DMA descriptor.

fields.name: EFRHD
fields.text: At 1, frames can be received in half duplex while transmitting.

fields.name: RXCOEN
fields.text: At 1, the receive checksum engine runs and frames with a bad IP, TCP or UDP checksum are dropped.

fields.name: DCPF
fields.text: At 1, valid pause frames are not copied to memory, whatever CAF, a hash match or a type ID match says; a destination address match still copies one. Valid pause frames still count in the pause statistics and still pause transmission.

fields.name: DBW
fields.text: Width of the data bus; 64 bits by default.

fields.name: CLK
fields.text: Divider from MCK to the management data clock MDC; set it to suit MCK so that MDC stays at or below 2.5 MHz for 802.3 conformance. MDC runs only during MDIO reads and writes.

fields.name: RFCS
fields.text: At 1, received frames go to memory without their 4-byte frame check sequence, and the reported length is 4 bytes shorter.

fields.name: LFERD
fields.text: At 1, a frame is dropped when its measured length is less than its length field (bytes 13 and 14 of an untagged frame); applies only to length fields below 0x0600.

fields.name: RXBUFO
fields.text: How many bytes into the receive buffer the received data starts.

fields.name: PEN
fields.text: At 1, transmission pauses on receipt of a non-zero 802.3 classic pause frame, if PFC has not been negotiated.

fields.name: RTY
fields.text: Keep at 0 for normal operation. At 1, back-off between collisions is always one slot time, for testing the too-many-retries condition; it also shortens the pause counter's decrement from every 512 bit times to every GRXCK cycle, for pause frame tests.

fields.name: MAXFS
fields.text: At 1, frames up to 1536 bytes are accepted; at 0, any frame longer than 1518 bytes is rejected.

fields.name: UNIHEN
fields.text: 1 accepts a unicast frame when the 6-bit hash of its destination address selects a set bit in the hash register; 0 turns unicast hashing off.

fields.name: MTIHEN
fields.text: 1 accepts a multicast frame when the 6-bit hash of its destination address selects a set bit in the hash register; 0 turns multicast hashing off.

fields.name: NBC
fields.text: 1 rejects frames sent to the broadcast address 0xFFFFFFFFFFFF; 0 accepts them.

fields.name: CAF
fields.text: At 1, every valid frame is accepted.

fields.name: JFRAME
fields.text: At 1, jumbo frames up to 10240 bytes are accepted; 10240 bytes is the default length.

fields.name: DNVLAN
fields.text: 1 passes only VLAN-tagged frames on to address matching; 0 passes tagged and untagged frames.

fields.name: FD
fields.text: 1 selects full duplex: the transmitter ignores collision and carrier sense, and reception can run during transmission. 0 turns full duplex off.

fields.name: SPD
fields.text: 1 selects 100 Mbps; 0 selects 10 Mbps.

fields.name: IDLE
fields.text: Reads 1 when the PHY management logic is idle, its operation finished.

fields.name: MDIO
fields.text: Current level of the MDIO pin.

fields.name: MII
fields.text: Picks the MII or RMII interface.

fields.name: DDRP
fields.text: Chooses what happens to received packets when no AHB resource is free; writes are ignored unless the DMA runs full store and forward with the packet buffer.

values.text: Packets wait in the SRAM packet buffer until an AHB buffer is free.
Packets in the receive packet buffer are dropped automatically while no AHB resource is free.

fields.name: DRBS
fields.text: Size of each receive buffer in AHB system memory, in units of 64 bytes: 0x02 is 128 bytes, 0x18 is 1536 bytes (one maximum-length frame), 0xA0 is 10240 bytes (one 10K jumbo frame). Never write 0x00.

fields.name: TXCOEN
fields.text: Turns on IP, TCP and UDP checksum generation in the transmitter.

values.text: The transmitter's checksum engine computes the checksums of transmit frames and puts them in.

fields.name: TXPBMS
fields.text: At 0, the transmit packet buffer uses half the memory, so the GMAC uses less memory; set it to 1 when the whole configured memory is there. Sizes given are for the default 4 KB maximum.

values.text: Top address bits unused; 2 KB used.

fields.name: RXBMS
fields.text: Size of the receive packet buffer: the full 4 KB default, a half, a quarter or an eighth of it.

fields.name: ESPA
fields.text: Byte order of AHB transfers for packet data.

fields.name: ESMA
fields.text: Byte order of AHB transfers for management descriptors.

fields.name: FBLDO
fields.text: AHB burst length the DMA tries for frame data; SINGLE transfers are used where space or data size do not allow it, and management operations never use it. A write is reduced to one-hot form automatically (x is don't care).

values.name: INCR4
values.text: 001xx: try INCR4 AHB bursts; the default.

fields.name: HRESP
fields.text: Set when the DMA receives an HRESP not OK. Write 1 to clear.

fields.name: UND
fields.text: Set when the transmitter had to cut a frame short because no more data came, or when a transmit status write back was attempted before the previous one finished. With the DMA in internal FIFO mode it is also set when, after the SOP data went into the FIFO, the AHB grant came too late, an AHB not OK came back, or a used bit was read. Write 1 to clear.

fields.name: TXCOMP
fields.text: Set when a frame has gone out. Write 1 to clear.

fields.name: TFC
fields.text: Set on an error while reading a transmit frame over the AHB, such as an HRESP error or buffers running out mid-frame (transmission then stops, the FCS is bad and GTXER goes high). With the DMA using its packet buffer, also set when a single frame does not fit the configured packet buffer. Write 1 to clear.

fields.name: TXGO
fields.text: Reads 1 while transmission is active; with the DMA interface it is the TXGO variable of the transmit buffer description.

fields.name: RLE
fields.text: Retry limit exceeded flag. Write 1 to clear.

fields.name: COL
fields.text: In 10/100 Mbps mode, set by a collision or a late collision. Write 1 to clear.

fields.name: UBR
fields.text: Set when the DMA reads a transmit buffer descriptor whose used bit is 1. Write 1 to clear.

registers.name: RBQB
registers.title: GMAC Receive Buffer Queue Base Address Register
notes: Where the list of receive buffer descriptors begins. Write it before NCR.RXEN turns reception on; once reception is on, writes are ignored. A read gives the address of the descriptor now in use, which moves on as buffers fill, so received frames are found by walking the descriptor list and checking each used bit, not by reading this register. Descriptors sit on 32-bit boundaries, are read with one 32-bit AHB access and are written with two separate non-sequential accesses.

fields.name: ADDR
fields.text: Software writes here where the receive queue begins.

registers.name: TBQB
registers.title: GMAC Transmit Buffer Queue Base Address Register
notes: Where the list of transmit buffer descriptors begins. Write it before NCR.TSTART starts transmission; once transmission has started, writes are ignored. The transmitter becomes active up to four MCK cycles after TSTART is written, and a write here within that time gives unpredictable results. A read gives the address of the descriptor now in use, which may not belong to the frame being sent, since the DMA handles two frames at a time. Descriptors sit on 32-bit boundaries, are written with one 32-bit AHB access and are read with two separate non-sequential accesses.

fields.name: ADDR
fields.text: Software writes here where the transmit queue begins.

registers.name: RSR
registers.title: GMAC Receive Status Register
notes: Each bit is cleared by writing 1 to it; no write can set a bit.

fields.name: HNO
fields.text: Set when the DMA receives an HRESP not OK. Write 1 to clear.

fields.name: RXOVR
fields.text: Set when a frame ended before its receive status could be taken; the buffer is recovered after an overrun. Write 1 to clear.

fields.name: REC
fields.text: Set once at least one frame has arrived and been stored in memory. Write 1 to clear.

fields.name: BNA
fields.text: Set when the DMA tried to take a new buffer and the pointer showed it owned by the processor. The DMA reads the pointer again at each end of frame until it finds a valid one; the flag is set after every failed descriptor read, even if software cleared it in between. Write 1 to clear.

registers.name: ISR
registers.title: GMAC Interrupt Status Register
notes: A bit here is set, and the GMAC interrupt raised, only for a source first enabled in the mask.

fields.name: PFNZ

fields.name: HRESP
fields.text: Set when the DMA receives an HRESP not OK. Cleared by reading.

fields.name: ROVR
fields.text: Goes to 1 when RX overrun is flagged in the receive status. Cleared by reading.

fields.name: TCOMP
fields.text: Set when a frame has gone out. Cleared by reading.

fields.name: TFC
fields.text: Set on an error while reading a transmit frame over the AHB, such as an HRESP error or buffers running out mid-frame.

fields.name: RLEX
fields.text: Transmit error: retry limit exceeded. Cleared by reading.

fields.name: TUR
fields.text: Set when the transmitter had to cut a frame short because no more data came, when a transmit status write back was attempted before the previous one finished, or when, after the SOP data went into the FIFO, the AHB grant came too late, an AHB not OK came back, or a used bit was read.

fields.name: TXUBR
fields.text: Set when the DMA reads a transmit buffer descriptor whose used bit is 1. Cleared by reading.

fields.name: RXUBR

fields.name: RCOMP

fields.name: MFS

registers.name: IMR
registers.title: GMAC Interrupt Mask Register
notes: The register's reset value is also given as 0x3FFFFFFF.

Read-only view of the interrupt masks: a bit at 0 means that interrupt is enabled, 1 that it is not. Every bit is 1 after reset; a write of 1 to IER clears a bit and a write of 1 to IDR sets it. For test, a write here sets or clears the matching ISR bits whatever the mask, and writing 1 raises the interrupt.

registers.name: MAN
registers.title: GMAC PHY Maintenance Register
notes: A write starts a shift that sends a PHY management frame on MDIO: each MDC cycle the top bit goes out on MDIO and the bottom bit is taken in from it. NSR.IDLE is set and an interrupt raised when it ends, about 2000 MCK cycles with MDC at MCK/32. A read during the shift returns the shift register as it stands; at the end the bits are back in place, with DATA holding the PHY's data after a read. The values written must form a valid management frame. Clause 22 and clause 45 PHYs are both served; WZO, CLTTO and OP are 0, 1, 10 for a clause 22 read; 0, 1, 01 for a clause 22 write; 0, 0, 11 for a clause 45 read; 0, 0, 01 for a clause 45 write; 0, 0, 10 for a clause 45 read with address.

fields.name: WZO
fields.text: Write 0.

fields.name: CLTTO
fields.text: Selects a clause 22 or clause 45 management frame.

fields.name: OP

fields.name: PHYA

fields.name: REGA

fields.name: WTN

fields.name: DATA

fields.name: SCOL
fields.text: Count of frames that met exactly one collision before going out successfully (no underrun).

fields.name: MCOL

fields.name: LCOL

fields.name: DEFT

fields.name: CSR

fields.name: UFRX
fields.text: Count of received frames shorter than 64 bytes (10/100 mode, full duplex) that have neither a CRC error nor an alignment error.

fields.name: OFRX
fields.text: Count of received frames longer than 1518 bytes (1536 with NCFGR.MAXFS=1) with no CRC error, alignment error or receive symbol error.

fields.name: JRX
fields.text: Count of received frames longer than 1518 bytes (1536 with NCFGR.MAXFS=1) that also have a CRC, alignment or receive symbol error.

registers.name: FCSE
registers.title: GMAC Frame Check Sequence Errors Register

fields.name: FCKR
fields.text: Count of frames of a whole number of bytes, 64 to 1518 bytes long (1536 with NCFGR.MAXFS=1), with a bad CRC; also counts a symbol error in a frame of valid length and a whole number of bytes. Counts a bad-FCS frame whether or not NCFGR.IRXFCS=1 lets it be copied to memory.

registers.name: LFFE
registers.title: GMAC Length Field Frame Errors Register

fields.name: LFER
fields.text: Count of received frames whose measured length is less than their length field (bytes 13 and 14); counted only when the length field is below 0x0600, the frame is not too long, and NCFGR.LFERD is 1.

fields.name: RXSE
fields.text: Count of frames received with GRXER asserted. In 10/100 mode they count whatever the frame length; such a frame of 64 to 1518 bytes (1536 with NCFGR.MAXFS=1) also counts as an FCS or alignment error, and a longer one as a jabber.

fields.name: AER
fields.text: Count of frames that are not a whole number of bytes, have a bad CRC once cut to a whole number of bytes, and are 64 to 1518 bytes long (1536 with NCFGR.MAXFS=1); also counts a symbol error in a frame of valid length that is not a whole number of bytes.

fields.name: RXRER
fields.text: Count of frames that are not a whole number of bytes, have a bad CRC once cut to a whole number of bytes, and are 64 to 1518 bytes long (1536 with NCFGR.MAXFS=1); also counts a symbol error in a frame of valid length that is not a whole number of bytes.

fields.name: RXOVR
fields.text: Count of address-matched frames that a receive overrun kept out of memory.

registers.name: IHCE

fields.name: HCKER
fields.text: Count of frames dropped for a wrong IP header checksum that are 64 to 1518 bytes (1536 with NCFGR.MAXFS=1) and have no CRC, alignment or symbol error.

fields.name: TCKER
fields.text: Count of frames dropped for a wrong TCP checksum that are 64 to 1518 bytes (1536 with NCFGR.MAXFS=1) and have no CRC, alignment or symbol error.

fields.name: UCKER
fields.text: Count of frames dropped for a wrong UDP checksum that are 64 to 1518 bytes (1536 with NCFGR.MAXFS=1) and have no CRC, alignment or symbol error.

fields.name: TCS
fields.text: Seconds count, writable; goes up by 1 each time the IEEE 1588 nanoseconds counter reaches one second, and may also go up on a write to TA.

fields.name: TCS
fields.text: Seconds count, writable; goes up by 1 each time the IEEE 1588 nanoseconds counter reaches one second, and may also go up on a write to TA.

fields.name: VTS
fields.text: Captured timer seconds value, writable; goes up by 1 each time the IEEE 1588 nanoseconds counter reaches one second, and may also go up on a write to TA.

registers.name: TSSN

fields.name: VTN
fields.text: Captured timer nanoseconds value, writable; goes up by 1 each time the IEEE 1588 nanoseconds counter reaches one second, and may also go up on a write to TA.

fields.name: TNS
fields.text: Nanoseconds count, writable and also changed by writes to TA; each clock cycle it goes up by the value in TI.

fields.name: ADJ
fields.text: 1 subtracts from the 1588 timer; 0 adds to it.

fields.name: ITDT
fields.text: Nanoseconds to add to or take from TN; the seconds register is carried or borrowed as needed.

fields.name: NIT
fields.text: How many increments pass before ACNS is used in place of CNS.

fields.name: ACNS
fields.text: Alternative nanoseconds added to TN each clock cycle.

fields.name: CNS
fields.text: Nanoseconds added to TN each clock cycle.

fields.name: RLPITR
fields.text: Counts changes from normal idle to low power idle on the receive side. Cleared by reading.

fields.name: RLPITI
fields.text: Goes up once per 16 AHB clock cycles while NCR.LPI is 1. Cleared by reading.

fields.name: TLPITR
fields.text: Counts the times NCR.LPI changes from 0 to 1.

fields.name: TLPITI
fields.text: Goes up once per 16 AHB clock cycles while NCR.LPI is 1. Cleared by reading.

fields.name: CACHEDIS1
fields.text: Turns off the cache on the AHB1 interface. Starting an NVM write or erase invalidates the cache lines on its own.

fields.name: CACHEDIS0
fields.text: Turns off the cache on the AHB0 interface. Starting an NVM write or erase invalidates the cache lines on its own.

fields.name: AHBNS1
fields.text: Makes every AHB1 access non-sequential.

values.text: Sequential accesses become non-sequential, so the bus is rearbitrated on every access.

fields.name: AHBNS0
fields.text: Makes every AHB0 access non-sequential.

values.text: Sequential accesses become non-sequential, so the bus is rearbitrated on every access.

fields.name: RWS
fields.text: Number of wait states on an NVM read while AUTOWS is 0, from 0 to 15 (the value is the count). Resets to 0; software may set it to suit the NVM access time and the system clock.

fields.name: PRM
fields.text: Chooses how the NVM block goes into and out of low-power mode around sleep.

values.name: SEMIAUTO
values.text: Low power on entering standby or on an SPRM command; leaves it at the first access.

values.name: FULLAUTO
values.text: Low power on entering standby or on an SPRM command; leaves it once the system is out of standby.

values.name: MANUAL
values.text: No low power on entering standby; low power on an SPRM command; leaves it at the first access.

fields.name: WMODE
fields.text: Chooses whether writing across an address boundary issues a write command by itself, and which boundary.

values.name: ADW
values.text: Automatic write at each double word.

values.name: AQW
values.text: Automatic write at each quad word.

fields.name: SUSPEN
fields.text: Allows a write or erase to be suspended.

values.text: Write and erase suspend/resume is off.
A read in the same bank can suspend a write or erase.

fields.name: AUTOWS
fields.text: Lets the controller set the read wait states itself, so it runs at any clock up to the device maximum; this adds at least one cycle of latency.

values.text: Off; CTRLA.RWS sets the wait states.
On; the wait states are set automatically.

fields.name: CMDEX
fields.text: Key that runs the command in CMD; write 0xA5 together with CMD. Any other key, or a command issued while the previous one is unfinished, is not carried out and sets INTFLAG.PROGE. STATUS.READY must be 1 when the command is issued. When a command arrives on APB in the same cycle as an AHB access, the AHB access goes first and the command runs once the AHB bus and the NVM block are both idle. INTFLAG.DONE is set when it finishes.

fields.name: CMD
fields.text: The command to run when the CMDEX key is written.

values.name: EP
values.text: Erase page (EP); only in the user page of the auxiliary space.

values.name: EB
values.text: Erase block (EB): erases the block at ADDR; not in the user page.

values.name: WP
values.text: Write page (WP): writes the page buffer to the page at ADDR; not in the user page.

values.name: WQW
values.text: Write quad word (WQW): writes 128 bits at ADDR.

values.name: SWRST
values.text: Software reset (SWRST): power-cycles the NVM, reruns the automatic calibration and resets the module's configuration registers.

values.name: LR
values.text: Lock region (LR): locks the region holding ADDR until the next reset.

values.name: UR
values.text: Unlock region (UR): unlocks the region holding ADDR until the next reset.

values.name: PBC
values.text: Page buffer clear (PBC): empties the page buffer.

values.name: BKSWRST
values.text: Bank swap and system reset (BKSWRST); with SmartEEPROM in use, its data is also moved to the other bank.

values.name: CELCK
values.text: Chip erase lock (CELCK): DSU CTRL.CE becomes unavailable, chip erase is disabled and Microchip failure analysis is limited; software must keep a way to run CEULCK.

values.name: CEULCK
values.text: Chip erase unlock (CEULCK): DSU CTRL.CE becomes available.

values.name: SBPDIS
values.text: Set STATUS.BPDIS (SBPDIS): boot loader protection is dropped until CBPDIS or the next start-up.

values.name: CBPDIS
values.text: Clear STATUS.BPDIS (CBPDIS): boot loader protection applies.

values.name: SEEFLUSH
values.text: Flush SmartEEPROM data in buffered mode.

values.name: LSEE
values.text: Lock all access to SmartEEPROM data.

fields.name: SEE
fields.text: Whether the part has SmartEEPROM.

fields.name: PSZ
fields.text: Size of an NVM page; a device family need not offer every size.

fields.name: NVMP
fields.text: How many pages the NVM main address space holds.

fields.name: SEEWRC
fields.text: Write 1 to turn off the SEEWRC interrupt; writing 0 does nothing. Reads back whether the SEEWRC interrupt is enabled.

fields.name: SEESOVF
fields.text: Write 1 to turn off the SEESOVF interrupt; writing 0 does nothing. Reads back whether the SEESOVF interrupt is enabled.

fields.name: SEESFULL
fields.text: Write 1 to turn off the SEESFULL interrupt; writing 0 does nothing. Reads back whether the SEESFULL interrupt is enabled.

fields.name: SUSP

fields.text: Whether the NVM is in power reduction mode. It enters by command or on sleep when CTRLA.PRM allows; it leaves on an AHB access to the NVM, on an SPRM or CPRM command, or on wake when CTRLA.PRM allows.

registers.name: ECCERR
registers.title: ECC Error Status
notes: Logs errors on the NVM read path. Tracking holds after the first error, except that after a single error it stays live and a dual error may overwrite it. Reading the register restarts tracking.

fields.name: TYPEH
fields.text: Kind of ECC error seen on the upper 64-bit read word. Reading the register returns it to none, unless an error lands in that same cycle.

values.name: None
values.text: No error since the last read.

values.name: Single
values.text: At least one single error since the last read.

values.name: Dual

REC stays clear even when its condition occurs.

RWC stays clear even when its condition occurs.

values.text: On; faster, but needs more system bus bandwidth.

values.text: On; CDWBN and WBDIS are ignored, and writing 1 to RCFG.EOM ends monitoring.

fields.name: CFDPRESC
fields.text: Prescaler of the clock failure detector, which is clocked by DFLL48: the CFD safe clock runs at the DFLL48 frequency divided by 2^CFDPRESC.

fields.name: STARTUP
fields.text: Start-up time of XOSCn, counted by OSCULP32K: code n waits 2^n OSCULP32K cycles plus 3 XOSC cycles. Approximate times in µs for 0x0 to 0xF: 31, 61, 122, 244, 488, 977, 1953, 3906, 7813, 15625, 31250, 62500, 125000, 250000, 500000, 1000000.

fields.name: SWBEN
fields.text: When the failed clock recovers, lets the XOSCn output return from the safe clock to its external source (clock input or crystal).

values.text: Switch back on; the bit clears itself once the XOSCn output is back on its external clock or crystal.

fields.name: CFDEN
fields.text: Turns the XOSCn clock failure detector on or off.

fields.name: ENALC
fields.text: Turns automatic loop control of XOSCn on or off.

values.text: Loop control on: the amplitude is tuned automatically while the crystal runs.

fields.name: IMULT
fields.text: Current multiplier of XOSCn: 6 for >24 to 48 MHz, 5 for >16 to 24 MHz, 4 for >8 to 16 MHz, 3 for 8 MHz.

fields.name: IPTAT
fields.text: Current reference of XOSCn: 3 for >8 to 48 MHz, 2 for 8 MHz. With a small CLOAD, the setting of the next lower frequency range may be used, drawing less current.

fields.name: LOWBUFGAIN
fields.text: Only acts when XOSCCTRLn.ENALC=1, adjusting the amplitude in automatic loop control: 0 (the default) allows a low-amplitude oscillator; 1 roughly doubles the amplitude, for stability problems.

values.text: Low buffer gain of XOSCn off.
Low buffer gain of XOSCn on.

fields.name: ONDEMAND
fields.text: With 1, XOSCn runs only while enabled (XOSCCTRLn.ENABLE=1) and a peripheral asks for its clock, and is off otherwise; with 0 it runs whenever enabled. On-demand still applies in standby sleep mode.

values.text: Running only while a peripheral asks for it as a clock source.

fields.name: RUNSTDBY
fields.text: Sets whether XOSCn runs in standby sleep mode. With ONDEMAND=0 the clock source always runs in standby.

values.text: Stopped in standby unless a peripheral asks for the clock.
Runs in standby: with ONDEMAND=1 only while a peripheral asks for the clock, with ONDEMAND=0 all the time.

fields.name: XTALEN
fields.text: Picks how the XOSCn pads are used: external clock input or crystal.

values.text: External clock into XIN; XOUT is free for general-purpose I/O.

fields.name: ENABLE
fields.text: Turns oscillator XOSCn on or off.

fields.name: ONDEMAND
fields.text: With 1, the DFLL runs only while enabled (DFLLCTRLA.ENABLE=1) and a peripheral asks for its clock, and is off otherwise; with 0 it runs whenever enabled. On-demand still applies in standby sleep mode.

values.text: Running only while a peripheral asks for it as a clock source.

fields.name: RUNSTDBY
fields.text: Sets whether the DFLL runs in standby sleep mode. With ONDEMAND=0 the clock source always runs in standby.

values.text: Stopped in standby unless a peripheral asks for the clock.
Runs in standby: with ONDEMAND=1 only while a peripheral asks for the clock, with ONDEMAND=0 all the time.

fields.name: ENABLE
fields.text: Turns the DFLL on or off. Write-synchronized: the DFLL changes state some time after the write, though the written value reads back at once.

fields.name: WAITLOCK
fields.text: Sets whether the DFLL output clock waits for lock.

values.text: Clock goes out only once fine lock is reached.

fields.name: BPLCKC
fields.text: Skips the coarse lock step.

fields.name: QLDIS
fields.text: Quick lock disable.

fields.name: CCDIS
fields.text: Chill cycle disable.

fields.name: USBCRM
fields.text: USB clock recovery mode.

fields.name: LLAW
fields.text: Lose lock after wake: whether locks are dropped on waking from sleep when the DFLL clock was stopped.

fields.name: STABLE
fields.text: Stable DFLL frequency: whether FINE keeps tracking after fine lock.

values.text: FINE follows changes in output frequency.
FINE is frozen after fine lock.

fields.name: MODE
fields.text: Selects open-loop or closed-loop operation of the DFLL.

registers.name: DFLLVAL
registers.title: DFLL48M Value
notes: The register's reset value is also given as 0x0000XXXX.

fields.name: DIFF
fields.text: In closed-loop mode (DFLLCTRLB.MODE=1), the ideal DFLL cycle count minus the counted cycles. Not updated in open-loop mode, where it is not valid.

fields.name: COARSE
fields.text: Coarse calibration value; read-only in closed-loop mode. Holds the factory coarse calibration for 48 MHz after reset.

fields.name: FINE
fields.text: Fine calibration value; read-only in closed-loop mode. Loaded with the factory calibration for 48 MHz after reset.

fields.name: CSTEP
fields.text: Largest step allowed in coarse adjustment in closed-loop mode; the frequency overshoot on retuning depends on it.

fields.name: FSTEP
fields.text: Largest step allowed in fine adjustment in closed-loop mode; the frequency overshoot on retuning depends on it.

fields.name: MUL
fields.text: Multiply factor: CLK_DFLL frequency over CLK_DFLL_REF frequency. A write drops the locks and returns the fine calibration to mid-range.

fields.name: DFLLMUL
fields.text: 1 while a write to DFLLMUL is crossing clock domains; 0 once it is done. Writes only.

fields.name: DFLLVAL
fields.text: 1 while a read or write of DFLLVAL is crossing clock domains; 0 once it is done.

fields.name: DFLLCTRLB
fields.text: 1 while a write to DFLLCTRLB is crossing clock domains; 0 once it is done. Writes only.

fields.name: ENABLE
fields.text: 1 while a change of the ENABLE bit is crossing clock domains; 0 once it is done.

fields.name: ONDEMAND
fields.text: With 1, DPLLn runs only while enabled (DPLLnCTRLA.ENABLE=1) and a peripheral asks for its clock, and is off otherwise; with 0 it runs whenever enabled. On-demand still applies in standby sleep mode.

values.text: Running only while a peripheral asks for it as a clock source.

fields.name: RUNSTDBY
fields.text: Sets whether DPLLn runs in standby sleep mode. With ONDEMAND=0 the clock source always runs in standby.

values.text: Stopped in standby unless a peripheral asks for the clock.
Runs in standby: with ONDEMAND=1 only while a peripheral asks for the clock, with ONDEMAND=0 all the time.

fields.name: ENABLE
fields.text: Turns DPLLn on or off. This takes a few clock cycles; DPLLnSYNCBUSY.ENABLE shows when it has finished.

fields.name: LDRFRAC
fields.text: Fractional part of the DPLLn frequency multiplier. The new value reads back at once and sets DPLLnSYNCBUSY.DPLLRATIO, which clears when the output has taken it.

fields.name: LDR
fields.text: Integer part of the DPLLn frequency multiplier. The new value reads back at once and sets DPLLnSYNCBUSY.DPLLRATIO, which clears when the change is done.

fields.name: DIV
fields.text: Divider for the XOSC reference: fDIV = fXOSC / (2 × (DIV + 1)).

fields.name: DCOEN
fields.text: Turns on the DCO filter controller.

values.text: Controller off; the PLL sets the sigma-delta DAC itself.
Controller on; DCOFILTER sets the sigma-delta DAC filter bandwidth.

fields.name: DCOFILTER
fields.text: Selects the sigma-delta DCO filter of DPLLn, as capacitor and bandwidth Fn: 0x0 0.5 pF, 3.21 MHz; 0x1 1 pF, 1.6 MHz; 0x2 1.5 pF, 1.1 MHz; 0x3 2 pF, 0.8 MHz; 0x4 2.5 pF, 0.64 MHz; 0x5 3 pF, 0.55 MHz; 0x6 3.5 pF, 0.45 MHz; 0x7 4 pF, 0.4 MHz.

fields.name: LBYPASS
fields.text: Lock bypass.

fields.name: LTIME
fields.text: Lock time-out of DPLLn.

fields.name: REFCLK
fields.text: Selects the reference clock of DPLLn.

fields.name: WUF
fields.text: Wake up fast: whether the output waits for lock after start-up.

values.text: Clock output after start-up and lock time.
Clock output after start-up time only.

fields.name: DPLLRATIO
fields.text: Synchronization state of DPLLnRATIO.

values.text: DPLLnRATIO changed and is being synchronized.

fields.name: ENABLE
fields.text: Synchronization state of DPLLnCTRLA.ENABLE.

values.text: DPLLnCTRLA.ENABLE changed and is being synchronized.

fields.name: CLKRDY
fields.text: Whether the DPLLn output clock is running.

fields.name: LOCK
fields.text: Whether DPLLn has reached the target frequency.

values.text: Not locked: DPLLn is off or still settling on the target frequency.

registers.name: INTENCLR
registers.title: Interrupt Enable Clear
notes: Turns interrupts off without a read-modify-write; the change also shows in INTENSET.

fields.name: XOSC32KFAIL
fields.text: Writing 1 clears the XOSC32K clock failure interrupt enable, turning that interrupt off; writing 0 has no effect.

values.text: XOSC32K clock failure interrupt on; a request is made when its flag is set.

fields.name: XOSC32KRDY
fields.text: Writing 1 clears the XOSC32K ready interrupt enable, turning that interrupt off; writing 0 has no effect.

registers.name: INTENSET
registers.title: Interrupt Enable Set
notes: Turns interrupts on without a read-modify-write; the change also shows in INTENCLR.

fields.name: XOSC32KFAIL
fields.text: Writing 1 sets the XOSC32K clock failure interrupt enable, turning that interrupt on; writing 0 has no effect.

values.text: XOSC32K clock failure interrupt on; a request is made when its flag is set.

fields.name: XOSC32KRDY
fields.text: Writing 1 sets the XOSC32K ready interrupt enable, turning that interrupt on; writing 0 has no effect.

fields.name: XOSC32KFAIL
fields.text: XOSC32K clock failure flag: goes to 1 when STATUS.XOSC32KFAIL rises from 0 to 1, and requests an interrupt if INTENSET.XOSC32KFAIL is 1. Writing 1 clears it; writing 0 has no effect.

fields.name: XOSC32KRDY
fields.text: XOSC32K ready flag: goes to 1 when STATUS.XOSC32KRDY rises from 0 to 1, and requests an interrupt if INTENSET.XOSC32KRDY is 1. Writing 1 clears it; writing 0 has no effect.

fields.name: XOSC32KSW
fields.text: XOSC32K clock switch: whether the XOSC32K output now comes from the safe clock.

values.text: Not switched; the crystal oscillator drives XOSC32K.
Switched; the safe clock drives XOSC32K.

fields.name: XOSC32KFAIL
fields.text: XOSC32K clock failure detector result.

fields.name: XOSC32KRDY
fields.text: XOSC32K ready.

values.text: XOSC32K is stable and can serve as a clock source.

fields.name: RTCSEL
fields.text: Clock source of the RTC. Besides 0x0 and 0x1: 0x4 is XOSC1K, 1.024 kHz from the 32 kHz external oscillator; 0x5 is XOSC32K, 32.768 kHz from the 32 kHz external crystal oscillator; 0x2, 0x3, 0x6 and 0x7 are reserved.

values.name: ULP1K
values.text: 1.024 kHz from the internal 32 kHz ULP oscillator.

values.name: ULP32K
values.text: 32.768 kHz from the internal 32 kHz ULP oscillator.

fields.name: CGM
fields.text: Gain of the external crystal oscillator.

fields.name: WRTLOCK
fields.text: Blocks further writes to XOSC32K, freezing its configuration.

fields.name: STARTUP
fields.text: Start-up time of the oscillator, counted by OSCULP32K. Per code: OSCULP32K cycles (plus 3 XOSC32K cycles in each case) and the approximate time for a 32.768 kHz crystal: 0x0 2048, 62.592 ms; 0x1 4096, 125.092 ms; 0x2 16384, 500.092 ms; 0x3 32768, 1000.0092 ms; 0x4 65536, 2000.0092 ms; 0x5 131072, 4000.0092 ms; 0x6 262144, 8000.0092 ms; 0x7 reserved. The actual start-up time is 1 OSCULP32K cycle plus 3 XOSC32K cycles.

fields.name: ONDEMAND
fields.text: Sets how XOSC32K and its clock failure detector answer peripheral clock requests: with 0 they always run in active or idle mode, and in standby when RUNSTDBY=1; with 1 they run only while a peripheral requests the clock.

fields.name: RUNSTDBY
fields.text: Sets how XOSC32K and its clock failure detector behave in standby sleep mode: with 1 they always run if ONDEMAND=0 and run only on a peripheral request if ONDEMAND=1; with 0 they run only while a peripheral requests the clock.

fields.name: EN1K
fields.text: Turns the 1.024 kHz output on or off.

fields.name: EN32K
fields.text: Turns the 32.768 kHz output on or off.

fields.name: XTALEN
fields.text: Picks how the XIN32 and XOUT32 pads are used: external clock input or crystal.

values.text: External clock on XIN32; XOUT32 free for general-purpose I/O.

fields.name: ENABLE
fields.text: Turns the oscillator on or off.

fields.name: CFDPRESC
fields.text: Prescaler of the clock failure detector.

values.text: CFD safe clock at the OSCULP32K frequency.
CFD safe clock at half the OSCULP32K frequency.

fields.name: SWBACK
fields.text: When the failed clock recovers, lets the XOSC32K output return from the safe clock to its external source (clock input or crystal).

values.text: Switch back on; the bit clears itself when the XOSC32K output has switched back.

fields.name: CFDEN
fields.text: Turns the clock failure detector on or off.

fields.name: CFDEO
fields.text: Lets the clock failure detector put out an event when it finds a clock failure.

values.text: An event is put out on a clock failure.

registers.name: OSCULP32K
registers.title: 32KHz Ultra Low Power Internal Oscillator (OSCULP32K) Control
notes: The register's reset value is also given as 0x00000000.

fields.name: WRTLOCK
fields.text: Blocks further writes to OSCULP32K, freezing its configuration.

fields.name: EN1K
fields.text: Turns the 1 kHz output on or off.

fields.name: EN32K
fields.text: 32 kHz output enable.

fields.name: ENABLE
fields.text: Turns the FREQM on or off. The change takes effect after synchronization: the written value reads back at once, SYNCBUSY.ENABLE is set and clears when done. Not enable-protected.

fields.name: SWRST
