fields.text: Writing 1 returns every FREQM register to its reset value and disables the FREQM; writing 0 does nothing. It overrides any other write in the same access. CTRLA.SWRST and SYNCBUSY.SWRST both clear when the reset, delayed by synchronization, is over. Not enable-protected.

fields.name: START
fields.text: Starts a measurement.

fields.name: REFNUM
fields.text: Length of a measurement in CLK_FREQM_REF cycles; must not be zero: 0x01 (1 cycle) to 0xFF (255 cycles).

fields.name: DONE
fields.text: Writing 1 clears the measurement done interrupt enable, turning that interrupt off; writing 0 has no effect.

fields.name: DONE
fields.text: Writing 1 sets the measurement done interrupt enable, turning that interrupt on; writing 0 has no effect.

fields.name: DONE
fields.text: Goes to 1 when STATUS.BUSY falls from 1 to 0. Writing 1 clears it; writing 0 has no effect.

fields.name: OVF
fields.text: Sticky: goes to 1 when the value counter overflows. Writing 1 clears it; writing 0 has no effect.

fields.name: BUSY
fields.text: Whether a measurement is running.

fields.name: ENABLE
fields.text: 1 while CTRLA.ENABLE is being synchronized; 0 once it is done.

fields.name: SWRST
fields.text: 1 while CTRLA.SWRST is being synchronized; 0 once it is done.

fields.name: VALUE
fields.text: Result of the measurement.

fields.name: SWRST
fields.text: Write 1 to return every EVSYS register to its reset state; this write wins over any other write in the same access, which is dropped. Writing 0 does nothing. Disabling the event generators first is recommended.

fields.name: CHANNELx
fields.text: Write 1 to bit x to fire a software event on channel x; writing 0 does nothing. Reads always give 0.

fields.name: RREN
fields.text: Picks the arbitration scheme used among channels at level priority.

fields.name: PRI
fields.text: With round-robin on (PRICTRL.RREN=1), holds the number of the last channel granted as the active level-priority channel; it updates whenever INTPEND or any CHINTFLAG register is written. With static arbitration (RREN=0) a nonzero value has no effect on the static order. Clearing RREN does not reset it.

fields.name: BUSY
fields.text: Reads 1 while the event on the channel named by ID has not yet been handled by every user on that channel.

fields.name: READY
fields.text: Reads 1 when every user on the channel named by ID can accept a new event on that channel.

fields.name: EVD
fields.text: One CLK_EVSYS_APB cycle after an event passes through the channel this flag goes to 1; requests an interrupt when CHINTENCLR/SET.EVD is 1. Never set on an asynchronous path. Write 1 to clear it, which also clears the matching flag in CHINTFLAGn for the channel n given by ID; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: OVR
fields.text: One CLK_EVSYS cycle after a channel overrun this flag goes to 1, requesting an interrupt when CHINTENCLR/SET.OVR is 1. An overrun is either a user on the channel named by ID not being ready when a new event arrives, or a new event arriving before every user has handled the previous one. Never set on an asynchronous path. Write 1 to clear it, which also clears the matching flag in CHINTFLAGn for the channel n given by ID; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: ID
fields.text: Holds the number of the highest-priority channel; writing it opens indirect access to that channel's interrupt flag register.

fields.name: CHINT
fields.text: Bit x is 1 while channel x has an interrupt pending; it clears when that channel's interrupts are disabled or their sources are cleared.

fields.name: BUSYCHx
fields.text: Bit x is 1 while an event on channel x is still waiting on at least one of its users, and 0 when channel x is idle. Always 0 for a channel on an asynchronous path.

fields.name: READYUSR
fields.text: Bit n is 1 when every user on channel n can accept a new event, and 0 when at least one cannot. Always 0 for a channel on an asynchronous path.

fields.name: ONDEMAND
fields.text: Sets whether the channel's generic clock is requested only when needed. No effect on an asynchronous path or on channels that support only asynchronous operation, where it reads 0.

values.text: The channel's generic clock runs continuously while the channel is configured and its clock source is enabled.
The generic clock is requested only while an event is being handled.

fields.name: RUNSTDBY
fields.text: Sets how a resynchronized channel behaves in standby sleep. No effect on an asynchronous path or on channels that support only asynchronous operation, where it reads 0.

values.text: Channel keeps running in standby, subject to CHANNEL.ONDEMAND.

fields.name: EDGSEL
fields.text: Chooses which edges of the generator signal make an event on the channel. Must be 0 on an asynchronous path.

values.name: NO_EVT_OUTPUT
values.text: No event output on a synchronous or resynchronized path.

fields.name: PATH
fields.text: Chooses the path the channel uses. The generator may restrict which paths are allowed; only channels 0 to 11 can be synchronous or resynchronized.

fields.name: EVGEN
fields.text: Chooses which event generator drives the channel.

fields.name: EVD
fields.text: Write 1 to clear the channel's event-detected interrupt enable, turning that interrupt off; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: OVR
fields.text: Write 1 to clear the channel's overrun interrupt enable, turning that interrupt off; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: EVD
fields.text: Write 1 to set the channel's event-detected interrupt enable, turning that interrupt on; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: OVR
fields.text: Write 1 to set the channel's overrun interrupt enable, turning that interrupt on; writing 0 does nothing.

registers.name: CHINTFLAG
registers.title: Channel n Interrupt Flag Status and Clear

fields.name: EVD
fields.text: One CLK_EVSYS_APB cycle after an event passes through the channel this flag goes to 1; requests an interrupt when CHINTENCLR/SET.EVD is 1. Never set on an asynchronous path. Write 1 to clear it; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: OVR
fields.text: One CLK_EVSYS cycle after a channel overrun this flag goes to 1, requesting an interrupt when CHINTENCLR/SET.OVR is 1. An overrun is either a user on the channel not being ready when a new event arrives, or a new event arriving before every user has handled the previous one. Never set on an asynchronous path. Write 1 to clear it; writing 0 does nothing.

registers.name: CHSTATUSn
registers.title: Channel n Status
notes: The register's reset value is also given as 0x01.

fields.name: BUSYCH
fields.text: 1 while an event on the channel is still waiting on at least one of its users; 0 when the channel is idle. Always 0 on an asynchronous path.

fields.name: RDYUSR
fields.text: 1 when every user on the channel can accept a new event; 0 when at least one cannot. Always 0 on an asynchronous path.

fields.name: CHANNEL
fields.text: Chooses the channel that feeds event user m: a value x selects channel x-1.

fields.name: DIR
fields.text: Bit y sets the direction of pin y in the group.

fields.name: DIRCLR
fields.text: Write 1 to a bit to clear that pin's DIR bit, making it an input; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: DIRSET
fields.text: Write 1 to a bit to set that pin's DIR bit, making it an output; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: DIRTGL
fields.text: Write 1 to a bit to invert that pin's DIR bit, reversing its direction; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: OUT
fields.text: For a pin set as output in DIR, the level it drives. For a pin set as input in DIR with PINCFG.PULLEN on, the direction of its pull.

values.text: Drives low, or pulls down when an input.
Drives high, or pulls up when an input.

fields.name: OUTCLR
fields.text: Write 1 to a bit to clear that pin's OUT bit: an output then drives low, and an input with PINCFG.PULLEN on is pulled down. Writing 0 does nothing.

values.text: Drives low, or pulls down when an input.

fields.name: OUTSET
fields.text: Write 1 to a bit to set that pin's OUT bit: an output then drives high, and an input with PULLEN on is pulled up. Writing 0 does nothing.

values.text: Drives high, or pulls up when an input.

fields.name: OUTTGL
fields.text: Write 1 to a bit to invert that pin's OUT bit: an output's drive level flips, and an input with PULLEN on has its pull direction flipped. Writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: IN
fields.text: Bit y gives the level the input sampler of pin y sees: 0 for low, 1 for high.

fields.name: SAMPLING
fields.text: Sets how the input samplers of pins configured as inputs in DIR take samples. Samplers switch on and off in groups of eight pins, so one pin of a byte asking for continuous sampling makes all eight sample continuously.

fields.name: HWSEL
fields.text: Picks which 16-pin half of the group the atomic write reconfigures. Reads 0.

fields.name: WRPINCFG
fields.text: Write 1 to have the atomic write load the written WRCONFIG.DRVSTR, PULLEN, INEN, PMUXEN and PINMASK values into PINCFGy of every pin chosen by WRCONFIG.PINMASK and WRCONFIG.HWSEL; writing 0 does nothing. Reads 0.

fields.name: WRPMUX
fields.text: Write 1 to have the atomic write load the written WRCONFIG.PMUX value into PMUXn of every pin chosen by WRCONFIG.PINMASK and WRCONFIG.HWSEL; writing 0 does nothing. Reads 0.

fields.name: PMUX
fields.text: Value loaded into PMUXn of the pins chosen by WRCONFIG.PINMASK and WRCONFIG.HWSEL when WRCONFIG.WRPMUX is set. Reads 0.

fields.name: DRVSTR
fields.text: Value loaded into PINCFGy.DRVSTR of the pins chosen by WRCONFIG.PINMASK and WRCONFIG.HWSEL when WRCONFIG.WRPINCFG is set. Reads 0.

fields.name: PULLEN
fields.text: Value loaded into PINCFGy.PULLEN of the pins chosen by WRCONFIG.PINMASK and WRCONFIG.HWSEL when WRCONFIG.WRPINCFG is set. Reads 0.

fields.name: INEN
fields.text: Value loaded into PINCFGy.INEN of the pins chosen by WRCONFIG.PINMASK and WRCONFIG.HWSEL when WRCONFIG.WRPINCFG is set. Reads 0.

fields.name: PMUXEN
fields.text: Value loaded into PINCFGy.PMUXEN of the pins chosen by WRCONFIG.PINMASK and WRCONFIG.HWSEL when WRCONFIG.WRPINCFG is set. Reads 0.

fields.name: PINMASK
fields.text: Chooses which pins of the half selected by WRCONFIG.HWSEL get reconfigured. Reads 0.

fields.name: PORTEI3
fields.text: PORT event input 3 enable.

values.text: Incoming events do not trigger EVACT3.

fields.name: EVACT3
fields.text: Action PORT takes on event input 3: 0x0 OUT, the pin's output register takes the event level; 0x1 SET, sets the pin's output register; 0x2 CLR, clears it; 0x3 TGL, toggles it.

values.name: OUT
values.text: Pin output register follows the event level.

values.name: SET
values.text: Pin output register set on event.

values.name: CLR
values.text: Pin output register cleared on event.

values.name: TGL
values.text: Pin output register toggled on event.

fields.name: PID3
fields.text: Selects the I/O pin of this group, 0 to 31, that EVACT3 acts on.

fields.name: PORTEI2
fields.text: PORT event input 2 enable.

values.text: Incoming events do not trigger EVACT2.

fields.name: EVACT2
fields.text: Action PORT takes on event input 2: 0x0 OUT, the pin's output register takes the event level; 0x1 SET, sets the pin's output register; 0x2 CLR, clears it; 0x3 TGL, toggles it.

values.name: OUT
values.text: Pin output register follows the event level.

values.name: SET
values.text: Pin output register set on event.

values.name: CLR
values.text: Pin output register cleared on event.

values.name: TGL
values.text: Pin output register toggled on event.

fields.name: PID2
fields.text: Selects the I/O pin of this group, 0 to 31, that EVACT2 acts on.

fields.name: PORTEI1
fields.text: PORT event input 1 enable.

values.text: Incoming events do not trigger EVACT1.

fields.name: EVACT1
fields.text: Action PORT takes on event input 1: 0x0 OUT, the pin's output register takes the event level; 0x1 SET, sets the pin's output register; 0x2 CLR, clears it; 0x3 TGL, toggles it.

values.name: OUT
values.text: Pin output register follows the event level.

values.name: SET
values.text: Pin output register set on event.

values.name: CLR
values.text: Pin output register cleared on event.

values.name: TGL
values.text: Pin output register toggled on event.

fields.name: PID1
fields.text: Selects the I/O pin of this group, 0 to 31, that EVACT1 acts on.

fields.name: PORTEI0
fields.text: PORT event input 0 enable.

values.text: Incoming events do not trigger EVACT0.

fields.name: EVACT0
fields.text: Action PORT takes on event input 0: 0x0 OUT, the pin's output register takes the event level; 0x1 SET, sets the pin's output register; 0x2 CLR, clears it; 0x3 TGL, toggles it.

values.name: OUT
values.text: Pin output register follows the event level.

values.name: SET
values.text: Pin output register set on event.

values.name: CLR
values.text: Pin output register cleared on event.

values.name: TGL
values.text: Pin output register toggled on event.

fields.name: PID0
fields.text: Selects the I/O pin of this group, 0 to 31, that EVACT0 acts on.

fields.name: PMUXO
fields.text: Peripheral function of the odd pin 2n+1 of the group, used when its PINCFGy.PMUXEN is 1; not every code is valid on every pin. 0x0 to 0xD select functions A to N in order; 0xE and 0xF are reserved.

fields.name: PMUXE
fields.text: Peripheral function of the even pin 2n of the group, used when its PINCFGy.PMUXEN is 1; not every code is valid on every pin. 0x0 to 0xD select functions A to N in order; 0xE and 0xF are reserved.

fields.name: DRVSTR
fields.text: Sets the drive strength of a pin used as an output. On devices with USB, PA24 and PA25 reset to 0.

fields.name: PULLEN
fields.text: Turns on the internal pull-up or pull-down of a pin used as an input.

values.text: Pull off; the input is high impedance.
Pull on; the input sits at a defined level when nothing drives it.

fields.name: INEN
fields.text: Controls the input buffer of a pin, whether input or output. With 0 the buffer is fully off and the pin's state cannot be read back.

values.text: Buffer off; the input is not sampled.
Buffer on; the input is sampled when needed.

fields.name: PMUXEN
fields.text: Hands the pin's direction and output level to the peripheral picked in PMUXn. With 0, DIR and OUT control the pad and PMUXn is ignored. With 1, the selected peripheral controls the pad, and IN still reads the pin when PINCFGn.INEN is set.

values.text: Multiplexer off; PORT registers control direction and drive.
Multiplexer on; the selected peripheral controls direction and drive.

peripherals.name: SERCOM USART
peripherals.title: SERCOM Synchronous and Asynchronous Receiver and Transmitter

fields.name: DORD
fields.text: Picks which end of a character goes out of the data register first. Not synchronized.

fields.name: CPOL
fields.text: In synchronous mode, sets which XCK edge changes the output data and which edge samples the input. Not synchronized.

fields.name: CMODE
fields.text: Chooses between asynchronous and synchronous operation. Not synchronized.

fields.name: FORM
fields.text: Sets the frame format. Not synchronized.

values.text: USART frame with a parity bit.
LIN host: generates break and sync, controlled by CTRLB.LINCMD.
LIN client auto-baud: detects break and sets the baud rate.
Auto-baud with break detection, frame with parity.

fields.name: SAMPA
fields.text: Sets which over-sampled clock ticks the receiver uses to take a bit's value. Not synchronized.

fields.name: RXPO
fields.text: Chooses which SERCOM pad carries received data (RxD). Not synchronized.

fields.name: TXPO
fields.text: Chooses which pads carry TxD and XCK, and where RTS/TE and CTS go. Not synchronized.

fields.name: SAMPR
fields.text: Sets the over-sampling rate and whether the baud generator is arithmetic or fractional. Not synchronized.

fields.name: RXINV
fields.text: Inverts the incoming RxD data. Start, parity and stop bits stay as they are, and parity is worked out on the inverted data. Valid only in ISO7816 T=0 mode (CTRLA.MODE = 0x7).

fields.name: TXINV
fields.text: Inverts the outgoing TxD data. Start, parity and stop bits stay as they are, and parity is worked out on the inverted data. Valid only in ISO7816 T=0 mode (CTRLA.MODE = 0x7).

fields.name: IBON
fields.text: Chooses when STATUS.BUFOVF goes high after a receive buffer overflow.

values.text: STATUS.BUFOVF rises at the overflow's place in the data stream.
STATUS.BUFOVF rises at once when the buffer overflows.

fields.name: RUNSTDBY
fields.text: Sets how the USART behaves in Standby sleep, with an external or an internal clock. Not synchronized.

rows: Once the transfer under way ends, the external clock is cut off and anything received is discarded.
Once the transfer under way ends, the generic clock stops; a Transfer Complete interrupt wakes the device only if the right ONDEMAND bits are set along the clock chain.
A Receive Complete interrupt wakes the device.
The generic clock keeps running in every sleep mode, and any interrupt can wake the device.

fields.name: MODE
fields.text: Picks the USART mode of the SERCOM and its clock source. Not synchronized.

fields.name: ENABLE
fields.text: Turns the USART on or off. The written value reads back at once, while SYNCBUSY.ENABLE stays set until the change has taken effect. Not enable-protected.

fields.name: SWRST
fields.text: Write 1 to return every SERCOM register except DBGCTRL to its reset value and disable the SERCOM; writing 0 does nothing. It overrides any other write made in the same access. While the reset runs, register writes give an APB error and reads return reset values. CTRLA.SWRST and SYNCBUSY.SWRST both clear when it finishes. Not enable-protected.

fields.name: LINCMD
fields.text: Controls how the LIN header is sent; used only when CTRLA.FORM selects LIN host. Strobe bits that always read 0. Not enable-protected.

values.text: A write to DATA sends a break field.
A write to DATA with the identifier sends break, sync and identifier on their own.

fields.name: RXEN
fields.text: Turns the receiver on or off. Writing 0 turns it off, empties the receive buffer and clears STATUS.FERR, PERR and BUFOVF. Writing 1 while the USART is off sets the bit at once. Writing 1 while the USART is on sets SYNCBUSY.CTRLB until the receiver is running, after which the bit reads 1. When the USART is enabled, CTRLB.RXEN clears and SYNCBUSY.CTRLB stays set until the receiver is on. Not enable-protected.

values.text: Receiver off, or still being turned on.
Receiver on, or will turn on when the USART is enabled.

fields.name: TXEN
fields.text: Turns the transmitter on or off. Writing 0 turns it off only after transmissions in progress and waiting have finished. Writing 1 while the USART is off sets the bit at once. Writing 1 while the USART is on sets SYNCBUSY.CTRLB until the transmitter is running, after which the bit reads 1. When the USART is enabled, CTRLB.TXEN clears and SYNCBUSY.CTRLB stays set until the transmitter is on. Not enable-protected.

values.text: Transmitter off, or still being turned on.
Transmitter on, or will turn on when the USART is enabled.

fields.name: PMODE
fields.text: Picks even or odd parity when parity is in use (CTRLA.FORM = 0x1 or 0x5). The transmitter adds the parity bit to every frame; the receiver checks it and sets STATUS.PERR on a mismatch. Not synchronized.

fields.name: ENC
fields.text: Chooses the data encoding. Not synchronized.

fields.name: SFDE
fields.text: Lets a start bit seen on RxD wake the device through the start-of-frame detector. Not synchronized.

values.text: Start-of-frame detection on; RXC wakes the device from any sleep mode.
Start-of-frame detection on; RXS wakes the device from any sleep mode.
Start-of-frame detection on; RXC and RXS both wake the device from any sleep mode.

fields.name: COLDEN
fields.text: Turns collision detection on. Not synchronized.

fields.name: SBMODE
fields.text: Sets how many stop bits are sent. Not synchronized.

fields.name: CHSIZE
fields.text: Sets the number of bits per character. Not synchronized.

fields.name: DATA32B
fields.text: Turns on 32-bit access to DATA for reads, writes or both; otherwise DATA is accessed by CTRLB.CHSIZE.

fields.name: MAXITER
fields.text: Highest number of retransmissions, and the number of NACKs in a row sent to the far transmitter when CTRLC.DSNACK is set. Valid only in ISO7816 T=0 mode (CTRLA.MODE = 0x7, CTRLA.CMODE = 0).

fields.name: DSNACK
fields.text: Limits how many NACKs go out for received parity errors. Valid only in ISO7816 T=0 mode with CTRLC.INACK = 0.

values.text: A NACK goes out on the ISO line for each parity error.
Parity errors are counted up to CTRLC.MAXITER, each sending a NACK; once that count is reached no more NACKs are sent.

fields.name: INACK
fields.text: Stops a NACK from being sent when a parity error is received. Valid only in ISO7816 T=0 mode.

fields.name: HDRDLY
fields.text: In LIN host mode (CTRLA.FORM = 0x2), sets the gap between break and sync and between sync and identifier. Applies only with CTRLB.LINCMD = 0x2. The setting must be chosen to meet the LIN specification.

values.text: Break to sync 1 bit time; sync to ID 1 bit time.
Break to sync 4 bit times; sync to ID 4 bit times.
Break to sync 8 bit times; sync to ID 4 bit times.
Break to sync 14 bit times; sync to ID 4 bit times.

fields.name: BRKLEN
fields.text: In LIN host mode (CTRLA.FORM = 0x2), sets how long the sent break field is. The setting must be chosen to meet the LIN specification.

fields.name: GTIME
fields.text: Guard time for RS485 mode (CTRLA.FORM = 0x0 or 0x1 with CTRLA.TXPO = 0x3) or ISO7816 mode (CTRLA.FORM = 0x7). In RS485 it is 0 to 7 bit times that TE stays high after the last stop bit once nothing is left to send. In ISO7816 T=0 it is 2 to 9 bit times between sent bytes.

fields.name: BAUD
fields.text: Sets the baud-rate generator. With arithmetic generation (CTRLA.SAMPR[0] = 0) all 16 bits are the baud value; with fractional generation (CTRLA.SAMPR[0] = 1) bits 15:13 become FP and bits 12:0 the integer baud value.

fields.name: FP
fields.text: Fractional part of the baud value, used with fractional baud generation (CTRLA.SAMPR[0] = 1).

fields.name: BAUD
fields.text: Integer baud value, used with fractional baud generation (CTRLA.SAMPR[0] = 1).

fields.name: RXPL
fields.text: With IrDA encoding (CTRLB.ENC = 1), sets the shortest pulse the IrDA receiver accepts, counted in serial engine clock periods SEper: a pulse is accepted when PULSE >= (RXPL + 2) * SEper.

registers.name: INTENCLR
registers.title: Interrupt Enable Clear
notes: Write 1s here to turn interrupts off without a read-modify-write; the change shows in INTENSET too.

fields.name: ERROR
fields.text: Write 1 to turn off the Error interrupt by clearing its enable; writing 0 does nothing. Reads the enable state.

fields.name: RXBRK
fields.text: Write 1 to turn off the Receive Break interrupt by clearing its enable; writing 0 does nothing. Reads the enable state.

fields.name: CTSIC
fields.text: Write 1 to turn off the Clear To Send Input Change interrupt by clearing its enable; writing 0 does nothing. Reads the enable state.

values.text: Clear To Send Input Change interrupt off.
Clear To Send Input Change interrupt on.

fields.name: RXS
fields.text: Write 1 to turn off the Receive Start interrupt by clearing its enable; writing 0 does nothing. Reads the enable state.

fields.name: RXC
fields.text: Write 1 to turn off the Receive Complete interrupt by clearing its enable; writing 0 does nothing. Reads the enable state.

fields.name: TXC
fields.text: Write 1 to turn off the Transmit Complete interrupt by clearing its enable; writing 0 does nothing. Reads the enable state.

fields.name: DRE
fields.text: Write 1 to turn off the Data Register Empty interrupt by clearing its enable; writing 0 does nothing. Reads the enable state.

registers.name: INTENSET
registers.title: Interrupt Enable Set
notes: Write 1s here to turn interrupts on without a read-modify-write; the change shows in INTENCLR too.

fields.name: ERROR
fields.text: Write 1 to turn on the Error interrupt by setting its enable; writing 0 does nothing. Reads the enable state.

fields.name: RXBRK
fields.text: Write 1 to turn on the Receive Break interrupt by setting its enable; writing 0 does nothing. Reads the enable state.

fields.name: CTSIC
fields.text: Write 1 to turn on the Clear To Send Input Change interrupt by setting its enable; writing 0 does nothing. Reads the enable state.

values.text: Clear To Send Input Change interrupt off.
Clear To Send Input Change interrupt on.

fields.name: RXS
fields.text: Write 1 to turn on the Receive Start interrupt by setting its enable; writing 0 does nothing. Reads the enable state.

fields.name: RXC
fields.text: Write 1 to turn on the Receive Complete interrupt by setting its enable; writing 0 does nothing. Reads the enable state.

fields.name: TXC
fields.text: Write 1 to turn on the Transmit Complete interrupt by setting its enable; writing 0 does nothing. Reads the enable state.

fields.name: DRE
fields.text: Write 1 to turn on the Data Register Empty interrupt by setting its enable; writing 0 does nothing. Reads the enable state.

fields.name: ERROR
fields.text: Set when any error is found; the errors are COLL, ISF, BUFOVF, FERR and PERR, each with its own flag in STATUS. Write 1 to clear. Writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: RXBRK
fields.text: Set when auto-baud is on (CTRLA.FORM) and a break character arrives. Write 1 to clear. Writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: CTSIC
fields.text: Set when the CTS pin changes level. Write 1 to clear. Writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: RXS
fields.text: Set when a start condition appears on RxD with start-of-frame detection on (CTRLB.SFDE = 1). Write 1 to clear. Writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: RXC
fields.text: Set while DATA holds unread data; cleared by reading DATA or turning the receiver off. Writes do nothing.

fields.name: TXC
fields.text: Set when the whole frame has left the transmit shift register and DATA holds nothing new. Cleared by writing 1 or by writing new data to DATA. Writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: DRE
fields.text: Set when DATA is empty and can take a new value; cleared by writing DATA. Writes do nothing.

fields.name: ITER
fields.text: Set in ISO7816 T=0 mode when the most NACK repetitions or retransmissions allowed have happened. Write 1 to clear. Writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: TXE
fields.text: In LIN host mode (CTRLA.FORM), set when any transmission in progress has finished and TxDATA is empty; in other modes it always reads 0. Write 1 to clear. Writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: COLL
fields.text: Set when collision detection is on (CTRLB.COLDEN) and a collision happens. Cleared by writing 1 or turning the receiver off. Writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: ISF
fields.text: Set when the frame format is auto-baud (CTRLA.FORM) and a received sync field is not 0x55. Cleared by writing 1 or turning the receiver off. Writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: CTS
fields.text: Shows the CTS pin's present level when flow control is on (CTRLA.TXPO). Writes do nothing.

fields.name: BUFOVF
fields.text: Set on a receive buffer overflow: the buffer is full, a character waits in the receive shift register and another start bit arrives. Read before DATA, it gives the status of the next character. Cleared by writing 1 or turning the receiver off. Writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: FERR
fields.text: Set when a received character's first stop bit is 0. Read before DATA, it gives the status of the next character. Cleared by writing 1 or turning the receiver off. Writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: PERR
fields.text: Set when parity checking is on (CTRLA.FORM = 0x1, 0x5 or 0x7) and a parity error is found. Read before DATA, it gives the status of the next character. Cleared by writing 1 or turning the receiver off. Writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: LENGTH
fields.text: High while a write to LENGTH is synchronizing. Writing LENGTH while this bit is high gives an APB error.

fields.name: RXERRCNT
fields.text: RXERRCNT is synchronized to the APB domain by itself when an error occurs; after waking from sleep this bit stays high until the new count can be read.

fields.name: CTRLB
fields.text: High while a write to CTRLB, made with the SERCOM enabled, is synchronizing. Writing CTRLB while this bit is high gives an APB error.

fields.name: ENABLE
fields.text: High while a write to CTRLA.ENABLE is synchronizing.

fields.name: SWRST
fields.text: High while a write to CTRLA.SWRST is synchronizing.

fields.name: RXERRCNT
fields.text: Count of parity errors and NACK errors together in ISO7816 mode (CTRLA.FORM = 0x7). Reading it clears it.

fields.name: LENEN
fields.text: In 32-bit extension mode, turns the length counter on for sending or for receiving.

fields.name: LEN
fields.text: In 32-bit extension mode, the data length after which INTFLAG.RXC or INTFLAG.DRE is raised.

fields.name: DATA
fields.text: Reading gives the receive data register; writing loads the transmit data register. Read it only when INTFLAG.RXC is set, reading STATUS first to catch any error for that character. Write it only when INTFLAG.DRE is set. Accesses are 32-bit or follow CTRLB.CHSIZE, as CTRLC.DATA32B sets.

fields.name: DBGSTOP
fields.text: Chooses whether the baud-rate generator keeps running while an external debugger halts the CPU.

fields.name: DORD
fields.text: Picks which end of a character goes out of the shift register first. Not synchronized.

fields.name: CPOL
fields.text: Clock idle level; with CPHA it sets the SPI transfer mode. Not synchronized.

values.text: SCK idles low; leading edge rises, trailing edge falls.
SCK idles high; leading edge falls, trailing edge rises.

fields.name: CPHA
fields.text: Clock phase; with CPOL it sets the SPI transfer mode. Mode 0x0 (CPOL 0, CPHA 0): sample on rising, change on falling. Mode 0x1 (0, 1): change on rising, sample on falling. Mode 0x2 (1, 0): sample on falling, change on rising. Mode 0x3 (1, 1): change on falling, sample on rising. Not synchronized.

values.text: Sample on the leading SCK edge, change on the trailing edge.
Sample on the trailing SCK edge, change on the leading edge.

fields.name: FORM
fields.text: Picks the client-mode frame format. With the address format, the first byte received is compared with ADDR.

fields.name: DIPO
fields.text: Chooses the pad for data in (DI): MISO as host, MOSI as client. Not synchronized.

fields.name: DOPO
fields.text: Chooses the pads for data out (DO) and SCK. As client, DOPO also places SS; as host, SS is set by the port configuration. DO is MOSI as host and MISO as client. Not synchronized.

rows: PAD[2] is host SS when MSSEN = 1; otherwise set by system configuration.
PAD[2] is host SS when MSSEN = 1; otherwise set by system configuration.

fields.name: IBON
fields.text: Chooses when STATUS.BUFOVF is set after a buffer overflow. Not synchronized.

values.text: STATUS.BUFOVF is set at the overflow's place in the data stream.
STATUS.BUFOVF is set at once when the buffer overflows.

fields.name: RUNSTDBY
fields.text: Sets how the SPI behaves in Standby sleep, as client or as host. Not synchronized.

rows: Off: everything received is discarded, the transaction under way included.
Once the transaction under way ends, the generic clock stops; any interrupt can wake the device.
The transaction under way carries on, and a Receive Complete interrupt wakes the device.
The generic clock keeps running during sleep, and any interrupt can wake the device.

fields.name: MODE
fields.text: Selects SPI for the SERCOM; must be 0x2 or 0x3. Not synchronized.

fields.name: ENABLE
fields.text: Turns the SPI on or off. The written value reads back at once, while SYNCBUSY.ENABLE stays set until the change has taken effect. Not enable-protected.

fields.name: SWRST
fields.text: Write 1 to return every SERCOM register except DBGCTRL to its reset value and disable the SERCOM; writing 0 does nothing. It overrides any other write made in the same access. While the reset runs, register writes give an APB error and reads return reset values. CTRLA.SWRST and SYNCBUSY.SWRST both clear when it finishes. Not enable-protected.

fields.name: RXEN
fields.text: Turns the receiver on or off. Writing 0 turns it off at once, empties the receive buffer, loses any reception in progress and clears STATUS.BUFOVF. Writing 1 while the SPI is off sets the bit at once. Writing 1 while the SPI is on sets SYNCBUSY.CTRLB until the receiver is running, after which the bit reads 1. When the SPI is enabled, CTRLB.RXEN clears and SYNCBUSY.CTRLB stays set until the receiver is on. Not enable-protected.

values.text: Receiver off, or still being turned on.
Receiver on, or will turn on when the SPI is enabled.

fields.name: AMODE
fields.text: Sets how a client matches addresses when the address frame format (CTRLA.FORM) is used; unused as host. Not synchronized.

values.name: 2_ADDRS
values.text: Client answers to the two addresses in ADDR and ADDRMASK.

values.name: RANGE
values.text: Client answers to every address from ADDRMASK up to ADDR, both included; ADDR is the top.

fields.name: MSSEN
fields.text: Lets the hardware drive SPI Select (SS) as host. Not synchronized.

fields.name: SSDE
fields.text: Lets a high-to-low edge on SS wake the device. Not synchronized.

fields.name: PLOADEN
fields.text: When set, the client shift register is preloaded while no transfer is running: data written to DATA with SS high moves to the shift register at once. Not synchronized.

fields.name: CHSIZE
fields.text: Sets the number of bits per character. Not synchronized.

fields.name: DATA32B
fields.text: Turns on 32-bit access to DATA; otherwise DATA is accessed by CTRLB.CHSIZE.

fields.name: ICSPACE
fields.text: When not 0, the least number of baud cycles SCK stays still between characters.

values.text: Least inter-character gap in baud cycles.

fields.name: BAUD
fields.text: Sets the baud-rate generator.

registers.name: INTENCLR
registers.title: Interrupt Enable Clear
notes: Write 1s here to turn interrupts off without a read-modify-write; the change shows in INTENSET too.

fields.name: ERROR
fields.text: Write 1 to turn off the Error interrupt by clearing its enable; writing 0 does nothing. Reads the enable state.

fields.name: SSL
fields.text: Write 1 to turn off the SPI Select Low interrupt by clearing its enable; writing 0 does nothing. Reads the enable state.

fields.name: RXC
fields.text: Write 1 to turn off the Receive Complete interrupt by clearing its enable; writing 0 does nothing. Reads the enable state.

fields.name: TXC
fields.text: Write 1 to turn off the Transmit Complete interrupt by clearing its enable; writing 0 does nothing. Reads the enable state.

fields.name: DRE
fields.text: Write 1 to turn off the Data Register Empty interrupt by clearing its enable; writing 0 does nothing. Reads the enable state.

registers.name: INTENSET
registers.title: Interrupt Enable Set
notes: Write 1s here to turn interrupts on without a read-modify-write; the change shows in INTENCLR too.

fields.name: ERROR
fields.text: Write 1 to turn on the Error interrupt by setting its enable; writing 0 does nothing. Reads the enable state.

fields.name: SSL
fields.text: Write 1 to turn on the SPI Select Low interrupt by setting its enable; writing 0 does nothing. Reads the enable state.

fields.name: RXC
fields.text: Write 1 to turn on the Receive Complete interrupt by setting its enable; writing 0 does nothing. Reads the enable state.

fields.name: TXC
fields.text: Write 1 to turn on the Transmit Complete interrupt by setting its enable; writing 0 does nothing. Reads the enable state.

fields.name: DRE
fields.text: Write 1 to turn on the Data Register Empty interrupt by setting its enable; writing 0 does nothing. Reads the enable state.

fields.name: ERROR
fields.text: Set when any error is found; BUFOVF and LENERR set it, each with its own flag in STATUS. Write 1 to clear. Writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: SSL
fields.text: Set in client mode when SS falls from high to low with CTRLB.SSDE on. Write 1 to clear. Writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: RXC
fields.text: Set while the receive buffer holds unread data; with address matching on, the first data of a transaction is the address. Cleared by reading DATA or turning the receiver off. Writes do nothing.

fields.name: TXC
fields.text: As host, set when the data has been shifted out and DATA holds nothing new; as client, set when SS goes high. With address matching on, set only for a transaction that began with a matching address. Cleared by writing 1 or by writing new data to DATA. Writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: DRE
fields.text: Set when DATA is empty and can take new data to send; cleared by writing DATA. Writes do nothing.

fields.name: LENERR
fields.text: Set in client mode, with the length counter on (LENGTH.LENEN = 1), when the length of a transfer while SS is low is not a whole multiple of LENGTH.LEN. Write 1 to clear. Writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: BUFOVF
fields.text: Set on a buffer overflow; the matching RxDATA is then 0. CTRLA.IBON sets when it is raised. Read before DATA, it gives the status of the next character. Cleared by writing 1 or turning the receiver off. Writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: LENGTH
fields.text: High while a write to LENGTH is synchronizing. Writing LENGTH while this bit is high gives an APB error. In client mode the clock runs only during a transfer, so the bit stays high until the next transfer starts.

fields.name: CTRLB
fields.text: High while a write to CTRLB, made with the SERCOM enabled, is synchronizing. Writing CTRLB while this bit is high gives an APB error.

fields.name: ENABLE
fields.text: High while a write to CTRLA.ENABLE is synchronizing.

fields.name: SWRST
fields.text: High while a write to CTRLA.SWRST is synchronizing.

fields.name: LENEN
fields.text: In 32-bit extension mode, turns the length counter on.

fields.name: LEN
fields.text: In 32-bit extension mode, the data length after which INTFLAG.RXC or INTFLAG.DRE is raised.

fields.name: ADDRMASK
fields.text: Address mask for the address frame format (CTRLA.FORM, CTRLB.AMODE).

fields.name: ADDR
fields.text: Address for the address frame format (CTRLA.FORM, CTRLB.AMODE).

fields.name: DATA
fields.text: Reading gives the receive data buffer; writing loads the transmit data buffer. Read it only when INTFLAG.RXC is set, and write it only when INTFLAG.DRE is set. Accesses are 32-bit or follow CTRLB.CHSIZE, as CTRLC.DATA32B sets.

fields.name: DBGSTOP
fields.text: Chooses whether the baud-rate generator keeps running while an external debugger halts the CPU.

fields.name: LOWTOUTEN
fields.text: Enables the SCL low time-out: when SCL stays low for 25-35 ms, the client lets go of any clock hold and resets its internal state machine; interrupt flags already set stay set. Not synchronized.

fields.name: SCLSM
fields.text: Picks the points at which SCL is stretched for software to act. Not synchronized.

values.text: SCL stretched at the default points.
SCL stretched only after the ACK bit.

fields.name: SPEED
fields.text: Selects the bus speed. Not synchronized.

values.text: Standard-mode up to 100 kHz and Fast-mode up to 400 kHz.

fields.name: SEXTTOEN
fields.text: Turns on the client SCL low extend time-out: once SCL has spent over 25 ms low in total between START and STOP, the client lets go of any clock hold and resets its state machine; interrupt flags already set stay set, and if the address had matched, PREC sets on the STOP. Not synchronized.

fields.name: SDAHOLD
fields.text: Sets how long SDA is held after the falling edge of SCL. Not synchronized.

fields.name: PINOUT
fields.text: Chooses two-wire or four-wire pin use. Not synchronized.

fields.name: RUNSTDBY
fields.text: Sets behaviour in standby sleep. Not synchronized.

values.text: Wakes on an address match, if that is enabled.

fields.name: MODE
fields.text: Write 0x4 to make the SERCOM an I2C client. Not synchronized.

fields.name: ENABLE
fields.text: Turns the SERCOM on or off. The written value reads back at once while SYNCBUSY.ENABLE is set; the peripheral changes state after a synchronization delay, and SYNCBUSY.ENABLE clears when it has. Not enable-protected.

fields.name: SWRST
fields.text: Software reset: a 1 returns every SERCOM register except DBGCTRL to its reset value and disables the SERCOM; a 0 does nothing. A 1 here overrides every other write in the same access. While the reset runs, any register write gives an APB error and reads return reset values. Completion takes a synchronization delay, after which CTRLA.SWRST and SYNCBUSY.SWRST both clear. Not enable-protected.

fields.name: ACKACT
fields.text: The ACK or NACK the client returns after it receives an address or data byte from the host. It is carried out when a command goes into CMD, or, with smart mode on (CTRLB.SMEN=1), when DATA is read. Change it at most once between interrupt requests. Not enable-protected.

fields.name: CMD
fields.text: Strobe bits that start a client operation, always reading 0. What happens depends on INTFLAG.DRDY, INTFLAG.AMATCH and STATUS.DIR. Issuing a command clears INTFLAG.DRDY, INTFLAG.AMATCH and INTFLAG.PREC. Not enable-protected.

rows: Acknowledge action, then wait for a START or repeated START.
Wait for a START or repeated START.
Answers INTFLAG.AMATCH or INTFLAG.DRDY; the action depends on the direction.
Acknowledge action, then receive the next byte.
Acknowledge action, then a client data interrupt.
Acknowledge action, then receive the next byte.
Read a byte, then receive ACK or NACK.

fields.name: AMODE
fields.text: Selects how the client matches addresses.

values.name: MASK
values.text: Matches ADDR.ADDR with ADDR.ADDRMASK as a mask.

values.name: 2_ADDRS
values.text: Matches either of the two addresses in ADDR.ADDR and ADDR.ADDRMASK.

values.name: RANGE
values.text: Matches every address from ADDR.ADDRMASK up to ADDR.ADDR, both ends included; ADDR.ADDR is the top.

fields.name: AACKEN
fields.text: When on, a matching address is acknowledged automatically.

fields.name: GCMD
fields.text: Turns on PMBus group command: INTFLAG.PREC then sets on any STOP seen on the bus if the client was addressed since the previous STOP.

fields.name: SMEN
fields.text: With smart mode on, a read of DATA.DATA acknowledges the received data automatically.

fields.name: DATA32B
fields.text: Makes accesses to the DATA register 32 bits wide instead of 8.

fields.name: SDASETUP
fields.text: Minimum setup time from SDA release to SCL release: tSU:DAT = (6 + 16 x SDASETUP) periods of CLK_SERCOMx_APB.

registers.name: INTENCLR
registers.title: Interrupt Enable Clear
notes: Clears interrupt enable bits without a read-modify-write; the result shows in INTENSET too.

fields.name: ERROR
fields.text: A 1 clears the Error interrupt enable, turning that interrupt off; a 0 does nothing.

fields.name: DRDY
fields.text: A 1 clears the Data Ready interrupt enable, turning that interrupt off; a 0 does nothing.

fields.name: AMATCH
fields.text: A 1 clears the Address Match interrupt enable, turning that interrupt off; a 0 does nothing.

fields.name: PREC
fields.text: A 1 clears the Stop Received interrupt enable, turning that interrupt off; a 0 does nothing.

registers.name: INTENSET
registers.title: Interrupt Enable Set
notes: Sets interrupt enable bits without a read-modify-write; the result shows in INTENCLR too.

fields.name: ERROR
fields.text: A 1 sets the Error interrupt enable, turning that interrupt on; a 0 does nothing.

fields.name: DRDY
fields.text: A 1 sets the Data Ready interrupt enable, turning that interrupt on; a 0 does nothing.

fields.name: AMATCH
fields.text: A 1 sets the Address Match interrupt enable, turning that interrupt on; a 0 does nothing.

fields.name: PREC
fields.text: A 1 sets the Stop Received interrupt enable, turning that interrupt on; a 0 does nothing.

fields.name: ERROR
fields.text: Sets on any error; the cause shows in STATUS.LENERR, SEXTTOUT, LOWTOUT, COLL or BUSERR. A 1 clears it; a 0 does nothing.

fields.name: DRDY
fields.text: Sets when the client has finished sending or receiving a byte. Hardware clears it on a write to DATA, a read of DATA with smart mode on, or a valid command in CMD. A 1 clears it; a 0 does nothing.

fields.name: AMATCH
fields.text: Sets when the client receives a valid address that matches. Hardware clears it when CMD is written. A 1 clears it, and the clear sends ACK or NACK as CTRLB.ACKACT says; a 0 does nothing.

fields.name: PREC
fields.text: Sets when a STOP ends a transaction this client is handling; a STOP between the host and another client sets it only with CTRLB.GCMD=1. Hardware clears it after a command at the next address match. A 1 clears it; a 0 does nothing.

fields.name: LENERR
fields.text: Sets when, with LENGTH.LENEN on, a STOP or repeated START arrives before or after LENGTH.LEN bytes. Clears by itself when CTRLB.CMD=0x3 answers a new START (ACK or NACK), or when INTFLAG.AMATCH is cleared. A 1 clears it; a 0 does nothing.

fields.name: HS
fields.text: Sets when the client sees a START followed by a Host Code. Clears by itself on a STOP; a 1 also clears it, a 0 does nothing.

fields.name: SEXTTOUT
fields.text: Sets on a client SCL low extend time-out. Clears by itself when CTRLB.CMD=0x3 answers a new START (ACK or NACK), or when INTFLAG.AMATCH is cleared. A 1 clears it; a 0 does nothing.

fields.name: CLKHOLD
fields.text: Set while the client holds SCL low to stretch the clock; it is set whenever INTFLAG.DRDY or INTFLAG.AMATCH is set and clears with that interrupt. Treat it as read-only.

fields.name: LOWTOUT
fields.text: Sets on an SCL low time-out. Clears by itself when CTRLB.CMD=0x3 answers a new START (ACK or NACK), or when INTFLAG.AMATCH is cleared. A 1 clears it; a 0 does nothing.

fields.name: SR
fields.text: At an address match, tells whether it followed a START or a repeated START. Valid only while INTFLAG.AMATCH is 1.

fields.name: DIR
fields.text: Direction of the last address the host sent.

fields.name: RXNACK
fields.text: Whether the host acknowledged the last data byte sent.

fields.name: COLL
fields.text: Sets when the client could not drive a high data bit or a NACK; it then lets go of SDA and SCL at once and waits to be addressed again. Meant for SMBus ARP; outside ARP a collision is a protocol violation, to be handled as a bus error. It raises no interrupt, so software checks it. Clears by itself when CTRLB.CMD=0x3 answers an address match (ACK or NACK), or when INTFLAG.AMATCH is cleared. A 1 clears it; a 0 does nothing.

values.text: No collision on the last byte sent.
Collision on the last byte sent.

fields.name: BUSERR
fields.text: Sets on an illegal bus condition, whoever owns the bus: a START, repeated START or STOP that breaks the protocol (such as a START straight into a STOP), or a time-out in mid-frame. Clears by itself when CTRLB.CMD=0x3 answers an address match (ACK or NACK), or when INTFLAG.AMATCH is cleared. A 1 clears it; a 0 does nothing.

fields.name: LENGTH
fields.text: Set after a write to LENGTH until it has synchronized; writing LENGTH again meanwhile gives an APB error. In client mode the clock runs only during transfers, so this stays set until the next transfer starts.

fields.name: ENABLE
fields.text: Set while CTRLA.ENABLE is being synchronized after a write to it; clears when done.

fields.name: SWRST
fields.text: Set while CTRLA.SWRST is being synchronized after a write to it; clears when done.

fields.name: LENEN
fields.text: Turns on the length counter in 32-bit mode (CTRLC.DATA32B=1).

fields.name: LEN
fields.text: Number of bytes, 0 to 255, after which INTFLAG.DRDY is raised, in 32-bit mode (CTRLC.DATA32B=1) with LENGTH.LENEN on.

fields.name: ADDRMASK
fields.text: A second matching address, a mask, or the bottom of an address range, as CTRLB.AMODE selects.

fields.name: TENBITEN
fields.text: Ten-bit addressing enable.

fields.name: ADDR
fields.text: The client's own address, compared against what the host sends: ADDR[6:0] for 7-bit addressing, ADDR[9:0] with ADDR.TENBITEN=1. On a match INTFLAG.AMATCH sets and STATUS.DIR shows read or write.

fields.name: GENCEN
fields.text: Enables answering the general call address: all zeros, direction bit included (a host write).

fields.name: DATA
fields.text: Gives access to the transmit and receive buffers. Data can be read or written only while the client holds SCL low (STATUS.CLKHOLD set), except reading the last byte after a STOP. An access starts bus activity set by CTRLB.ACKACT, CTRLB.SMEN and the access direction. Accesses are 32 bits with CTRLC.DATA32B=1, otherwise 8 bits.

fields.name: LOWTOUTEN
fields.text: Enables the SCL low time-out: when SCL stays low for 25-35 ms, the host lets go of any clock hold, ends the transaction and sends a STOP. INTFLAG.SB or INTFLAG.MB sets as usual, without the clock hold, and STATUS.LOWTOUT and STATUS.BUSERR set. Not synchronized.

fields.name: INACTOUT
fields.text: Bus inactivity time-out: when on and SCL is held low by any device for longer than the setting, the bus state goes to idle. Needed for SMBus, usable without it. Times assume 100 kHz. Not synchronized.

fields.name: SCLSM
fields.text: Picks the points at which SCL is stretched for software to act. Not synchronized.

values.text: SCL stretched at the default points.
SCL stretched only after the ACK bit.

fields.name: SPEED
fields.text: Selects the bus speed. Not synchronized.

values.text: Standard-mode up to 100 kHz and Fast-mode up to 400 kHz.

fields.name: SEXTTOEN
fields.text: Turns on the client SCL low extend time-out: once SCL has spent over 25 ms low in total between START and STOP, the host lets go of any clock hold, ends the transaction and sends a STOP. SB or MB sets as usual, CLKHOLD is released, and MEXTTOUT and BUSERR set. Not synchronized.

fields.name: MEXTTOEN
fields.text: Turns on the host SCL low extend time-out: once SCL has spent over 10 ms low in total in any one span (START to first ACK, between ACKs, or last ACK to STOP), the host lets go of any clock hold, ends the transaction and sends a STOP. SB or MB sets as usual, CLKHOLD is released, and MEXTTOUT and BUSERR set. Not synchronized.

fields.name: SDAHOLD
fields.text: Sets how long SDA is held after the falling edge of SCL. Not synchronized.

fields.name: PINOUT
fields.text: Chooses two-wire or four-wire pin use. Not synchronized.

fields.name: RUNSTDBY
fields.text: Sets behaviour in standby sleep. Not synchronized.

values.text: GCLK_SERCOMx_CORE stops; the host does not run in standby.
GCLK_SERCOMx_CORE runs in every sleep mode.

fields.name: MODE
fields.text: Write 0x5 to make the SERCOM an I2C host. Not synchronized.

fields.name: ENABLE
fields.text: Turns the SERCOM on or off. The written value reads back at once while SYNCBUSY.ENABLE is set; the peripheral changes state after a synchronization delay, and SYNCBUSY.ENABLE clears when it has. Not enable-protected.

fields.name: SWRST
fields.text: Software reset: a 1 returns every SERCOM register except DBGCTRL to its reset value and disables the SERCOM; a 0 does nothing. A 1 here overrides every other write in the same access. While the reset runs, any register write gives an APB error and reads return reset values. Completion takes a synchronization delay, after which CTRLA.SWRST and SYNCBUSY.SWRST both clear. Not enable-protected.

fields.name: ACKACT
fields.text: The ACK or NACK the host returns after it receives a data byte from a client. It is carried out when CTRLB.CMD is written, or, with smart mode on (CTRLB.SMEN=1), when DATA.DATA is read. Not enable-protected; not write-synchronized.

fields.name: CMD
fields.text: Strobe bits that start a host operation, always reading 0. The acknowledge action applies only when reading; when writing, a command can only give a repeated START or a STOP. ACKACT written in the same access takes effect before the command. Commands are accepted only while INTFLAG.SB or INTFLAG.MB is 1. Command 0x1 sends a repeated START and then the address already in ADDR.ADDR; for a new address, write ADDR.ADDR instead, which sends a repeated START and then that address. A command sets SYNCBUSY.SYSOP. Not enable-protected.

rows: Acknowledge action, then a byte read.

fields.name: QCEN
fields.text: Quick command enable. Not write-synchronized.

fields.name: SMEN
fields.text: With smart mode on, the acknowledge action goes out when DATA.DATA is read. Not write-synchronized.

fields.name: DATA32B
fields.text: Makes accesses to the DATA register 32 bits wide instead of 8.

fields.name: HSBAUDLOW
fields.text: Non-zero: High-speed SCL low time, HSBAUDLOW = fGCLK x TLOW - 1. Zero: HSBAUD times all of TLOW, THIGH, TSU;STO, THD;STA, TSU;STA. BAUD times TBUF.

fields.name: HSBAUD
fields.text: High-speed SCL high time, HSBAUD = fGCLK x THIGH - 1. With HSBAUDLOW at zero, it also times TLOW, TSU;STO, THD;STA, TSU;STA. BAUD times TBUF.

fields.name: BAUDLOW
fields.text: When non-zero, sets the SCL low time.

fields.name: BAUD
fields.text: Sets the SCL high time when BAUD.BAUDLOW is non-zero; when BAUDLOW is zero it sets both the high and low times.

registers.name: INTENCLR
registers.title: Interrupt Enable Clear
notes: Clears interrupt enable bits without a read-modify-write; the result shows in INTENSET too.

fields.name: ERROR
fields.text: A 1 clears the Error interrupt enable, turning that interrupt off; a 0 does nothing.

fields.name: SB
fields.text: A 1 clears the Client on Bus interrupt enable, turning that interrupt off; a 0 does nothing.

fields.name: MB
fields.text: A 1 clears the Host on Bus interrupt enable, turning that interrupt off; a 0 does nothing.

registers.name: INTENSET
registers.title: Interrupt Enable Set
notes: Sets interrupt enable bits without a read-modify-write; the result shows in INTENCLR too.

fields.name: ERROR
fields.text: A 1 sets the Error interrupt enable, turning that interrupt on; a 0 does nothing.

fields.name: SB
fields.text: A 1 sets the Client on Bus interrupt enable, turning that interrupt on; a 0 does nothing.

fields.name: MB
fields.text: A 1 sets the Host on Bus interrupt enable, turning that interrupt on; a 0 does nothing.

fields.name: ERROR
fields.text: Sets on any error; the cause shows in STATUS.LENERR, SEXTTOUT, MEXTTOUT, LOWTOUT, ARBLOST or BUSERR. A 1 clears it; a 0 does nothing.

fields.name: SB
fields.text: Sets when a byte is received cleanly in host read mode (no lost arbitration, no bus error); the host then holds SCL low. SCL is released and the flag clears on a write to ADDR.ADDR, a write to DATA.DATA, a read of DATA.DATA with CTRLB.SMEN on, or a valid command in CTRLB.CMD. A 1 also clears it; the transfer waits until one of those actions. A 0 does nothing.

fields.name: MB
fields.text: Sets when a byte is sent in host write mode, bus error or lost arbitration or not; also when arbitration is lost while sending a NACK in host read mode, or on a START with the bus state unknown. If arbitration was not lost, the host then holds SCL low. SCL is released and the flag clears on a write to ADDR.ADDR, a write to DATA.DATA, a read of DATA.DATA with CTRLB.SMEN on, or a valid command in CTRLB.CMD. A 1 also clears it; the transfer waits until one of those actions. A 0 does nothing.

fields.name: LENERR
fields.text: Sets when, with automatic length in use for DMA or 32-bit transfers, the client sends NACK before the host has written ADDR.LEN bytes. Clears on a write to ADDR or a write of 1; a 0 does nothing. Not write-synchronized.

fields.name: SEXTTOUT
fields.text: Sets on a client SCL low extend time-out. Clears on a write to ADDR or a write of 1, which normal use does not need; a 0 does nothing. Not write-synchronized.

fields.name: MEXTTOUT
fields.text: Sets on a host SCL low time-out. Clears on a write to ADDR or a write of 1; a 0 does nothing. Not write-synchronized.

fields.name: CLKHOLD
fields.text: Set while the host holds SCL low to stretch the clock; meaningful while either INTFLAG.SB or INTFLAG.MB is set. Clears when that flag clears and the next operation is given. Writes do nothing. Not write-synchronized.

fields.name: LOWTOUT
fields.text: Sets on an SCL low time-out. Clears on a write to ADDR or a write of 1; a 0 does nothing. Not write-synchronized.

fields.name: BUSSTATE
fields.text: Current state of the I2C bus. Only from UNKNOWN can it be forced, and only to IDLE, by writing 0x1; that write sets SYNCBUSY.SYSOP.

values.name: UNKNOWN
values.text: Unknown: waits for a STOP or to be forced to idle by software.

values.name: IDLE
values.text: Idle: waiting for a transaction to start.

values.name: OWNER
values.text: Owner: this host holds the bus.

values.name: BUSY
values.text: Busy: another host holds the bus.

fields.name: RXNACK
fields.text: Whether the client acknowledged the last address or data byte sent. Writes do nothing. Not write-synchronized.

fields.name: ARBLOST
fields.text: Sets when arbitration is lost while sending a high data bit or a NACK, or during a START or repeated START; INTFLAG.MB sets with it. Clears on a write to ADDR.ADDR or a write of 1; a 0 does nothing. Not write-synchronized.

fields.name: BUSERR
fields.text: Sets on an illegal bus condition, whoever owns the bus: a START, repeated START or STOP that breaks the protocol (such as a START straight into a STOP), or a time-out in mid-frame. If this host owns the bus at the time, STATUS.ARBLOST and INTFLAG.MB set too. Clears on a write to ADDR.ADDR or a write of 1; a 0 does nothing. Not write-synchronized.

fields.name: SYSOP
fields.text: Set after a write to CTRLB.CMD, STATUS.BUSSTATE, ADDR or DATA while the SERCOM is enabled, until that write has synchronized.

fields.name: ENABLE
fields.text: Set while CTRLA.ENABLE is being synchronized after a write to it; clears when done.

fields.name: SWRST
fields.text: Set while CTRLA.SWRST is being synchronized after a write to it; clears when done.

fields.name: LEN
fields.text: Length of a DMA or 32-bit transfer, 0 to 255 bytes. DMA needs LENEN set to 1.

fields.name: TENBITEN
fields.text: Turns on 10-bit addressing; may be written in the same access as ADDR to choose a 10-bit or 7-bit address.

fields.name: HS
fields.text: Turns on High-speed mode for this transfer, from repeated START to STOP; may be written in the same access as ADDR.

fields.name: LENEN
fields.text: Transfer length enable.

fields.name: ADDR
fields.text: Writing it starts an action that depends on the bus state. UNKNOWN: INTFLAG.MB and STATUS.BUSERR set and nothing more happens. BUSY: the host waits for IDLE. IDLE: the host sends a START and the address; if acknowledged, it holds SCL low and sets STATUS.CLKHOLD and INTFLAG.MB. OWNER: a repeated START follows, preceded by the acknowledge action if the last transfer was a read; do this while either INTFLAG.MB or INTFLAG.SB is set. A write clears STATUS.BUSERR, STATUS.ARBLOST and both INTFLAG.MB and INTFLAG.SB. Reading it never disturbs the bus. Bit 0 is the R/W bit: 0 write, 1 read.

fields.name: DATA
fields.text: Gives access to the transmit and receive buffers. Data can be read or written only while the host holds SCL low (STATUS.CLKHOLD set), except reading the last byte after a STOP has been sent. An access starts bus activity set by CTRLB.ACKACT, CTRLB.SMEN and the access direction. Accesses are 32 bits with CTRLC.DATA32B=1, otherwise 8 bits.

fields.name: DBGSTOP
fields.text: Sets what happens while an external debugger halts the CPU.

fields.name: LASTXFER
fields.text: Last transfer: writing 1 releases CS once the character in TXDATA has been sent.

values.text: CS is released once the character in TXDATA has gone out.

fields.name: ENABLE
fields.text: Writing 1 turns the QSPI on for sending and receiving; writing 0 turns it off. Once cleared, any transfer under way completes, then every pin becomes an input and no data moves.

fields.name: SWRST
fields.text: Writing 1 resets the QSPI through a software-triggered hardware reset; writing 0 does nothing. DMAC channels keep their state.

fields.name: DLYCS
fields.text: Shortest time CS stays inactive between deselect and the next select, the client's minimum deselect time. 0x00 gives one CLK_QSPI_AHB period; otherwise DLYCS = minimum inactive time × peripheral clock frequency.

fields.name: DLYBCT
fields.text: Delay added after each transfer to the same peripheral while CS stays asserted, and before CS is released if it is. 0x00 adds none and SCK keeps its duty cycle across characters. Ignored in Serial Memory mode (MODE=1). Otherwise DLYBCT = (delay × peripheral clock frequency) / 32.

fields.name: DATALEN
fields.text: Number of bits in each transfer. Do not use the reserved codes.

fields.name: CSMODE
fields.text: How CS is released.

values.name: NORELOAD
values.text: CS releases when TXDATA is not refilled before the current transfer ends.

values.name: LASTXFER
values.text: CS releases once CTRLA.LASTXFER is written 1 and the character in TXDATA has gone out.

fields.name: SMEMREG
fields.text: Serial memory register mode: which bus writes the serial memory registers.

values.text: Written over APB; reset the QSPI.

fields.name: WDRBT
fields.text: Wait for data read before transfer option.

fields.name: LOOPEN
fields.text: Turns on local loopback on the data serializer, MISO tied internally to MOSI, for testing; SPI mode only.

fields.name: MODE
fields.text: Picks SPI mode or Serial Memory mode.

fields.name: DLYBS
fields.text: Delay from CS going valid to the first SCK edge. At 0 it is half an SCK period; otherwise delay = DLYBS / MCK.

fields.name: BAUD
fields.text: SCK divider: a modulus counter divides CLK_QSPI_AHB down to SCK, set by any value 0 to 255, giving SCK rate = MCK / (BAUD + 1).

fields.name: CPHA
fields.text: Clock phase: picks which SCK edge shifts data out and which samples it; set together with CPOL to match host and client.

values.text: Sampled on the leading SCK edge, shifted on the trailing edge.
Shifted on the leading SCK edge, sampled on the trailing edge.

fields.name: CPOL
fields.text: Clock polarity: the idle level of SCK; set together with CPHA to match host and client.

fields.name: DATA
fields.text: Received data, right-justified; unused bits read 0.

fields.name: DATA
fields.text: Data to send, written right-justified.

fields.name: INSTREND
fields.text: Writing 1 disables the Instruction End interrupt; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: CSRISE
fields.text: Writing 1 disables the Chip Select Rise interrupt; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: ERROR
fields.text: Writing 1 disables the Overrun Error interrupt; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: TXC
fields.text: Writing 1 disables the Transmission Complete interrupt; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: DRE
fields.text: Writing 1 disables the Transmit Data Register Empty interrupt; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: RXC
fields.text: Writing 1 disables the Receive Data Register Full interrupt; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: INSTREND
fields.text: Writing 1 enables the Instruction End interrupt; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: CSRISE
fields.text: Writing 1 enables the Chip Select Rise interrupt; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: ERROR
fields.text: Writing 1 enables the Overrun Error interrupt; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: TXC
fields.text: Writing 1 enables the Transmission Complete interrupt; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: DRE
fields.text: Writing 1 enables the Transmit Data Register Empty interrupt; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: RXC
fields.text: Writing 1 enables the Receive Data Register Full interrupt; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: INSTREND
fields.text: Goes to 1 when an instruction end is detected; write 1 to clear, 0 does nothing.

fields.name: CSRISE
fields.text: Goes to 1 when CS is seen rising; write 1 to clear, 0 does nothing.

fields.name: ERROR
fields.text: Goes to 1 on an overrun: RXDATA loaded from the serializer twice or more without a read. Write 1 to clear, 0 does nothing.

fields.name: TXC
fields.text: Transmission complete: TXDATA and the shifter are both empty.

values.text: Cleared as soon as TXDATA is written.
TXDATA and the internal shifter are empty; with a transfer delay set, it rises once that delay has also ended.

fields.name: DRE
fields.text: TXDATA is ready for new data. Reads 0 while the QSPI is off or in reset, and goes to 1 as soon as CTRLA.ENABLE is set.

values.text: TXDATA holds data not yet moved to the serializer.
The last data written to TXDATA has moved to the serializer.

fields.name: RXC
fields.text: RXDATA holds newly received data.

values.text: Nothing received since RXDATA was last read.
Data was received and moved from the serializer to RXDATA since RXDATA was last read.

fields.name: CSSTATUS
fields.text: Chip select state.

fields.name: ENABLE
fields.text: Enable state of the QSPI.

fields.name: ADDR
fields.text: Address sent to the serial flash in the instruction frame.

fields.name: OPTCODE
fields.text: Option code sent to the serial flash.

fields.name: INSTR
fields.text: Instruction code sent to the serial flash.

fields.name: DUMMYLEN
fields.text: Number of dummy cycles the serial flash needs before data moves.

fields.name: DDREN
fields.text: Double data rate on or off; supported for reads only.

fields.name: CRMODE
fields.text: Continuous Read Mode on or off.

fields.name: TFRTYPE
fields.text: Kind of data transfer.

values.name: READ
values.text: Read from the serial memory, no scrambling; no random-location fetch.

values.name: READMEMORY
values.text: Data read from the serial memory, scrambled if scrambling is on; random-location fetch possible.

values.name: WRITE
values.text: Write to the serial memory, no scrambling.

values.name: WRITEMEMORY
values.text: Data write to the serial memory, scrambled if scrambling is on.

fields.name: ADDRLEN
fields.text: Address length.

fields.name: OPTCODELEN
fields.text: Option code length; must suit WIDTH: with WIDTH=6, sending the option over QuadSPI, a 1-bit option (OPTCODELEN=0) does not fit, as the option then needs at least 4 bits.

fields.name: DATAEN
fields.text: Data enable: whether the frame carries data.

values.text: No data sent to or read from the serial flash.
Data sent to or read from the serial flash.

fields.name: OPTCODEEN
fields.text: Option enable: whether the option code is sent.

fields.name: ADDREN
fields.text: Address enable: whether the address is sent.

fields.name: INSTREN
fields.text: Instruction enable: whether the instruction code is sent.

fields.name: WIDTH
fields.text: Bus width used for the instruction code, the address and option, and the data.

values.name: SINGLE_BIT_SPI
values.text: Instruction single-bit, address/option single-bit, data single-bit.

values.name: DUAL_OUTPUT
values.text: Instruction single-bit, address/option single-bit, data dual.

values.name: QUAD_OUTPUT
values.text: Instruction single-bit, address/option single-bit, data quad.

values.name: DUAL_IO
values.text: Instruction single-bit, address/option dual, data dual.

values.name: QUAD_IO
values.text: Instruction single-bit, address/option quad, data quad.

values.name: DUAL_CMD
values.text: Instruction dual, address/option dual, data dual.

values.name: QUAD_CMD
values.text: Instruction quad, address/option quad, data quad.

fields.name: RANDOMDIS
fields.text: Leaves the per-chip random value out of the scrambling.

values.text: Scrambling uses the user key plus a random value that can vary between chips.
Scrambling uses the user key alone.

fields.name: ENABLE
fields.text: Turns scrambling and unscrambling on or off.

fields.name: KEY
fields.text: Scrambling user key value.

fields.name: MODE
fields.text: Picks USB device or host operation.

fields.name: RUNSTDBY
fields.text: Keeps the USB clock running in standby. Enable-protected.

fields.name: ENABLE
fields.text: Turns the USB on or off. Write-synchronized: the written value reads back at once and SYNCBUSY.ENABLE is set until the change has taken effect, then cleared.

fields.name: SWRST
fields.text: Writing 1 returns every USB register to its reset value and disables the USB; writing 0 does nothing. Any other write in the same operation is discarded. CTRLA.SWRST and SYNCBUSY.SWRST clear when the reset is done; poll SYNCBUSY.SWRST to know when, and until then only registers and bits that have SWRST can be accessed.

fields.name: ENABLE
fields.text: 1 while CTRLA.ENABLE is being synchronized between clock domains; cleared when done.

fields.name: SWRST
fields.text: 1 while CTRLA.SWRST is being synchronized between clock domains; cleared when done.

registers.name: QOSCTRL
registers.title: QOS Control
notes: The register's reset value is also given as 0x000x0F.

fields.name: DQOS
fields.text: Memory access priority for endpoint or pipe data reads and writes, per the SRAM quality of service levels.

fields.name: CQOS
fields.text: Memory access priority for endpoint or pipe configuration reads and writes, per the SRAM quality of service levels.

registers.name: FSMSTATUS
registers.title: Finite State Machine Status
notes: The register's reset value is also given as 0xXXXX.

fields.name: FSMSTATE
fields.text: State of the USB controller's finite state machine.

values.name: OFF
values.text: L3: powered off, disconnected or disabled.

fields.name: DESCADD
fields.text: Base address in RAM of the main USB descriptor; bits 1:0 must be written 0.

registers.name: PADCAL
registers.title: Pad Calibration
notes: Before the USB is enabled, software copies the pad trim values held in the NVM Software Calibration Area (SW0) into PADCAL; without them the specified accuracy is not met.

fields.name: TRIM
fields.text: Calibrates how well DP/DM rise and fall times match.

fields.name: TRANSN
fields.text: Calibrates the NMOS output impedance of the DP/DM drivers.

fields.name: TRANSP
fields.text: Calibrates the PMOS output impedance of the DP/DM drivers.

fields.name: LPMHDSK
fields.text: Link Power Management handshake setting.

fields.name: GNAK
fields.text: Global NAK: sets how NAK is answered. Not synchronized.

values.text: The handshake gives the transaction's real status.
Every transaction is answered NAK whatever the endpoint bank status.

fields.name: NREPLY
fields.text: No reply except to SETUP, endpoint 0 only; hardware clears it when a SETUP packet arrives.

values.text: Off: endpoint 0 transactions follow the USB 2.0 standard.
On: endpoint 0 ignores everything except SETUP.

fields.name: SPDCONF
fields.text: Speed setting.

fields.name: UPRSM
fields.text: Sends an upstream resume. Cleared on a USB reset or once the resume has gone out.

values.text: Writing 1 sends an upstream resume to the host as a remote wakeup.

fields.name: DETACH
fields.text: Detaches the device from the bus.

values.text: Attached; the device can communicate on the bus.
Reset value: internal pull-ups off, so the device is off the bus.

fields.name: ADDEN
fields.text: Turns the device address on; cleared when a USB reset arrives.

values.text: Writing 0 turns DADD off and returns the device to address 0.

fields.name: LPMSUSP
fields.text: Goes to 1 when the USB acknowledges a Link Power Management transaction with ACK and enters Suspend; interrupts if LPMSUSP is enabled. Write 1 to clear, 0 does nothing.

fields.name: LPMNYET
fields.text: Goes to 1 when the USB answers a Link Power Management transaction with NYET; interrupts if LPMNYET is enabled. Write 1 to clear, 0 does nothing.

fields.name: RAMACER
fields.text: Goes to 1 on a RAM access underflow during an IN data stage; interrupts if RAMACER is enabled. Write 1 to clear, 0 does nothing.

fields.name: UPRSM
fields.text: Goes to 1 when the USB sends an upstream resume; interrupts if UPRSM is enabled. Write 1 to clear, 0 does nothing.

fields.name: EORSM
fields.text: Goes to 1 when the USB detects a valid host-started end of resume; interrupts if EORSM is enabled. Write 1 to clear, 0 does nothing.

fields.name: WAKEUP
fields.text: Goes to 1 when a filtered non-idle signal on the lines wakes the USB; interrupts if WAKEUP is enabled. Write 1 to clear, 0 does nothing.

fields.name: EORST
fields.text: Goes to 1 when a USB end of reset is detected; interrupts if EORST is enabled. Write 1 to clear, 0 does nothing.

fields.name: SOF
fields.text: Goes to 1 when a USB start of frame is detected, every 1 ms, and FNUM is updated; interrupts if SOF is enabled. Write 1 to clear, 0 does nothing.

fields.name: SUSPEND
fields.text: Goes to 1 when the bus has been idle in suspend for 3 frame periods (J state for 3 ms); interrupts if SUSPEND is enabled. Write 1 to clear, 0 does nothing.

fields.name: EPINT
fields.text: EPINT[n] is 1 while endpoint n has an interrupt pending, as raised in its EPINTFLAGn register; it clears once none is pending.

fields.name: EPTYPE1
fields.text: Sets the endpoint type for the IN direction (bank 1); a USB reset clears it on every endpoint but endpoint 0, which keeps its value.

fields.name: EPTYPE0
fields.text: Sets the endpoint type for the OUT direction (bank 0); a USB reset clears it on every endpoint but endpoint 0, which keeps its value.

registers.title: EndPoint Status n
notes: The register's reset value is also given as 0x00.

fields.name: BK1RDY
fields.text: Shows whether bank 1 is ready; a 1 written to EPSTATUSCLR.BK1RDY clears it and a 1 written to EPSTATUSSET.BK1RDY sets it.

values.text: Not ready: an IN endpoint's bank is not yet filled; a Control/OUT endpoint's bank is empty.
Ready: an IN endpoint's bank is filled; a Control/OUT endpoint's bank is full.

fields.name: BK0RDY
fields.text: Shows whether bank 0 is ready; a 1 written to EPSTATUSCLR.BK0RDY clears it and a 1 written to EPSTATUSSET.BK0RDY sets it.

values.text: Not ready: an IN endpoint's bank is not yet filled; a Control/OUT endpoint's bank is empty.
Ready: an IN endpoint's bank is filled; a Control/OUT endpoint's bank is full.

fields.name: STALLRQ
fields.text: Requests a STALL on bank x; cleared through EPSTATUSCLR.STALLRQ, set by a 1 written to EPSTATUSSET.STALLRQ, and cleared by hardware when a SETUP packet arrives.

values.text: STALL request on: the host gets a STALL handshake for bank x.

fields.name: CURBK
fields.text: Shows which bank the next single or multi-packet transfer uses; cleared through EPSTATUSCLR.CURBK, set by a 1 written to EPSTATUSSET.CURBK.

fields.name: DTGLIN
fields.text: Data toggle of the next IN transaction; cleared through EPSTATUSCLR.DTGLIN, set by a 1 written to EPSTATUSSET.DTGLIN.

values.text: Next IN transaction expects PID DATA0.
Next IN transaction expects PID DATA1.

fields.name: DTGLOUT
fields.text: Data toggle of the next OUT transaction; cleared through EPSTATUSCLR.DTGLOUT, set by a 1 written to EPSTATUSSET.DTGLOUT.

values.text: Next OUT transaction expects PID DATA0.
Next OUT transaction expects PID DATA1.

fields.name: STALL
fields.text: Set on a transmit stall, and raises an interrupt when EPINTENCLR/SET.STALL is 1; it sets for a single-bank OUT or a dual-bank IN/OUT endpoint when the current bank is 0. Write 1 to clear; a 0 does nothing.

fields.name: RXSTP
fields.text: Set when a SETUP is received, and raises an interrupt when EPINTENCLR/SET.RXSTP is 1. Write 1 to clear; a 0 does nothing.

fields.name: TRFAIL
fields.text: Set when a transfer fails, and raises an interrupt when EPINTENCLR/SET.TRFAIL is 1; it sets for a single-bank OUT or a dual-bank IN/OUT endpoint when the current bank is 0. Write 1 to clear; a 0 does nothing.

fields.name: TRCPT
fields.text: Set when a transfer completes, and raises an interrupt when EPINTENCLR/SET.TRCPT is 1; it sets for a single-bank OUT or a dual-bank IN/OUT endpoint when the current bank is 0. Write 1 to clear; a 0 does nothing.
