fields.name: ADDR
fields.text: Absolute RAM word address of the bank's data buffer; its two low bits must be 0 so the buffer starts 32-bit aligned.

fields.name: AUTO_ZLP
fields.text: Turns on hardware handling of the zero-length-packet handshake, for IN endpoints only; with it off, firmware handles the handshake.

fields.name: SIZE
fields.text: Largest packet the endpoint takes; sizes above 64 bytes are for isochronous endpoints only.

fields.name: MULTI_PACKET_SIZE
fields.text: 14-bit byte count for multi-packet transfers. IN: total bytes sent so far, written 0 when a new transfer is set up. OUT: total size of the whole transfer, a multiple of the maximum packet size.

fields.name: BYTE_COUNT
fields.text: 14-bit byte count. IN: bytes to send in the next IN transaction. OUT or SETUP: bytes received in the last OUT or SETUP transaction.

registers.name: EXTREG
registers.title: Extended Register
notes: The register's reset value is also given as 0xXXXXXXX.

fields.name: VARIABLE
fields.text: VARIABLE field of a received extended (LPM) token, updated once the USB has answered the LPM transaction with ACK. Bits 3:0 are bLinkState, 7:4 BESL, 8 bRemoteWake, 10:9 reserved, as the USB 2.0 LPM addendum defines them.

fields.name: SUBPID
fields.text: SUBPID field of a received extended (LPM) token, updated once the USB has answered the LPM transaction with ACK.

registers.name: STATUS_BK
registers.title: Device Status Bank
notes: The register's reset value is also given as 0xXXXXXXX.

fields.name: ERRORFLOW
fields.text: Set when a flow error occurred in a transfer to or from this bank: an OUT transfer answered with NAK, or an isochronous OUT overrun. Not valid for IN transfers. EPSTATUS.TRFAIL0 and TRFAIL1 also show flow errors.

fields.name: CRCERR
fields.text: Set when a CRC error is found in an isochronous OUT endpoint bank.

fields.name: L1RESUME
fields.text: Write 1 to send a USB L1 Resume, whose length is set by BESL in EXTREG.VARIABLE[7:4]; a 0 does nothing. Cleared once the L1 Resume is sent or a USB reset is requested.

values.text: Sends a USB L1 Resume; set only while Start-of-Frame generation is on (SOFE = 1).

fields.name: VBUSOK
fields.text: Tells the host that VBUS is good and USB operation may start; while it is 0 host operation stays halted even with the host configured and enabled.

fields.name: BUSRESET
fields.text: Sends a USB reset on the bus.

values.text: No reset generated; hardware writes it to 0 when the reset ends or a device disconnects, and a 0 written does nothing.
Sends a USB reset on the bus.

fields.name: SOFE
fields.text: Turns Start-of-Frame generation on or off.

values.text: SOF generation off; the bus is suspended.
Sends SOF at full speed and keep-alive at low speed; hardware sets it when a USB reset ends (INTFLAG.RST), when a downstream resume ends (INTFLAG.DNRSM) and when an L1 resume ends.

fields.name: AUTORESUME
fields.text: Turns automatic resume on or off.

fields.name: SPDCONF
fields.text: Selects the host's speed.

fields.name: RESUME
fields.text: Write 1 to send a USB Resume; a 0 does nothing. Cleared once the Resume is sent or a USB reset is requested.

values.text: Sends a USB Resume on the bus.

registers.name: HSOFC
registers.title: Host Start-of-Frame Control
notes: Locked for a short time just before each Start-of-Frame goes out, so a write may need reading back and repeating. A USB reset clears it.

fields.name: FLENCE
fields.text: At 1, FLENC[3:0] trims the time between Start-of-Frames by up to +/-0.06%; must be 0 at low speed.

values.text: SOF period follows signed FLENC[3:0]: 1 ms + FLENC/12000 ms.

fields.name: FLENC
fields.text: Signed 4-bit trim that FLENCE = 1 adds to the internal frame length; with FLENCE at 0 the frame length is the frame counter's top value.

fields.name: LINESTATE
fields.text: Present DP/DM line state.

fields.name: SPEED
fields.text: Speed the host is using now.

fields.name: FNUM
fields.text: Present SOF number; a write loads a new number, which takes effect at the next SOF and clears MFNUM. The register spans two byte addresses, so a byte-wide write can corrupt the count; write it as a word or half-word.

fields.name: FLENHIGH
fields.text: Top 8 bits of the internal frame counter; at full speed with a 12 MHz USB clock the counter runs to 12000 so an SOF goes out every 1 ms.

registers.name: INTFLAG
registers.title: Host Interrupt Flag Status and Clear

fields.name: DDISC
fields.text: Set when the device leaves the bus, and raises an interrupt when INTENCLR/SET.DDISC is 1. Write 1 to clear; a 0 does nothing.

fields.name: DCONN
fields.text: Set when a new device joins the bus, and raises an interrupt when INTENCLR/SET.DCONN is 1. Write 1 to clear; a 0 does nothing.

fields.name: RAMACER
fields.text: Set on a RAM access error during an OUT stage, and raises an interrupt when INTENCLR/SET.RAMACER is 1. Write 1 to clear; a 0 does nothing.

fields.name: UPRSM
fields.text: Set when an upstream resume from the device is received, and raises an interrupt when INTENCLR/SET.UPRSM is 1. Write 1 to clear; a 0 does nothing.

fields.name: DNRSM
fields.text: Set when the USB has sent a downstream resume, and raises an interrupt when INTENCLR/SET.DNRSM is 1. Write 1 to clear; a 0 does nothing.

fields.name: WAKEUP
fields.text: Set when, in suspend (SOFE = 0), an upstream resume or a device disconnection is seen, or when, operational (VBUSOK = 1), a device connection is seen; raises an interrupt when INTENCLR/SET.WAKEUP is 1. Write 1 to clear; a 0 does nothing.

fields.name: RST
fields.text: Set once the host has sent a bus reset to the device, and raises an interrupt when INTENCLR/SET.RST is 1. Write 1 to clear; a 0 does nothing.

fields.name: HSOF
fields.text: Set each time a full-speed SOF or low-speed keep-alive goes out (every 1 ms), when FNUM also updates; raises an interrupt when INTENCLR/SET.HSOF is 1. Write 1 to clear; a 0 does nothing.

fields.name: EPINT
fields.text: Bit n is set while pipe n has an interrupt pending (PINTFLAG) and clears when none is left; writes do nothing.

fields.name: PTYPE
fields.text: Pipe type; a USB reset sent by the host clears it.

fields.name: BK
fields.text: Number of banks for the pipe; must be 0 for control pipes, which use only bank 0 for SETUP, IN and OUT. Cleared when a USB reset is sent; ignored when PTYPE is EXTENDED.

fields.name: PTOKEN
fields.text: Pipe token: 0x0 SETUP (CONTROL pipes only), 0x1 IN, 0x2 OUT, 0x3 reserved. Ignored when PTYPE is EXTENDED; cleared when a USB reset is sent.

registers.name: BINTERVALn
registers.title: Interval for the Bulk-Out/Ping Transaction for Endpoint n

fields.name: BINTERVAL
fields.text: Ping / bulk-out period. At 0, OUT tokens repeat within one frame until acked; above 0, one OUT token goes every BINTERVAL frames until acked. Period by pipe type: interrupt, 1 to 255 ms; isochronous, 2^BINTERVAL times 1 ms; bulk and control, 1 to 255 ms; extended LPM ignores it and uses 1 ms after a NYET. A USB reset sent by the host, or PEN[n] at 0, clears it.

fields.name: BK1RDY
fields.text: Shows whether bank 1 is ready; a 1 written to the CLR register's BK1RDY clears it and one written to the SET register's BK1RDY sets it. Control pipes do not use bank 1.

values.text: Not ready: IN bank empty; Control/OUT bank not yet filled.
Ready: IN bank full; Control/OUT bank filled.

fields.name: BK0RDY
fields.text: Shows whether bank 0 is ready; a 1 written to the CLR register's BK0RDY clears it and one written to the SET register's BK0RDY sets it. Control pipes use only bank 0.

values.text: Not ready: IN bank not empty; Control/OUT bank not yet filled.
Ready: IN bank full; Control/OUT bank filled.

fields.name: PFREEZE
fields.text: Freezes the pipe; a 1 written to the CLR register's PFREEZE clears it and one written to the SET register's PFREEZE sets it. Hardware also sets it on a received STALL, when the pipe is enabled (PEN rises), when an LPM transaction ends with any handshake or times out, and when a transfer ends in a pipe error. Set mid-transaction, the transaction still completes, and it reads 1 only after that.

values.text: Pipe frozen: no further requests go to the device on this pipe.

fields.name: CURBK
fields.text: Shows which bank the next single or multi-packet transfer uses.

fields.name: DTGL
fields.text: Data toggle for the token type (IN/OUT/SETUP), flipped by hardware after each data transaction; a 1 written to the CLR register's DTGL clears it and one written to the SET register's DTGL sets it.

registers.name: PCKSIZE
registers.title: Packet Size
notes: The register's reset value is also given as 0xXXXXXXX.

fields.name: AUTO_ZLP
fields.text: Turns on hardware handling of the zero-length-packet handshake, for OUT pipes only; with it off, firmware handles the handshake.

fields.name: SIZE
fields.text: Pipe's packet size; sizes above 64 bytes are for isochronous pipes only. Cleared when a USB reset is sent.

fields.name: MULTI_PACKET_SIZE
fields.text: 14-bit byte count for multi-packet transfers. IN: total bytes sent, written 0 when a new transfer is set up. OUT: total size of the whole transfer, a multiple of the maximum packet size.

fields.name: BYTE_COUNT
fields.text: 14-bit byte count: on an OUT pipe, what the latest OUT or SETUP transaction carried; on an IN pipe, what the coming IN transaction should bring.

registers.name: EXTREG
registers.title: Extended Register
notes: The register's reset value is also given as 0xXXXXXXX.

fields.name: VARIABLE
fields.text: VARIABLE field sent with an extended (LPM) token. Bits 3:0 are bLinkState, 7:4 BESL, 8 bRemoteWake, 10:9 reserved, as the USB 2.0 LPM addendum defines them.

fields.name: SUBPID
fields.text: SUBPID field sent with an extended (LPM) token, set to a SubPID type from the USB 2.0 LPM addendum.

registers.name: STATUS_BK
registers.title: Host Status Bank
notes: The register's reset value is also given as 0xXXXXXXX.

fields.name: ERRORFLOW
fields.text: Set when a flow error occurred in a transfer to or from this bank: an IN or OUT transfer that received NAK, an isochronous IN overrun or an isochronous OUT underflow.

fields.name: CRCERR
fields.text: Set when a CRC error is found in an isochronous IN bank.

fields.name: PERMAX
fields.text: Number of errors the pipe allows before hardware freezes it.

fields.name: PEPNUM
fields.text: Endpoint number the pipe addresses.

fields.name: PDADDR
fields.text: Device address the pipe addresses.

registers.name: STATUS_PIPE
registers.title: Host Status Pipe
notes: The register's reset value is also given as 0xXXXXXXX.

fields.name: ERCNT
fields.text: Count of errors seen on the pipe.

fields.name: CRC16ER
fields.text: Set when a CRC16 error is found in an IN transaction.

fields.name: TOUTER
fields.text: Set when a USB transaction times out.

fields.name: PIDER
fields.text: Set when a PID error is found in a USB transaction.

fields.name: DAPIDER
fields.text: Set when a data PID error is found in a USB transaction.

fields.name: DTGLER
fields.text: Set when a data toggle error is found.

fields.name: REL
fields.text: Core release number, one BCD digit.

fields.name: STEP
fields.text: Step within the core release, one BCD digit.

fields.name: SUBSTEP
fields.text: Sub-step within the core release, one BCD digit.

fields.name: ETV
fields.text: Endianness test value; reads as 0x87654321.

fields.name: QOS
fields.text: Priority the CAN asks for when it reads or writes data in the Message RAM.

registers.name: DBTP
registers.title: Data Bit Timing and Prescaler
notes: Writable only while CCCR.CCE and CCCR.INIT are both 1.
Bit time ranges from 4 to 49 tq; one tq ranges from 1 to 32 GCLK_CAN periods, tq = (DBRP + 1) mtq.
At GCLK_CAN = 8 MHz the reset value 0x00000A33 gives a 500 kbit/s data-phase rate.
The data-phase rate set here must be at least the arbitration-phase rate set in NBTP.

fields.name: TDC
fields.text: Turns transceiver delay compensation on or off.

fields.name: DBRP
fields.text: Data-phase prescaler: GCLK_CAN is divided by DBRP + 1 to make the time quantum the bit time is counted in; 0 to 31.

fields.name: DTSEG1
fields.text: Data-phase time before the sample point (Prop_Seg plus Phase_Seg1), DTSEG1 + 1 tq; 0 to 31.

fields.name: DTSEG2
fields.text: Data-phase time after the sample point (Phase_Seg2), DTSEG2 + 1 tq; 0 to 15.

fields.name: DSJW
fields.text: Data-phase resynchronization jump width, DSJW + 1 tq; 0 to 15.

fields.name: RX
fields.text: Reads the live level on CAN_RX.

fields.name: TX
fields.text: Selects what drives the CAN_TX pin.

values.name: CORE
values.text: The CAN core drives CAN_TX, changing at the end of each bit time; reset setting.

fields.name: LBCK
fields.text: Turns loop back mode on or off.

registers.name: RWD
registers.title: RAM Watchdog
notes: Writable only while CCCR.CCE and CCCR.INIT are both 1.
The watchdog watches the Message RAM READY output: each Message RAM access through the AHB host interface loads the counter with RWD.WDC, and READY reloads it.
If READY does not come before the counter reaches zero, the counter stops and IR.WDI is set.

fields.name: WDV
fields.text: Present count of the Message RAM watchdog.

fields.name: WDC
fields.text: Value the Message RAM watchdog counter starts from; 0x00, the reset value, turns the counter off.

fields.name: TXP
fields.text: Transmit pause. Writable only while CCE and INIT are both 1.

values.text: After each frame it sends successfully, the CAN waits two bit times before its next transmission.

fields.name: EFBI
fields.text: Edge filtering while integrating onto the bus.

values.text: An edge for hard synchronization needs two dominant tq in a row.

fields.name: PXHD
fields.text: Turns protocol exception handling off; with it off, a protocol exception makes the CAN send an error frame.

fields.name: BRSE
fields.text: Lets transmissions switch bit rate; ignored while FDOE is 0.

values.text: No bit rate switching on transmit.

fields.name: FDOE
fields.text: Turns CAN FD operation on or off.

fields.name: TEST
fields.text: Test mode. A 0 can always be written; a 1 only while CCE and INIT are both 1.

values.text: Normal operation; TEST stays at its reset values.
Test mode; TEST can be written.

fields.name: DAR
fields.text: Turns automatic retransmission off. Writable only while CCE and INIT are both 1.

values.text: Frames that fail are sent again automatically.

fields.name: MON
fields.text: Bus monitoring mode. A 0 can always be written; a 1 only while CCE and INIT are both 1.

fields.name: CSR
fields.text: Asks the CAN to stop its clocks.

values.text: Request: once pending transfers finish and the bus is idle, INIT is set and then CSA.

fields.name: CSA
fields.text: Shows the clock stop request has been granted.

values.text: CLK_CANx_AHB and GCLK_CAN may be stopped to power the CAN down.

fields.name: ASM
fields.text: Restricted operation mode. A 0 can always be written; a 1 only while CCE and INIT are both 1.

fields.name: CCE
fields.text: Opens the protected configuration registers to CPU writes; writable only while INIT is 1.

values.text: Protected registers writable while INIT is 1.

fields.name: INIT
fields.text: Starts initialization. A written value crosses clock domains and may take time to read back; read INIT to confirm the last write took before writing it again.

registers.name: NBTP
registers.title: Nominal Bit Timing and Prescaler
notes: Writable only while CCCR.CCE and CCCR.INIT are both 1.
Bit time ranges from 4 to 385 tq; one tq ranges from 1 to 512 GCLK_CAN periods, tq = (NBRP + 1) mtq.
Bit length is NTSEG1 + NTSEG2 + 3 tq in programmed values, or Sync_Seg + Prop_Seg + Phase_Seg1 + Phase_Seg2 in functional terms.
Information processing time is zero: data for the next bit is ready on the clock edge right after sampling.
At GCLK_CAN = 8 MHz the reset value 0x06000A03 gives 500 kbit/s.

fields.name: NSJW
fields.text: Arbitration-phase resynchronization jump width, NSJW + 1 tq; 0 to 127.

fields.name: NBRP
fields.text: Arbitration-phase prescaler: GCLK_CAN is divided by NBRP + 1 to make the time quantum; 0 to 511.

fields.name: NTSEG1
fields.text: Arbitration-phase time before the sample point (Prop_Seg plus Phase_Seg1), NTSEG1 + 1 tq; 1 to 255.

fields.name: NTSEG2
fields.text: Arbitration-phase time after the sample point (Phase_Seg2), NTSEG2 + 1 tq; 0 to 127.

registers.name: TSCC
registers.title: Timestamp Counter Configuration
notes: Writable only while CCCR.CCE and CCCR.INIT are both 1.

fields.name: TCP
fields.text: Unit of the timestamp and timeout counters, TCP + 1 CAN bit times (1 to 16).

values.text: TCP + 1 CAN bit times per counter step.

fields.name: TSS
fields.text: Picks the timestamp counter source.

values.name: INC
values.text: Counter counts in steps set by TCP.

registers.name: TSCV
registers.title: Timestamp Counter Value
notes: A write to TSCV clears the counter in internal mode and does nothing in external mode.
A wrap around is the counter going from non-zero to zero other than by a write to TSCV.

fields.name: TSC
fields.text: Timestamp counter, captured at start of frame on receive and transmit. With TSCC.TSS = 0x1 it counts in units of 1 to 16 bit times set by TSCC.TCP; wrapping sets IR.TSW.

registers.name: TOCC
registers.title: Timeout Counter Configuration
notes: Writable only while CCCR.CCE and CCCR.INIT are both 1.

fields.name: TOP
fields.text: Timeout period: the value the timeout down-counter starts from.

fields.name: TOS
fields.text: Picks what runs the timeout counter. Continuous: a write to TOCV loads TOCC.TOP and counting goes on. FIFO-run: an empty FIFO loads TOCC.TOP and counting starts when the first element is stored.

values.name: TXEF
values.text: Run by the Tx Event FIFO.

fields.name: ETOC
fields.text: Turns the timeout counter on or off.

registers.name: TOCV
registers.title: Timeout Counter Value
notes: Writing TOCV reloads the counter from TOCC.TOP.

fields.name: TOC
fields.text: Timeout counter, counting down in units of 1 to 16 bit times set by TSCC.TCP; at zero it stops and sets IR.TOO. TOCC.TOS sets how it starts and restarts.

registers.name: ECR
registers.title: Error Counter
notes: While CCCR.ASM is 1, protocol errors do not raise TEC or REC, but CEL still counts.

fields.name: CEL
fields.text: Counts protocol errors that raise TEC or REC; reading CEL clears it. It holds at 0xFF, and the next TEC or REC increase sets IR.ELO.

fields.name: RP
fields.text: Receive error passive.

fields.name: REC
fields.text: Present receive error count, 0 to 127.

fields.name: TEC
fields.text: Present transmit error count, 0 to 255.

registers.name: PSR
registers.title: Protocol Status
notes: After a CAN FD frame with BRS set reaches its data phase, the next error or good frame shows in DLEC, not LEC.
A bad fixed stuff bit in a CAN FD CRC sequence is reported as a form error, not a stuff error.
Setting or clearing CCCR.INIT does not shorten Bus_Off recovery. On Bus_Off the CAN sets CCCR.INIT itself and stops bus activity.
Once the CPU clears CCCR.INIT, the CAN waits for 129 bus idle periods of 11 recessive bits each, then resumes and resets its error counters.

During that wait each run of 11 recessive bits writes a Bit0 error code to PSR.LEC and is counted in ECR.REC, so the CPU can follow the recovery and tell whether the bus is stuck dominant or disturbed.

fields.name: TDCV
fields.text: Secondary sample point position in the data phase: measured CAN_TX to CAN_RX delay plus TDCR.TDCO, in mtq from the start of the sent bit; 0 to 127 mtq.

fields.name: PXE
fields.text: Protocol exception event flag; reading clears it.

values.text: No protocol exception since the last read.

fields.name: RFDF
fields.text: Set when a CAN FD frame arrives; reading clears it.

values.text: No CAN FD frame since the CPU last cleared this bit.
A frame with FDF set arrived, whether or not filtering accepted it.

fields.name: RBRS
fields.text: BRS flag of the latest CAN FD frame received; reading clears it.

values.text: BRS was set; set along with RFDF, regardless of filtering.

fields.name: RESI
fields.text: ESI flag of the latest CAN FD frame received; reading clears it.

fields.name: DLEC
fields.text: Last error type seen in the data phase of CAN FD frames that have BRS set, coded as LEC; cleared to 0 when such a frame is sent or received without error.

fields.name: BO
fields.text: Bus_Off state.

fields.name: EW
fields.text: Error warning state.

values.text: One or both error counters at 96 or more.

fields.name: EP
fields.text: Error passive state.

values.text: Error_Active: the node joins in bus traffic as usual and sends an active error flag on errors.

fields.name: ACT
fields.text: What the node is doing on the bus.

fields.name: LEC
fields.text: Type of the latest error on the bus; cleared to 0 when a frame is sent or received without error, and set to 7 by a read of PSR.

values.name: NONE
values.text: No error since a good frame last reset LEC.

values.name: STUFF
values.text: Stuff error: more than five like bits in a row where the frame forbids it.

values.name: FORM
values.text: Form error: a received frame had a malformed fixed-format field.

values.name: ACK
values.text: Ack error: no other node acknowledged a frame the CAN sent.

values.name: BIT1
values.text: Bit1 error: sending a recessive bit outside the arbitration field, the CAN saw the bus dominant.

values.name: BIT0
values.text: Bit0 error: sending a dominant bit (data, identifier, acknowledge, active error flag or overload flag), the CAN saw the bus recessive. During Bus_Off recovery it is also set at each run of 11 recessive bits, so the CPU can follow the recovery.

values.name: CRC
values.text: CRC error: a received frame's CRC did not match the one worked out from its data.

values.name: NC
values.text: No change: every read of PSR sets LEC to 7; 7 means no bus event since the last CPU read.

registers.name: TDCR
registers.title: Transmitter Delay Compensation
notes: Writable only while CCCR.CCE and CCCR.INIT are both 1.

fields.name: TDCO
fields.text: Offset from the measured CAN_TX to CAN_RX delay to the secondary sample point; 0 to 127 mtq.

fields.name: TDCF
fields.text: Filter window: the earliest allowed secondary sample point position; dominant CAN_RX edges that would put it earlier are left out of the delay measurement. Active when TDCF is above TDCO; 0 to 127 mtq.

registers.name: IR
registers.title: Interrupt
notes: Each flag sets on the edge of its condition. Writing 1 clears a flag; writing 0 does nothing. A hard reset clears the register.

fields.name: ARA
fields.text: Set on an access to a reserved address.

fields.name: PED
fields.text: Set on a protocol error in the data phase.

values.text: Protocol error in the data phase: PSR.DLEC is neither 0 nor 7.

fields.name: PEA
fields.text: Set on a protocol error in the arbitration phase.

values.text: Protocol error in the arbitration phase: PSR.LEC is neither 0 nor 7.

fields.name: WDI
fields.text: Set on a Message RAM watchdog event.

values.text: Watchdog event: READY did not come.

fields.name: BO
fields.text: Set when the Bus_Off state changes.

fields.name: EW
fields.text: Set when the error warning state changes.

fields.name: EP
fields.text: Set when the error passive state changes.

fields.name: ELO
fields.text: Set when the error logging counter overflows.

fields.name: BEU
fields.text: Set when external parity or ECC logic on the Message RAM, if fitted, finds a bit error it cannot correct; this also sets CCCR.INIT so corrupt data is not sent.

values.text: No bit error on Message RAM reads.
Uncorrected bit error found, such as by parity logic.

fields.name: BEC
fields.text: Set when external parity or ECC logic on the Message RAM, if fitted, finds and corrects a bit error.

values.text: No bit error on Message RAM reads.
Corrected bit error found, such as by ECC.

fields.name: DRX
fields.text: Set each time a received frame is written to a dedicated Rx Buffer.

values.text: One or more received frames written to an Rx Buffer.

fields.name: TOO
fields.text: Set when the timeout counter runs out.

fields.name: MRAF
fields.text: Message RAM access failure. Set when the Rx Handler did not finish filtering or storing a frame before the next frame's arbitration field arrived (that work is dropped and the next frame handled), or could not write a frame to the Message RAM (storing is dropped). Either way the FIFO put index or the buffer's New Data flag is left alone, and a part-stored frame is overwritten by the next one stored there. Also set when the Tx Handler could not read a frame from the Message RAM in time: that transmission is dropped and the CAN enters restricted operation mode, left only when the CPU clears CCCR.ASM.

fields.name: TSW
fields.text: Set when the timestamp counter wraps.

fields.name: TEFL
fields.text: Set when a Tx Event FIFO element is lost.

values.text: An element was lost; also set by a write to a Tx Event FIFO of size zero.

fields.name: TEFF
fields.text: Set when the Tx Event FIFO fills.

fields.name: TEFW
fields.text: Set when the Tx Event FIFO reaches its watermark.

fields.name: TEFN
fields.text: Set when a Tx Event FIFO element is written.

values.text: The Tx Handler wrote an element.

fields.name: TFE
fields.text: Set when the Tx FIFO empties.

fields.name: TCF
fields.text: Set when a transmission cancellation finishes.

fields.name: TC
fields.text: Set when a transmission completes.

fields.name: HPM
fields.text: Set when a high priority message arrives.

fields.name: RF1L
fields.text: Set when a message for Rx FIFO 1 is lost.

values.text: A message was lost; also set by a write to an Rx FIFO 1 of size zero.

fields.name: RF1F
fields.text: Set when Rx FIFO 1 fills.

fields.name: RF1W
fields.text: Set when Rx FIFO 1 reaches its watermark.

fields.name: RF1N
fields.text: Set when a new message is written to Rx FIFO 1.

fields.name: RF0L
fields.text: Set when a message for Rx FIFO 0 is lost.

values.text: A message was lost; also set by a write to an Rx FIFO 0 of size zero.

fields.name: RF0F
fields.text: Set when Rx FIFO 0 fills.

fields.name: RF0W
fields.text: Set when Rx FIFO 0 reaches its watermark.

fields.name: RF0N
fields.text: Set when a new message is written to Rx FIFO 0.

registers.name: IE
registers.title: Interrupt Enable
notes: Each bit lets the matching IR flag raise an interrupt line.

fields.text: Lets IR.ARA (access to a reserved address) raise an interrupt.

fields.name: BOE

fields.text: Lets IR.TC (transmission complete) raise an interrupt.

fields.name: HPME
fields.text: Lets IR.HPM (high priority message) raise an interrupt.

fields.name: RF1LE

fields.name: EINTn
fields.text: One bit per CAN interrupt line (bit 0 for line 0, bit 1 for line 1) to turn that line on.

registers.name: GFC
registers.title: Global Filter Configuration
notes: Writable only while CCCR.CCE and CCCR.INIT are both 1.

fields.name: ANFS
fields.text: What happens to a received 11-bit ID frame that matches no filter element.

fields.name: ANFE
fields.text: What happens to a received 29-bit ID frame that matches no filter element.

fields.name: RRFS
fields.text: Rejects every remote frame with an 11-bit ID.

values.text: Remote frames go through the filters.

fields.name: RRFE
fields.text: Rejects every remote frame with a 29-bit ID.

values.text: Remote frames go through the filters.

registers.name: SIDFC
registers.title: Standard ID Filter Configuration
notes: Writable only while CCCR.CCE and CCCR.INIT are both 1.

fields.name: LSS
fields.text: Number of standard ID filter elements; anything above 128 counts as 128.

values.text: That many standard ID filter elements.

fields.name: FLSSA
fields.text: Where the standard ID filter list starts. The CAN reaches the Message RAM in 32-bit words, so this is a word address: bits 1:0 are ignored and read back as 0; only bits 15:2 count.

fields.name: LSE
fields.text: Number of extended ID filter elements; anything above 64 counts as 64.

values.text: That many extended ID filter elements.

fields.name: FLESA
fields.text: Where the extended ID filter list starts. The CAN reaches the Message RAM in 32-bit words, so this is a word address: bits 1:0 are ignored and read back as 0; only bits 15:2 count.

registers.name: XIDAM
registers.title: Extended ID AND Mask
notes: Writable only while CCCR.CCE and CCCR.INIT are both 1.

fields.name: EIDM
fields.text: ANDed with a received extended frame's ID before filtering, meant for masking 29-bit SAE J1939 IDs. All ones, the reset value, leaves the ID untouched.

registers.name: HPMS
registers.title: High Priority Message Status
notes: Refreshed each time a filter element set to raise a priority event matches, giving status of and quick access to high priority frames.

fields.name: FLST
fields.text: Which list the matching filter element is in.

fields.name: FIDX
fields.text: Index of the matching filter element: 0 to SIDFC.LSS - 1 for standard, 0 to XIDFC.LSE - 1 for extended.

fields.name: MSI
fields.text: Where the frame was put.

fields.name: BIDX
fields.text: Rx FIFO element the frame went into; meaningful only while MSI[1] is 1.

fields.name: NDn

fields.name: F0OM
fields.text: Rx FIFO 0 mode: blocking or overwrite.

fields.name: F0WM
fields.text: Fill level that raises IR.RF0W; above 64 the watermark interrupt is off.

fields.name: F0S

fields.name: F0SA
fields.text: Where Rx FIFO 0 starts in the Message RAM. The CAN reaches the Message RAM in 32-bit words, so this is a word address: bits 1:0 are ignored and read back as 0; only bits 15:2 count.

fields.name: RF0L
fields.text: Mirror of IR.RF0L, cleared with it. Overwriting the oldest message while RXF0C.F0OM is 1 does not set it.

values.text: A message was lost; also set by a write to an Rx FIFO 0 of size zero.

fields.name: F0AI

fields.name: F0DS

TFQS plus NDTB must not exceed 32; nothing checks for a bad setting.
The Tx Buffers section of the Message RAM begins with the dedicated Tx Buffers.

fields.name: TFQM
fields.text: Tx FIFO or Tx Queue.

fields.name: TFQS

values.text: That many Tx Buffers in the Tx FIFO or Queue.

fields.name: NDTB
fields.text: Number of dedicated Tx Buffers; anything above 32 counts as 32.

fields.name: TBSA
fields.text: Where the Tx Buffers section starts in the Message RAM. The CAN reaches the Message RAM in 32-bit words, so this is a word address: bits 1:0 are ignored and read back as 0; only bits 15:2 count.

registers.name: TXFQS
registers.title: Tx FIFO/Queue Status
notes: With dedicated Tx Buffers and a Tx FIFO or Queue together, the put and get indexes count Tx Buffers from the first dedicated one: with 12 dedicated buffers and a 20-buffer FIFO, put index 15 is the FIFO's fourth buffer.

fields.name: TFQF
fields.text: Tx FIFO or Queue is full.

fields.name: TFQPI
fields.text: Tx FIFO or Queue write pointer, 0 to 31.

fields.name: TFGI
fields.text: Tx FIFO read pointer, 0 to 31; reads 0 in queue mode (TXBC.TFQM = 1).

fields.name: TFFL
fields.text: Free Tx FIFO elements in a row from TFGI, 0 to 32; reads 0 in queue mode (TXBC.TFQM = 1).

registers.name: TXESC
registers.title: Tx Buffer Element Size Configuration
notes: Writable only while CCCR.CCE and CCCR.INIT are both 1.
Sets how many data bytes a Tx Buffer element holds. Sizes above 8 bytes are meant only for CAN FD.

fields.name: TBDS
fields.text: Data bytes per Tx Buffer element; when an element's DLC asks for more bytes than this, the extra bytes go out as padding 0xCC.

registers.name: TXBRP
registers.title: Tx Buffer Request Pending
notes: A TXBRP bit set during a Tx scan is left out of that scan; if that buffer is then cancelled, its add request is dropped at once and the TXBRP bit cleared.

fields.name: TRPn
fields.text: One pending-request bit per Tx Buffer, set only for buffers TXBC configures. Setting one starts a Tx scan for the highest-priority request (lowest Message ID). A bit clears when its transmission completes or is cancelled through TXBCR; a cancel during a transmission takes effect when it ends, successful or not, and the TXBCR bit clears right after. A finished cancellation shows in TXBCF after a good transmission (with its TXBTO bit), when transmission had not started, on lost arbitration, or on a transmit error. With DAR set every unsuccessful transmission is cancelled and its TXBCF bit set.

registers.name: TXBAR
registers.title: Tx Buffer Add Request
notes: An add request for a buffer whose TXBRP bit is already set is ignored.

fields.name: ARn
fields.text: One add-request bit per Tx Buffer: writing 1 sets it, 0 does nothing, so one write can queue several buffers. Set only for buffers TXBC configures. The bits clear at once if no Tx scan is running, otherwise when the scan ends.

fields.name: CRn
fields.text: One cancel-request bit per Tx Buffer: writing 1 sets it, 0 does nothing, so one write can cancel several buffers. Set only for buffers TXBC configures; each stays set until its TXBRP bit clears.

fields.name: TOn
fields.text: One bit per Tx Buffer, set when its TXBRP bit clears after a good transmission and cleared when a 1 written to TXBAR requests a new one.

fields.name: CFn
fields.text: One bit per Tx Buffer, set when its TXBRP bit clears after a cancel through TXBCR, or at once if TXBRP was not set when cancelled; cleared when a 1 written to TXBAR requests a new transmission.

fields.name: TIEn
fields.text: One transmission interrupt enable per Tx Buffer.

registers.name: TXBCIE
registers.title: Tx Buffer Cancellation Finished Interrupt Enable

fields.name: CFIEn
fields.text: One cancellation-finished interrupt enable per Tx Buffer.

registers.name: TXEFC
registers.title: Tx Event FIFO Configuration
notes: Writable only while CCCR.CCE and CCCR.INIT are both 1.

fields.name: EFWM
fields.text: Fill level that raises IR.TEFW; above 32 the watermark interrupt is off.

fields.name: EFS
fields.text: Number of Tx Event FIFO elements, numbered 0 to EFS - 1; anything above 32 counts as 32.

values.text: That many Tx Event FIFO elements.

fields.name: EFSA
fields.text: Where the Tx Event FIFO starts in the Message RAM. The CAN reaches the Message RAM in 32-bit words, so this is a word address: bits 1:0 are ignored and read back as 0; only bits 15:2 count.

fields.name: TEFL
fields.text: Mirror of IR.TEFL, cleared with it.

values.text: An element was lost; also set by a write to a Tx Event FIFO of size zero.

fields.name: EFF
fields.text: Tx Event FIFO is full.

fields.name: EFPI
fields.text: Tx Event FIFO write pointer, 0 to 31.

fields.name: EFGI
fields.text: Tx Event FIFO read pointer, 0 to 31.

fields.name: EFFL
fields.text: How many elements the Tx Event FIFO holds, 0 to 32.

fields.name: EFAI
fields.text: After reading one or more elements from the Tx Event FIFO, the host writes the index of the last one read here; TXEFS.EFGI becomes EFAI + 1 and TXEFS.EFFL is updated.

fields.name: ADDR
fields.text: In an SDMA transfer, the system memory address; after the SDMA transfer stops it holds the address of the next contiguous data, and writing the next address restarts the transfer. Access it only while no transaction runs; reads during a transfer can be invalid; an interrupt can ask software to update it. With Auto CMD23 it holds the 32-bit block count sent as the CMD23 argument: the full 32 bits with ADMA, limited by BCR (65535 blocks at most) without ADMA.

fields.name: BOUNDARY
fields.text: Size of the contiguous SDMA buffer in system memory: the SDMA transfer pauses at each such boundary and the DMA interrupt asks software to update SSAR. At 0 (4 Kbytes) the low 12 bits of SSAR address data inside the buffer and the upper 20 bits locate the buffer. Active only while TMR.DMAEN is 1.

fields.name: BLKSIZE
fields.text: Block size of data transfers for CMD17, CMD18, CMD24, CMD25 and CMD53, from 1 to 512. Access it only while no transaction runs: during a transfer, reads can be invalid and writes are ignored.

fields.name: BLKCNT
fields.text: Number of blocks to transfer, 1 up to the maximum block count; used only when TMR.BCEN is 1 and only for multiple-block transfers. The peripheral counts it down after each block and stops at 0; at 0 no block is transferred. Access it only while no transaction runs: during a transfer reads can be invalid and writes are ignored. After a suspend command completes it reads the blocks still to transfer; the saved count is written back before a resume command.

fields.name: ARG1
fields.text: The SD command argument, bits 39 to 8 of the command format of the SD Physical Layer or e.MMC 4.51 standard.

registers.name: TMR
registers.title: Transfer Mode Register
notes: Set before sending a command that transfers data (CR.DPSEL) or a Resume command; saved on Suspend and restored before Resume. Not writable while a data transaction runs; writes are ignored while PSR.CMDINHD is 1.
Transfer type: MSBSEL 0, single transfer; MSBSEL 1 with BCEN 0, infinite transfer; MSBSEL 1, BCEN 1, BLKCNT non-zero, multiple transfer; MSBSEL 1, BCEN 1, BLKCNT 0, multiple transfer stopped.

fields.name: MSBSEL
fields.text: Write 1 for multiple-block transfer commands on the DAT lines and 0 for every other command. At 0, BCR need not be written.

fields.name: DTDSEL
fields.text: Direction of DAT line data: 1 moves data from the card or device to the peripheral; 0 for all other commands.

fields.name: ACMDEN
fields.text: Selects an automatic command for ending multiple-block reads and writes. At 1 (Auto CMD12) the peripheral sends CMD12 after the last block, only if the command needs it; errors go to ACESR. At 2 (Auto CMD23) the peripheral sends CMD23 before the command written to CR, with SSAR as its 32-bit block count argument, and skips the second command if the CMD23 response has errors (reported in ACESR). Auto CMD23 needs a card supporting CMD23 (SCR[33] = 1), ADMA rather than SDMA if DMA is used, and only CMD18 or CMD25; the command index is not checked.

fields.name: BCEN
fields.text: Enables BCR, which matters only for multiple-block transfers; 0 disables it, for an infinite transfer. For an ADMA2 transfer of more than 65535 blocks this bit is 0 and the descriptor table gives the length.

fields.name: DMAEN
fields.text: Enables DMA, possible only when CA0R.ADMA2SUP shows it is supported; HC1R.DMASEL picks the DMA mode. Without DMA support it has no meaning and reads 0. When 1, a DMA operation starts on a write to the upper byte of CR.

fields.name: CMDIDX
fields.text: Command number (CMD0 to CMD63, ACMD0 to ACMD63), as in bits 45 to 40 of the SD, SDIO or e.MMC command format.

fields.name: CMDTYP
fields.text: Command Type: the kind of command sent.

values.name: SUSPEND
values.text: SDIO CMD52 writing Bus Suspend in the CCCR.

values.name: RESUME
values.text: SDIO CMD52 writing Function Select in the CCCR.

values.name: ABORT
values.text: CMD12, or SDIO CMD52 writing I/O Abort in the CCCR.

fields.name: DPSEL
fields.text: 1 when the command carries data on the DAT lines. 0 for commands on the CMD line only (such as CMD52), commands without data that use busy on DAT[0] (such as CMD38), and the resume command.

fields.name: CMDICEN
fields.text: When 1, the peripheral compares the response's index field with the command index and flags a mismatch as EISTR.CMDIDX; when 0, the index is not checked.

fields.name: CMDCCEN
fields.text: When 1, the peripheral checks the response's CRC field, placed according to the response length, and flags an error as EISTR.CMDCRC; when 0, the CRC is not checked.

fields.name: RESPTYP
fields.text: Response type expected for the command in CMDIDX.

registers.name: RR
registers.title: Response Register n
notes: The register's reset value is also given as 0x000000000.

fields.name: CMDRESP
fields.text: Command response. R1/R1b normal card status: R[39:8] in RR0. R1b Auto CMD12 and R1 Auto CMD23 card status: R[39:8] in RR3. R2 (CID or CSD): R[127:8] in RR0, RR1, RR2 and RR3[23:0]. R3 (memory OCR), R4 (I/O OCR), R5/R5b (SDIO) and R6 (published RCA and card status): R[39:8] in RR0. R[] is a bit range of the response as sent on the bus.

fields.name: BUFDATA
fields.text: 32-bit port to the peripheral's data buffer.

fields.name: CMDLL
fields.text: Level of the CMD line, for error recovery and debugging.

fields.name: DATLL
fields.text: Levels of DAT[3:0], for error recovery and debugging, such as reading the busy level on DAT[0].

fields.name: WRPPL
fields.text: Level of the WP pin, for memory and combo cards.

fields.name: CARDDPL
fields.text: Inverse of the CD pin, not debounced; may be valid while CARDSS is 1 but not guaranteed, because of propagation delay. For testing only, as software must debounce it.

fields.name: CARDSS
fields.text: For testing: 1 when CARDDPL is stable, 0 when it is not. CARDSS 1 with CARDINS 0 means no card. SRR.SWRSTALL does not affect it.

values.text: Stable: no card or card inserted.

fields.name: CARDINS
fields.text: Debounced card-present state. A 0-to-1 change sets NISTR.CINS when NISTER.CINS is 1 (interrupt when NISIER.CINS is 1); a 1-to-0 change sets NISTR.CREM when NISTER.CREM is 1 (interrupt when NISIER.CREM is 1). SRR.SWRSTALL does not affect it.

fields.name: BUFRDEN
fields.text: For non-DMA reads: 1 while readable data is in the buffer. It falls when all block data has been read and rises when block data is ready, which sets NISTR.BRDRDY when NISTER.BRDRDY is 1 (interrupt when NISIER.BRDRDY is 1).

fields.name: BUFWREN
fields.text: For non-DMA writes: 1 while the buffer has room for write data. It falls when all block data has been written and rises when the start of block data can be written, which sets NISTR.BWRRDY when NISTER.BWRRDY is 1 (interrupt when NISIER.BWRRDY is 1).

fields.name: RTACT
fields.text: 1 while a read transfer is active. Set after the end bit of a read command, or when a read restarts through BGCR.CONTR. Cleared when the last block of BLKSIZE has gone to the system (for ADMA2, the descriptor table marks the end), or when all valid blocks are transferred and none is in progress after BGCR.STPBGR. A 1-to-0 change sets NISTR.TRFC when NISTER.TRFC is 1 (interrupt when NISIER.TRFC is 1).

fields.name: WTACT
fields.text: 1 while a write transfer is active; 0 means no valid write data is held. Set after the end bit of a write command, or when a write restarts through BGCR.CONTR. Cleared after the CRC status of the last block of the transfer count (for ADMA2, from the descriptor table), or of a block where BGCR.STPBGR stops the transfer. During a write stopped by STPBGR, a 1-to-0 change sets NISTR.BLKGE when NISTER.BLKGE is 1 (interrupt when NISIER.BLKGE is 1). Shows whether commands not using DAT can be sent during write busy.

fields.name: RTREQ
fields.text: Set when the peripheral asks software to re-tune because temperature drift moved the data window and the tuned sampling point lost margin. Cleared when a command is sent by setting HC2R.EXTUN. A 0-to-1 change sets NISTR.RTEVT when NISTER.RTEVT is 1 (interrupt when NISIER.RTEVT is 1). Never set while HC2R.SCLKSEL is 0 (fixed sampling clock).

fields.name: DLACT
fields.text: 1 while a DAT line is in use. Read: set after the read command's end bit or on BGCR.CONTR; cleared when the final block's end bit arrives (for ADMA2, the descriptor table's last transfer) or when a read stops at a block gap after BGCR.STPBGR, which sets NISTR.BLKGE when NISTER.BLKGE is 1 (interrupt when NISIER.BLKGE is 1). The read is held by driving Read Wait on DAT[2] or by stopping the SD clock; if Read Wait is already driven because the buffer is full, it stays driven to hold the read. Suspend/Resume needs Read Wait. Write: set after the write command's end bit or on BGCR.CONTR; cleared once the card ends its busy signal on the final block (no busy for 8 SDCLK counts as not busy; for ADMA2, the descriptor table's last transfer), or when the card ends busy ahead of a block-gap stop requested by BGCR.STPBGR. Command with busy: set after the command's end bit, cleared when busy ends. For writes and busy commands, a 1-to-0 change sets NISTR.TRFC when NISTER.TRFC is 1 (interrupt when NISIER.TRFC is 1).

fields.name: CMDINHD
fields.text: 1 when DLACT or RTACT is 1; 0 means the next command may be sent. Commands with busy (R1b, R5b) count here. A 1-to-0 change sets NISTR.TRFC when NISTER.TRFC is 1 (interrupt when NISIER.TRFC is 1). After it falls, software can save registers 0x000 to 0x00D for a suspend.

values.text: A command using DAT may be sent.
No command using DAT may be sent.

fields.name: CMDINHC
fields.text: 0 when the CMD line is free and a command may be sent on it. Set as soon as CR is written; cleared when the response arrives. With Auto CMD12 or Auto CMD23 it is cleared by the read/write command's response, not by the CMD12 or CMD23 response. It does not show that Auto CMD12 is being sent, so a command written during Auto CMD12 is sent as well as CMD12. While it is 0, CMD-only commands may be sent even if CMDINHD is 1. A 1-to-0 change sets NISTR.CMDC when NISTER.CMDC is 1 (interrupt when NISIER.CMDC is 1). On a command conflict (EISTR.CMDCRC) or a Command Not Issued by Auto CMD12 error it stays 1 and CMDC is not set.

values.text: A CMD-only command may be sent.

fields.name: CARDDSEL
fields.text: SD/SDIO mode only. Source of card detection.

fields.name: CARDDTL
fields.text: SD/SDIO mode only. While CARDDSEL is 1, gives the card-inserted state.

fields.name: DMASEL
fields.text: Selects the DMA mode; check CA0R for the supported modes. TMR.DMAEN decides whether DMA is used.

fields.name: HSEN
fields.text: Check CA0R.HSSUP before setting. At 0 (default) CMD and DAT are driven on the falling SD clock edge (up to 25 MHz); at 1 on the rising edge (up to 50 MHz). With HC2R.PVALEN 1, clear CCR.SDCLKEN before changing it to avoid clock glitches and set SDCLKEN again afterwards. Effective only while MC1R.DDR is 0; CCR divider DIV must be non-zero when HSEN is 1.

fields.name: DW
fields.text: Data width; must match the card. With the extended 8-bit width set it has no effect and the width is 8 bits.

fields.name: LEDCTRL
fields.text: SD/SDIO mode only. Signals that the card must not be removed while it is accessed; kept at 1 throughout a sequence of several commands.

fields.name: SDBVSEL
fields.text: Card bus voltage; check the voltage support in CA0R first. An unsupported voltage leaves the bus unpowered.

fields.name: SDBPWR
fields.text: Powers the SD bus. Cleared by the peripheral when the card is removed; when 0, CMD and DAT[7:0] are tri-stated and CK is driven low.

fields.name: INTBG
fields.text: SD/SDIO mode only, valid only in 4-bit mode of an SDIO card; picks the sample point in the interrupt cycle: 1 enables interrupt detection at the block gap of multiple-block transfers. Keep 0 when the card cannot signal an interrupt during such transfers. Software sets it from the SDIO card's CCCR on insertion.

fields.name: RWCTRL
fields.text: SD/SDIO mode only. 1 uses the Read Wait protocol on DAT[2] to hold read data; otherwise SDCLK is stopped, which restricts commands. Set from the SDIO card's CCCR on insertion; never 1 for a card without Read Wait, or DAT lines can conflict. At 0 Suspend/Resume is not supported.

fields.name: CONTR
fields.text: Write 1, with STPBGR at 0, to restart a transaction stopped at a block gap. Cleared by the peripheral when DLACT (read) or WTACT (write) rises as the transaction restarts, so it need not be cleared. Writes are ignored while STPBGR is 1.

fields.name: STPBGR
fields.text: 1 halts reads and writes at the coming block gap, in non-DMA, SDMA and ADMA modes alike; keep it 1 until NISTR.TRFC. Clearing both it and CONTR does not restart the transaction. Works with or without Read Wait: reads are held by Read Wait on DAT[2] if supported, otherwise by stopping the SD clock. For writes through BDPR, set it after all block data is written, and write no more to BDPR while it is 1. Affects PSR.RTACT, WTACT, DLACT and CMDINHD.

fields.name: WKENCREM
fields.text: Enables a wake-up event from NISTR.CREM; the card's FN_WUS in the CIS has no effect on it.

fields.name: WKENCINS
fields.text: Enables a wake-up event from NISTR.CINS; the card's FN_WUS in the CIS has no effect on it.

fields.name: WKENCINT
fields.text: Enables a wake-up event from NISTR.CINT; may be set to 1 only if FN_WUS in the SDIO card's CIS is 1.

fields.name: SDCLKFSEL
fields.text: Low 8 bits of the 10-bit SDCLK divider DIV (DIV[9:8] = USDCLKFSEL). With CLKGSEL 0: F_SDCLK = F_BASECLK / (2 x DIV), or F_BASECLK when DIV is 0. With CLKGSEL 1: F_SDCLK = F_MULTCLK / (DIV + 1). Written by the user when HC2R.PVALEN is 0, loaded from a PVR when it is 1.

fields.name: USDCLKFSEL
fields.text: Bits 9 and 8 of the SDCLK divider DIV, extending SDCLKFSEL to 10 bits.

fields.name: CLKGSEL
fields.text: Selects the SDCLK generator mode. Not writable and reads 0 when CA1R.CLKMULT is 0 (no programmable mode). Written by the user when HC2R.PVALEN is 0, loaded from a PVR when it is 1.

fields.name: SDCLKEN
fields.text: Writing 0 stops the SD clock; SDCLKFSEL may be changed while it is 0, and the clock keeps its old frequency until SDCLK stops. Cleared when PSR.CARDINS clears.

fields.name: INTCLKS
fields.text: Set when the clock is stable after INTCLKEN is set; wait for it before setting SDCLKEN.

fields.name: INTCLKEN
fields.text: 0 stops the internal clock for very low power while the peripheral is unused or waiting for a wake-up interrupt; registers stay readable and writable. Writing 1 starts the clock, and INTCLKS is set once it is stable. Card detection is not affected.

fields.name: DTCVAL
fields.text: Sets the DAT line timeout interval: TIMEOUT = 2^(DTCVAL + 13) / F_BASECLK (MHz), in microseconds; DTCVAL = 0xF is reserved. Timeouts are flagged in EISTR.DATTEO; clearing EISTER.DATTEO while writing this field avoids spurious timeouts.

fields.name: SWRSTDAT
fields.text: Writing 1 resets part of the data circuit and the DMA circuit, clearing BDPR.BUFDATA; PSR.BUFRDEN, BUFWREN, RTACT, WTACT, DLACT and CMDINHD; BGCR.CONTR and STPBGR; and NISTR.BRDRDY, BWRRDY, DMAINT, BLKGE and TRFC.

fields.name: SWRSTCMD
fields.text: Writing 1 resets part of the command circuit, clearing PSR.CMDINHC and NISTR.CMDC.

fields.name: SWRSTALL
fields.text: Writing 1 resets the whole peripheral except card detection; required during initialization. Clears itself once CA0R and CA1R are valid and readable. After it, send a reset command and reinitialize the card. Clears to 0: SSAR, BSR, BCR, ARG1R, TMR, CR, RR, BDPR, PSR (except CMDLL, DATLL, WRPPL, CARDDPL, CARDSS, CARDINS), HC1R, PCR, BGCR, WCR, CCR, TCR, NISTR, EISTR, NISTER, EISTER, NISIER, EISIER, ACESR, HC2R, AESR, ASAR, SISR, MC1R, MC2R, ACR, CC2R and CACR (except KEY).

fields.name: ERRINT
fields.text: Read-only; set when any EISTR bit is set, so one check shows an error.

fields.name: BOOTAR
fields.text: e.MMC mode only. Set when a boot acknowledge pattern is received from the e.MMC. Set only when NISTER.BOOTAR is 1; interrupts only when NISIER.BOOTAR is 1. Writing 1 clears it.

fields.name: CINT
fields.text: SD/SDIO mode only. Card interrupt; writing 1 does not clear it, clearing the card's interrupt source does. In 1-bit mode it is detected without SDCLK, for wake-up; in 4-bit mode it is sampled in the interrupt cycle, with some delay. To service it, NISTER.CINT may be cleared, which clears the latched status and stops the interrupt to the system, then set again after the card's interrupt sources are reset. DAT[1] detection works with one card per slot; on a shared bus, with SBCR.INTPSEL 0 this status applies, otherwise INT_A, INT_B or INT_C carry device interrupts. Set only when NISTER.CREM is 1; interrupts only when NISIER.CREM is 1.

fields.name: CREM
fields.text: SD/SDIO mode only. Set when PSR.CARDINS goes from 1 to 0. When clearing it, check PSR.CARDINS, as the detect state may change during the clear without an interrupt. Set only when NISTER.CREM is 1; interrupts only when NISIER.CREM is 1. Writing 1 clears it.

values.text: Card state unstable or card inserted.

fields.name: CINS
fields.text: SD/SDIO mode only. Set when PSR.CARDINS goes from 0 to 1. When clearing it, check PSR.CARDINS, as the detect state may change during the clear without an interrupt. Set only when NISTER.CINS is 1; interrupts only when NISIER.CINS is 1. Writing 1 clears it.

values.text: Card state unstable or card removed.

fields.name: BRDRDY
fields.text: Set when PSR.BUFRDEN goes from 0 to 1. Set only when NISTER.BRDRDY is 1; interrupts only when NISIER.BRDRDY is 1. Writing 1 clears it.

fields.name: BWRRDY
fields.text: Set when PSR.BUFWREN goes from 0 to 1. Set only when NISTER.BWRRDY is 1; interrupts only when NISIER.BWRRDY is 1. Writing 1 clears it.

fields.name: DMAINT
fields.text: Set when an SDMA transfer reaches the buffer boundary in BSR.BOUNDARY, or with ADMA when a descriptor line with its int field set completes; not set after TRFC. Set only when NISTER.DMAINT is 1; interrupts only when NISIER.DMAINT is 1. Writing 1 clears it.

fields.name: BLKGE
fields.text: Set when a read or write stops at a block gap, only while BGCR.STPBGR is 1: for a read on the falling edge of PSR.DLACT (needs Read Wait), for a write on the falling edge of PSR.WTACT after the CRC status. Set only when NISTER.BLKGE is 1; interrupts only when NISIER.BLKGE is 1. Writing 1 clears it.

values.text: Transaction stopped at a block gap.

fields.name: TRFC
fields.text: Set when a read or write transfer or a command with busy completes. Read: on the falling edge of PSR.RTACT, when the data length is done and read by the system, or when a stop at the block gap through BGCR.STPBGR finishes. Write: on the falling edge of PSR.DLACT, when the last data is written and busy released, or when a block-gap stop finishes with busy released. Command with busy: when busy ends. Set only when NISTER.TRFC is 1; interrupts only when NISIER.TRFC is 1. Writing 1 clears it. TRFC outranks EISTR.DATTEO: with both 1 the command has completed.

fields.name: CMDC
fields.text: Set at the end bit of a command response; with Auto CMD12 or Auto CMD23, by the read/write command's response, not the CMD12 or CMD23 one. Set only when NISTER.CMDC is 1; interrupts only when NISIER.CMDC is 1. Writing 1 clears it. EISTR.CMDTEO outranks CMDC: CMDTEO 1 (CMDC either) means no response within 64 SDCLK cycles; CMDC 1 with CMDTEO 0 means a response was received; both 0, interrupted by another factor.

fields.name: BOOTAE
fields.text: e.MMC mode only. Set when the e.MMC boot acknowledge status is not 010. Set only when EISTER.BOOTAE is 1; interrupts only when EISIER.BOOTAE is 1. Writing 1 clears it.

fields.name: ADMA
fields.text: Set on an error during an ADMA transfer, with the ADMA state saved in AESR; also set when an invalid descriptor (Valid = 0) is found in state ST_FDS, which AESR.ERRST shows. Set only when EISTER.ADMA is 1; interrupts only when EISIER.ADMA is 1. Writing 1 clears it.

fields.name: ACMD
fields.text: Shared by Auto CMD12 and Auto CMD23: set when any of ACESR[4:0] goes from 0 to 1. For Auto CMD12 it is also set when Auto CMD12 is not sent because of an earlier command error. Set only when EISTER.ACMD is 1; interrupts only when EISIER.ACMD is 1. Writing 1 clears it.

fields.name: CURLIM
fields.text: 1 when the peripheral has stopped powering the card, after PCR.SDBPWR requested power, because of a failure such as an illegal card; 0 when power is supplied without error. Detection may take some sampling time. Set only when EISTER.CURLIM is 1; interrupts only when EISIER.CURLIM is 1. Writing 1 clears it.

fields.name: DATEND
fields.text: Set when a 0 is found at the end bit of read data on DAT or of the CRC status. Set only when EISTER.DATEND is 1; interrupts only when EISIER.DATEND is 1. Writing 1 clears it.

fields.name: DATCRC
fields.text: Set on a CRC error in read data on DAT, or when the write CRC status is not 010. Set only when EISTER.DATCRC is 1; interrupts only when EISIER.DATCRC is 1. Writing 1 clears it.

fields.name: DATTEO
fields.text: Set on a busy timeout for an R1b or R5b response, a busy timeout after the write CRC status, a write CRC status timeout, or a read data timeout. Set only when EISTER.DATTEO is 1; interrupts only when EISIER.DATTEO is 1. Writing 1 clears it.

fields.name: CMDIDX
fields.text: Set on a command index error in the response. Set only when EISTER.CMDIDX is 1; interrupts only when EISIER.CMDIDX is 1. Writing 1 clears it.

fields.name: CMDEND
fields.text: Set when the end bit of a command response is 0. Set only when EISTER.CMDEND is 1; interrupts only when EISIER.CMDEND is 1. Writing 1 clears it.

fields.name: CMDCRC
fields.text: Set on a CRC error in a returned response while CMDTEO is 0, or on a CMD line conflict: the peripheral drove 1 but saw 0 at the next SDCLK edge, so it aborts the command and sets both this bit and CMDTEO. Set only when EISTER.CMDCRC is 1; interrupts only when EISIER.CMDCRC is 1. Writing 1 clears it. With CMDTEO: 0/0 no error, 0/1 response timeout, 1/0 response CRC error, 1/1 CMD line conflict.

fields.name: CMDTEO
fields.text: Set when no response arrives within 64 SDCLK cycles of the command's end bit; on a CMD line conflict it is set at once, together with CMDCRC, as the command is aborted. Set only when EISTER.CMDTEO is 1; interrupts only when EISIER.CMDTEO is 1. Writing 1 clears it. With CMDCRC: 0/0 no error, CMDTEO alone response timeout, CMDCRC alone response CRC error, both CMD line conflict.

registers.name: NISTER

fields.name: BOOTAR
fields.text: e.MMC mode only. Enables the NISTR.BOOTAR flag.

fields.name: CINT
fields.text: Enables the NISTR.CINT flag. At 0 the peripheral clears card interrupt requests to the system and stops card interrupt detection; 1 restarts it. Can be cleared before servicing the card interrupt and set again once the card's requests are cleared.

fields.name: CREM

fields.name: CINS

fields.name: CMDC

fields.name: ADMA

fields.name: CINT
fields.text: SD/SDIO mode only. Interrupt request from NISTR.CINT.

fields.name: CREM

fields.name: CINS

fields.text: Interrupt request from EISTR.ACMD.

fields.text: Interrupt request from EISTR.CURLIM.

fields.text: Interrupt request from EISTR.DATCRC.

fields.text: Interrupt request from EISTR.DATTEO.

fields.name: CMDEND

fields.name: CMDCRC

fields.name: CMDTEO
fields.text: Interrupt request from EISTR.CMDTEO.

fields.name: CMDNI
fields.text: 1 when CMD_wo_DAT was not sent because of an Auto CMD12 error (ACESR[4:1]); 0 when the Auto CMD error came from Auto CMD23.

fields.name: ACMDIDX
fields.text: Set on a command index error in the auto command's response.

fields.name: ACMDEND
fields.text: Set when the end bit of the auto command's response is 0.

fields.name: ACMDCRC
fields.text: Set on a CRC error in the auto command's response. With ACMDTEO: 0/0 no error, ACMDTEO alone response timeout, ACMDCRC alone response CRC error, both CMD line conflict.

fields.name: ACMDTEO
fields.text: Set when no response arrives within 64 SDCLK cycles of the auto command's end bit; while 1, ACESR[4:2] have no meaning. With ACMDCRC: 0/0 no error, ACMDTEO alone response timeout, ACMDCRC alone response CRC error, both CMD line conflict.

fields.name: ACMD12NE
fields.text: 1 when an error prevents Auto CMD12 from stopping a memory multiple-block transfer; not set when the transfer never started because of a command error, as no Auto CMD12 is needed. While 1, ACESR[4:1] have no meaning. 0 when the Auto CMD error came from Auto CMD23.

registers.name: HC2R-EMMC
registers.title: Host Control 2 Register: e.MMC
notes: This layout applies in e.MMC mode; HC2R-DEFAULT applies in SD/SDIO mode.

fields.name: PVALEN
fields.text: 1 makes the peripheral set CCR.SDCLKFSEL, CCR.CLKGSEL and HC2R.DRVSEL from the PVR for automatic SDCLK frequency setting regardless of the system; 0 leaves CCR.CLKGSEL and CCR.SDCLKFSEL to the user.

fields.name: SCLKSEL
fields.text: Sampling clock for CMD and DAT, set by tuning and valid once EXTUN clears: 1 means tuning succeeded, 0 that it failed. Writing 1 is ignored; writing 0 resets the tuning circuit, and setting EXTUN also clears it. A reset tuning circuit takes time to tune again, so keeping it at 1 lets re-tuning finish quickly. Must not change while a response or read block is being received.

fields.name: EXTUN
fields.text: Write 1 to start tuning; clears itself when tuning ends, with the result in SCLKSEL. Writing 0 aborts tuning.

fields.name: DRVSEL
fields.text: Output driver strength for 1.8 V signaling; no effect at 3.3 V. Chosen according to which of driver types A, C and D CA1R reports as supported. Written by the user when PVALEN is 0, loaded from a PVR when it is 1.

fields.name: HS200EN
fields.text: 0xB enables e.MMC HS200 mode; values other than 0 and 0xB are forbidden with an e.MMC device. With PVALEN 1 it selects the PVR from which CCR.SDCLKFSEL, CCR.CLKGSEL and DRVSEL are loaded. Clear CCR.SDCLKEN before changing it to avoid a clock glitch, then set SDCLKEN again. Effective only while MC1R.DDR is 0.

registers.name: HC2R-DEFAULT
registers.title: Host Control 2 Register: SD/SDIO
notes: This layout applies in SD/SDIO mode; HC2R-EMMC applies in e.MMC mode.

fields.name: PVALEN
fields.text: 1 makes the peripheral set CCR.SDCLKFSEL, CCR.CLKGSEL and HC2R.DRVSEL from the PVR for automatic SDCLK frequency setting regardless of the system; 0 leaves CCR.CLKGSEL and CCR.SDCLKFSEL to the user.

fields.name: ASINTEN
fields.text: May be 1 only if the card supports asynchronous interrupts and CA0R.ASINTSUP is 1; applies to the DAT[1] interrupt in 4-bit SD mode. When 1, SDCLK may be stopped while an asynchronous interrupt is awaited, saving power, and the card interrupt is still passed on when the card asserts it.

fields.name: SCLKSEL
fields.text: Sampling clock for CMD and DAT, set by tuning and valid once EXTUN clears: 1 means tuning succeeded, 0 that it failed. Writing 1 is ignored; writing 0 resets the tuning circuit, and setting EXTUN also clears it. A reset tuning circuit takes time to tune again, so keeping it at 1 lets re-tuning finish quickly. Must not change while a response or read block is being received.

fields.name: EXTUN
fields.text: Write 1 to start tuning; clears itself when tuning ends, with the result in SCLKSEL. Writing 0 aborts tuning.

fields.name: DRVSEL
fields.text: Output driver strength for 1.8 V signaling; no effect at 3.3 V. Chosen according to which of driver types A, C and D CA1R reports as supported. Written by the user when PVALEN is 0, loaded from a PVR when it is 1.

fields.name: VS18EN
fields.text: Controls the I/O cell regulator; the card supply stays 3.3 V either way. 0 to 1 starts switching signaling from 3.3 V to 1.8 V, 1 to 0 back to 3.3 V; each regulator output must settle within 5 ms. May be set only when CA1R shows SDR50SUP, SDR104SUP or DDR50SUP and the card supports UHS-I (S18A = 1).

fields.name: UHSMS
fields.text: Selects the UHS-I mode; effective while VS18EN is 1. With PVALEN 1 it selects the PVR from which CCR.SDCLKFSEL, CCR.CLKGSEL and DRVSEL are loaded. Clear CCR.SDCLKEN before changing it to avoid a clock glitch, then set SDCLKEN again.

values.name: DDR50
values.text: DDR50; effective only while MC1R.DDR is 0.

registers.name: CA0R
registers.title: Capabilities 0 Register
notes: Not written by the user.

fields.name: SLTYPE
fields.text: Slot usage in the system; one register set per slot. 0 is a removable card, 1 a single non-removable device on the slot.

fields.name: ASINTSUP
fields.text: Asynchronous Interrupt Support (SDIO).

fields.name: SB64SUP
fields.text: Whether the 64-bit address descriptor mode is supported, with a 64-bit address system bus.

fields.name: V18VSUP
fields.text: 1.8 V supply support.

fields.name: V30VSUP
fields.text: 3.0 V supply support. Signal and supply voltages are limited by the device's supply voltage.

fields.name: V33VSUP
fields.text: 3.3 V supply support. Signal and supply voltages are limited by the device's supply voltage.

fields.name: SRSUP
fields.text: Whether Suspend/Resume is supported; at 0, Suspend and Resume commands are not sent.

fields.name: SDMASUP
fields.text: Whether SDMA can move data directly between system memory and the peripheral.

fields.name: HSSUP
fields.text: Whether the peripheral and system support high speed, with SDCLK from 25 MHz to 50 MHz.

fields.name: ADMA2SUP
fields.text: Whether ADMA2 can be used.

fields.name: ED8SUP
fields.text: Whether the 8-bit bus width can be used.

fields.name: MAXBLKL
fields.text: Largest block size that can be read and written to the peripheral's buffer. SD memory cards always use 512-byte blocks.

fields.name: BASECLKF
fields.text: Base clock (BASECLK) frequency in MHz, used to work out the SDCLK divider in CCR.SDCLKFSEL; at 0 it must be found another way. BASECLK is GCLK_SDHCx divided by 2.

fields.name: TEOCLKU
fields.text: Unit of the clock frequency used for data timeout detection.

fields.name: TEOCLKF
fields.text: Timeout clock (TEOCLK) frequency used for data timeout detection, in the unit set by TEOCLKU (kHz at 0, MHz at 1); at 0 it must be found another way.

registers.name: CA1R
registers.title: Capabilities 1 Register
notes: The register's reset value is also given as 0x00000070.
Not written by the user.

fields.name: CLKMULT
fields.text: Multiplier between BASECLK and MULTCLK: F_MULTCLK = F_BASECLK x (CLKMULT + 1). 0 means the programmable clock mode is not supported.

fields.name: TSDR50
fields.text: 1 when SDR50 needs tuning; SDR104 always needs it.

fields.name: TCNTRT
fields.text: Starting count of the re-tuning timer, used in CA1R.RTMODE 1 to 3: T = 2^(TCNTRT - 1) seconds, from 0 to 1024 s; 0 disables the timer.

fields.name: DRVDSUP
fields.text: Driver Type D Support.

fields.name: DRVCSUP
fields.text: Driver Type C Support.

fields.name: DRVASUP
fields.text: Driver Type A Support.

fields.name: DDR50SUP
fields.text: DDR50 Support.

fields.name: SDR104SUP
fields.text: SDR104 Support.

fields.name: SDR50SUP
fields.text: SDR50 Support.

fields.name: MAXCUR18V
fields.text: Maximum current at 1.8 V: I_max = 4 x MAXCUR18V mA; meaningful only when CA0R.V18VSUP is 1; at 0 it must be found another way.

fields.name: MAXCUR30V
fields.text: Maximum current at 3.0 V: I_max = 4 x MAXCUR30V mA; meaningful only when CA0R.V30VSUP is 1; at 0 it must be found another way.

fields.name: MAXCUR33V
fields.text: Maximum current at 3.3 V: I_max = 4 x MAXCUR33V mA; meaningful only when CA0R.V33VSUP is 1; at 0 it must be found another way.
