fields.name: LMIS
fields.text: Set when, with TMR.BCEN set, the descriptor table's total length differs from BCR.BLKCNT x BSR.BLKSIZE, or when the total length is not a multiple of BSR.BLKSIZE.

fields.name: ERRST
fields.text: ADMA state when an error stopped an ADMA transfer; never 2, as ADMA does not stop there.

values.name: ST_STOP
values.text: Stop DMA; the address is that of the descriptor after the one in error.

values.name: ST_FDS
values.text: Fetch descriptor; the address is that of the descriptor in error.

values.name: ST_TRF
values.text: Transfer data; the address is that of the descriptor after the one in error.

fields.name: ADMASA
fields.text: Byte address of the descriptor being executed. Set to the descriptor table start before ADMA starts; ADMA advances it to the next descriptor line to fetch. When EISTR.ADMA is set it holds a valid descriptor address according to AESR.ERRST. The table and this address must be 32-bit aligned; ADMA2 treats the low 2 bits as 0.

registers.name: PVR
registers.title: Preset Value Register
notes: One PVR applies according to the bus speed mode: PVR0 for initialization (3.3 V or 1.8 V), PVR1 for default speed (3.3 V), PVR2 for high speed (3.3 V). With HC2R.PVALEN 1, CCR.SDCLKFSEL and CCR.CLKGSEL are set from it and need not be set by the user. PVR0 is not chosen by bus speed mode: set CCR.SDCLKFSEL before initialization and set PVALEN after it. Preset values are not meant to be written by the user; they can be changed only while CACR.CAPWREN is 1.

fields.name: DRVSEL
fields.text: Value loaded into HC2R.DRVSEL when this preset applies.

fields.name: CLKGSEL
fields.text: Value loaded into CCR.CLKGSEL when this preset applies.

fields.name: SDCLKFSEL
fields.text: Value loaded into CCR.SDCLKFSEL when this preset applies.

fields.name: INTSSL
fields.text: Logical OR of the interrupt and wake-up signals of each SDHC instance: INTSSL[x] is SDHCx; the device has 2 instances.

fields.name: VVER
fields.text: Vendor version number; reserved, value may change, no function.

fields.name: SVER
fields.text: SD Host Controller specification version.

values.text: Version 2.00, with ADMA and test register.

fields.name: HDATLL
fields.text: Levels of DAT[7:4], for error recovery and debugging.

fields.name: FCD
fields.text: With e.MMC, 1 skips card detection through the CD signal.

values.name: DISABLED
values.text: Off: CD signal used, with debounce.

fields.name: RSTN
fields.text: Drives the e.MMC reset signal.

fields.name: BOOTA
fields.text: Set to match BOOT_ACK in the e.MMC extended CSD. When 1, the peripheral waits for the boot acknowledge pattern before boot data. A wrong pattern sets EISTR.BOOTAE when EISTER.BOOTAE is 1 (interrupt when EISIER.BOOTAE is 1); no pattern sets EISTR.DATTEO when EISTER.DATTEO is 1 (interrupt when EISIER.DATTEO is 1).

fields.name: OPD
fields.text: Sets the command line to open drain.

fields.name: DDR
fields.text: Selects e.MMC high speed DDR mode.

values.text: High speed DDR on; CCR divider DIV must be non-zero when HSEN is 1.

fields.name: CMDTYP
fields.text: e.MMC Command Type: marks e.MMC-specific commands.

values.name: STREAM
values.text: Stream read (CMD11) or stream write (CMD20); e.MMC up to revision 4.41 only.

values.name: BOOT
values.text: Boot operation starts at the next CR write; boot data are read straight from the e.MMC.

fields.name: ABOOT
fields.text: Writing 1 leaves boot operation mode; writing 0 is ignored.

fields.name: SRESP
fields.text: Writing 1 sends the CMD40 response automatically, taking the e.MMC from interrupt mode to data transfer mode; writing 0 is ignored. Effective only when MC1R.CMDTYP is WAITIRQ.

fields.name: BMAX
fields.text: Largest AHB burst used for DMA transfers.

fields.name: FSDCLKD
fields.text: Chooses whether SDCLK keeps running for 8 SDCLK cycles past the final read block's end bit, or past the end bit of a write's CRC status.

values.text: SDCLK kept; it cannot stop right after the transaction.
SDCLK not kept; it can stop right after the transaction.

fields.name: KEY
fields.text: Key; must be 0x46 for a write of CAPWREN to take effect.

values.name: KEY
values.text: Lets the CAPWREN write take effect; any other value aborts it. Reads 0.

fields.name: CAPWREN
fields.text: Write enable for the capabilities registers; writable only with KEY 0x46.

fields.name: NIDBG
fields.text: Non-Intrusive Debug.

values.name: IDBG
values.text: Debugger reads of BDPR advance the buffer read pointer.

values.name: NIDBG
values.text: Debugger reads of BDPR leave the buffer read pointer unchanged.

fields.name: RUNSTDBY
fields.text: Keeps GCLK_CCL running in standby sleep mode; has no effect in configurations that need no generic clock. Write it before the CCL is enabled.

values.text: GCLK_CCL is not needed in standby.

fields.name: ENABLE
fields.text: Enable: turns the CCL on.

fields.name: SWRST
fields.text: Software reset: a 1 returns every CCL register to its reset value; a 0 does nothing.

registers.name: SEQCTRL
registers.title: Sequential Control x
notes: Cannot be written while LUTCTRLx.ENABLE = 1.

fields.name: SEQSEL
fields.text: Selects the sequential configuration.

registers.name: LUTCTRL
registers.title: LUT Control n
notes: Cannot be written while LUTCTRLn.ENABLE = 1.

fields.name: TRUTH
fields.text: Truth table: the LUT output for each combination of inputs IN[2:0].

fields.name: LUTEO
fields.text: LUT event output enable.

fields.name: LUTEI
fields.text: LUT event input enable.

fields.name: INVEI
fields.text: Inverts the incoming event.

fields.name: INSELx
fields.text: Source of LUT input x (x = 0 to 2), four bits per input.

values.name: AC
values.text: AC: CMP[0] for LUT0, CMP[1] for LUT1, CMP[2] for LUT2, CMP[3] for LUT3.

values.name: TC
values.text: TC: TC0 for LUT0, TC1 for LUT1, TC2 for LUT2, TC3 for LUT3.

values.name: ALTTC
values.text: Alternate TC: TC1 for LUT0, TC2 for LUT1, TC3 for LUT2, TC4 for LUT3.

values.name: TCC
values.text: TCC: TCC0 for LUT0, TCC1 for LUT1, TCC2 for LUT2, TCC3 for LUT3.

values.name: SERCOM
values.text: SERCOM: SERCOM0 for LUT0, SERCOM1 for LUT1, SERCOM2 for LUT2, SERCOM3 for LUT3.

fields.name: EDGESEL
fields.text: Turns on the edge detector.

fields.name: FILTSEL
fields.text: Chooses the filtering on the LUT output.

fields.name: ENABLE
fields.text: LUT enable: turns this LUT on.

fields.name: CTYPE
fields.text: Counter measure type: one bit per countermeasure, each bit turning its countermeasure (1 to 4) on or off.

fields.name: XORKEY
fields.text: XOR key operation: a key word written to KEYWORD is XORed into what the key register already holds.

values.text: New key word is XORed with the old one.

fields.name: KEYGEN
fields.text: Last key generation: computes the final NK words of the expanded key.

values.text: Computes the final NK words of the key expansion.

fields.name: LOD
fields.text: Last output data mode.

values.text: Encryption runs in last output data mode.

fields.name: STARTMODE
fields.text: Chooses whether encryption or decryption starts manually or automatically.

fields.name: CIPHER
fields.text: Chooses encryption or decryption.

fields.name: KEYSIZE
fields.text: Length of the key used to encrypt or decrypt.

fields.name: CFBS
fields.text: Input block size in cipher feedback mode.

fields.name: AESMODE
fields.text: AES mode of operation.

fields.name: ENABLE
fields.text: Enable: turns the AES module on.

fields.name: SWRST
fields.text: Software reset: a 1 returns every AES register to its reset value and disables the module, and any other bits written alongside it are ignored; a 0 does nothing.

fields.name: GFMUL
fields.text: GF multiplication, GCM mode only: a 1 runs a GF multiplication of the data buffer content with the HASHKEY content.

values.text: Runs a GF multiplication of the data buffer with HASHKEY.

fields.name: EOM
fields.text: End of message, GCM mode only: a 1 produces the message's final GHASH.

values.text: Produces the final GHASH for the message.

fields.name: NEWMSG
fields.text: New message: in CBC, CFB, OFB and CTR modes, a 1 tells the module a message begins, so the first block is processed with the initialization vector.

values.text: Marks the start of a new message.

fields.name: START
fields.text: Starts an encryption or decryption in manual mode.

registers.name: INTENCLR
registers.title: Interrupt Enable Clear
notes: Turns interrupts off without a read-modify-write; the change shows in INTENSET too.

fields.name: GFMCMP
fields.text: GF multiplication complete interrupt: a 1 turns it off; a 0 does nothing.

fields.name: ENCCMP
fields.text: Encryption complete interrupt: a 1 turns it off; a 0 does nothing.

registers.name: INTENSET
registers.title: Interrupt Enable Set
notes: Turns interrupts on without a read-modify-write; the change shows in INTENCLR too.

fields.name: GFMCMP
fields.text: GF multiplication complete interrupt: a 1 turns it on; a 0 does nothing.

fields.name: ENCCMP
fields.text: Encryption complete interrupt: a 1 turns it on; a 0 does nothing.

fields.name: GFMCMP
fields.text: GF multiplication complete: goes high in GCM mode once the GHASHx registers hold the GHASH result. Writing 1 clears it, writing 0 does nothing; a manual start (CTRLB.START) or a read of GHASHx also clears it.

fields.name: ENCCMP
fields.text: Encryption complete: goes high when an encryption or decryption finishes and the result is in the data register. Writing 1 clears it, writing 0 does nothing; it also clears on a manual start (START), a read of INDATAx with LOD = 0, a write of INDATAx with LOD = 1, or a read of HASHKEYx.

fields.name: INDATAPTR
fields.text: Input data pointer: which of the four data words the next access at the INDATA address reaches; writing it moves the pointer.

fields.name: DBGRUN
fields.text: Debug run: 1 lets the AES keep running while the CPU is halted in debug, 0 stops it. Writable only while the AES is disabled.

fields.name: KEYWORD
fields.text: One 32-bit word of the key: four, six or eight registers hold a 128-, 192- or 256-bit key, KEYWORD0 first and KEYWORD3, KEYWORD5 or KEYWORD7 last. With CTRLA.XORKEY set, a write stores the XOR of the new word and the old content.

fields.name: INDATA
fields.text: Data access: each read or write reaches one of four 32-bit data words that make up the 128-bit block, the one chosen by DATABUFPTR.INDATAPTR. Input and output share this buffer, and a read returns zeros while an operation is running.

fields.name: INTVECTV
fields.text: One 32-bit word of the 128-bit initialization vector, INTVECTV0 first and INTVECTV3 last, used as an extra starting input by some modes. Write-only, so it cannot be read back. In CBC, OFB and CFB it is the initialization vector; in CTR it is the counter value.

fields.name: HASHKEY
fields.text: One 32-bit word of the 128-bit hash key, which the module derives from the AES key; it can also be written to run a single GF128 multiplication.

fields.name: GHASH
fields.text: One 32-bit word of the GHASH result of a GF128 multiplication in GCM mode. A fresh key written to KEYWORD resets it to zero; it can also be written.

fields.name: CIPLEN
fields.text: Cipher length: the number of bytes of ciphertext to process, set by software in GCM mode to produce the tag.

fields.name: RANDSEED
fields.text: Random seed: writing it reseeds the random number generator.

fields.name: RUNSTDBY
fields.text: Run in standby: sets whether the TRNG keeps running in standby sleep mode.

fields.name: ENABLE
fields.text: Enable: turns the TRNG on.

fields.name: DATARDYEO
fields.text: Data ready event output: when on, an event goes out each time a new random value is ready.

registers.name: INTENCLR
registers.title: Interrupt Enable Clear
notes: Turns interrupts off without a read-modify-write; the change shows in INTENSET too.

fields.name: DATARDY
fields.text: Data ready interrupt: a 1 turns its request off.

registers.name: INTENSET
registers.title: Interrupt Enable Set
notes: Turns interrupts on without a read-modify-write; the change shows in INTENCLR too.

fields.name: DATARDY
fields.text: Data ready interrupt: a 1 turns its request on.

fields.name: DATARDY
fields.text: Data ready: goes high when a new random value is made, raising an interrupt if INTENCLR/SET.DATARDY = 1. Writing 1 or reading DATA clears it; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: DATA
fields.text: The 32-bit random output value.

fields.name: R2R
fields.text: Enables rail-to-rail operation.

values.text: Rail-to-rail on; set only in differential mode.

fields.name: PRESCALER
fields.text: Divides the peripheral clock to give the ADC clock. Not synchronized. On the client ADC it has no effect while CTRLA.SLAVEEN=1.

fields.name: ONDEMAND
fields.text: With this bit set, the ADC runs only while a peripheral requests it and stays off otherwise; with it clear, an enabled ADC runs all the time. In standby, on-demand still works if CTRLA.RUNSTDBY=1; with RUNSTDBY=0 the ADC is off. Not synchronized. On the client ADC it has no effect while CTRLA.SLAVEEN=1; the host's ONDEMAND governs.

values.text: Runs only while a peripheral requests a conversion; off otherwise.

fields.name: RUNSTDBY
fields.text: Sets whether the ADC keeps running in standby sleep. Not synchronized. On the client ADC it has no effect while CTRLA.SLAVEEN=1; the host's RUNSTDBY governs the client in standby.

values.text: Keeps going in standby: on peripheral request if CTRLA.ONDEMAND=1, all the time if ONDEMAND=0.

fields.name: SLAVEEN
fields.text: Turns on host/client pairing; exists only on the client ADC. Not synchronized and settable only there; reads 0 on the host ADC.

values.text: ADC1 runs as client of ADC0.

fields.name: DUALSEL
fields.text: On the host ADC, picks how a trigger starts conversions in host/client mode. No effect while ADC1.CTRLA.SLAVEEN=0.

values.name: BOTH
values.text: A start event or software trigger converts on both ADCs.

values.name: INTERLEAVE
values.text: A start event or software trigger converts on ADC0 and ADC1 in turn; usable only with single conversions (CTRLB.FREERUN=0).

fields.name: ENABLE
fields.text: Turns the ADC on or off, after a synchronization delay. The written value reads back at once and SYNCBUSY.ENABLE sets; SYNCBUSY.ENABLE clears when the change has taken effect. On the client ADC it has no effect while CTRLA.SLAVEEN=1.

fields.name: SWRST
fields.text: Writing 1 returns every ADC register except DBGCTRL to reset and turns the ADC off; other writes in the same access are dropped. Writing 0 does nothing. The reset is synchronized; CTRLA.SWRST and SYNCBUSY.SWRST both clear when it is done.

fields.name: WINMONEO
fields.text: Enables the event output that fires when the window monitor detects a match.

fields.name: RESRDYEO
fields.text: Enables the event output that fires when a conversion result is ready.

fields.name: STARTINV
fields.text: Inverts the start-conversion event input. On the client ADC it has no effect while CTRLA.SLAVEEN=1.

fields.name: FLUSHINV
fields.text: Inverts the flush event input. On the client ADC it has no effect while CTRLA.SLAVEEN=1.

fields.name: STARTEI
fields.text: Lets an incoming event start a conversion. On the client ADC it has no effect while CTRLA.SLAVEEN=1.

values.text: Any incoming event starts a conversion.

fields.name: FLUSHEI
fields.text: Lets an incoming event flush the ADC and start a new conversion. On the client ADC it has no effect while CTRLA.SLAVEEN=1.

values.text: Any incoming event flushes and starts a new conversion.

fields.name: DBGRUN
fields.text: Sets whether the ADC keeps running while an external debugger halts the CPU. Not cleared by software reset. Write it only when no conversion is in progress. With host/client pairing on, host and client must hold the same value.

values.text: ADC stops while the CPU is halted.
ADC keeps running while the CPU is halted.

fields.name: DSEQSTOP
fields.text: When 1, DMA sequencing stops by itself once the last sequence configuration finishes; one further conversion still runs after that.

fields.name: MUXNEG
fields.text: Selects the negative ADC input.

fields.name: DIFFMODE
fields.text: Differential mode.

values.text: Differential: the ADC converts the voltage between the MUXPOS and MUXNEG inputs.

fields.name: MUXPOS
fields.text: Selects the positive ADC input. Choosing the bandgap or a temperature sensor channel requires a matching SAMPCTRL.SAMPLEN value from the operating conditions.

fields.name: WINSS
fields.text: When 1, the window compares each single conversion rather than the accumulated value; the count of matching conversions is in STATUS.WCC and the last sample's result is in RESS.

fields.name: WINMODE
fields.text: Turns on the window monitor and picks its condition.

fields.name: RESSEL
fields.text: Picks the conversion result width: 12, 10 or 8 bits.

fields.name: CORREN
fields.text: When on, RESULT is corrected for gain and offset from GAINCORR and OFFSETCORR; this adds 13 cycles to the conversion.

fields.name: FREERUN
fields.text: Free running mode.

values.text: Free running: each finished conversion starts the next.

fields.name: LEFTADJ
fields.text: When 1, the 12-bit result's high byte sits in the upper part of RESULT; 0 (default) right-aligns it.

fields.name: REFCOMP
fields.text: Enables offset compensation of the reference buffer, which lowers gain error at the cost of a longer reference start-up.

fields.name: REFSEL
fields.text: Picks the ADC reference voltage.

values.name: INTREF
values.text: Internal bandgap reference; its setting is SUPC VREF.SEL.

values.name: INTVCC0
values.text: Half of VDDANA; for VDDANA above 2.0 V only.

values.name: AREFC
values.text: External reference on AREFC; ADC1 only.

fields.name: ADJRES
fields.text: Division coefficient applied to the result, in powers of 2.

fields.name: SAMPLENUM
fields.text: Number of samples summed into RESULT. If the result grows wider, CTRLB.RESSEL must be changed.

fields.name: OFFCOMP
fields.text: When 1, the comparator offset is compensated in each sampling period for low offset and immunity to temperature and voltage drift; this adds three clock cycles, fixing sampling at 4 CLK_ADC cycles. Must be 0 for SAMPLEN to apply; OFFCOMP=1 with SAMPLEN>0 is not allowed.

fields.name: SAMPLEN
fields.text: Sampling time in CLK_ADC cycles, which sets the ADC input impedance: sampling time = (SAMPLEN+1) x CLK_ADC period.

fields.name: WINLT
fields.text: Lower threshold of the window monitor, when it is on.

fields.name: WINUT
fields.text: Upper threshold of the window monitor, when it is on.

fields.name: GAINCORR
fields.text: With CTRLB.CORREN=1, the gain-error correction applied before the result is stored: a fraction with 1 integer and 11 fraction bits, from 0.10000000000 to 1.11111111111 (1/2 <= GAINCORR < 2).

fields.name: OFFSETCORR
fields.text: With CTRLB.CORREN=1, the offset-error correction applied before the result is stored, in two's complement.

fields.name: START
fields.text: Write 1 to start a conversion or sequence; hardware clears it once the conversion begins. Writing 1 while it is set, or writing 0, does nothing.

fields.name: FLUSH
fields.text: Write 1 to flush the ADC pipeline: the ADC clock restarts on the next peripheral clock edge and conversions in progress are dropped. Clears when the flush is done; a pending conversion then starts anew. Writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: WINMON
fields.text: Write 1 to clear the window monitor interrupt enable; 0 does nothing.

values.text: Window monitor interrupt on; requests an interrupt when its flag sets.

fields.name: OVERRUN
fields.text: Write 1 to clear the overrun interrupt enable; 0 does nothing.

values.text: Overrun interrupt on; requests an interrupt when its flag sets.

fields.name: RESRDY
fields.text: Write 1 to clear the result ready interrupt enable; 0 does nothing.

values.text: Result ready interrupt on; requests an interrupt when its flag sets.

fields.name: WINMON
fields.text: Write 1 to enable the window monitor interrupt; 0 does nothing.

fields.name: OVERRUN
fields.text: Write 1 to enable the overrun interrupt; 0 does nothing.

fields.name: RESRDY
fields.text: Write 1 to enable the result ready interrupt; 0 does nothing.

fields.name: WINMON
fields.text: Sets one GCLK_ADC cycle after a window monitor match and requests an interrupt if INTENCLR/SET.WINMON=1. Cleared by writing 1 or by reading RESULT; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: OVERRUN
fields.text: Sets when RESULT is overwritten before the CPU read the previous value; requests an interrupt if INTENCLR/SET.OVERRUN=1. Cleared by writing 1; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: RESRDY
fields.text: Sets when a conversion result is ready; requests an interrupt if INTENCLR/SET.RESRDY=1. Cleared by writing 1 or by reading RESULT; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: WCC
fields.text: Count of samples that matched the window comparator. Writes have no effect.

fields.name: ADCBUSY
fields.text: Reads 1 while data acquisition is in progress. Writes have no effect.

fields.name: SWTRIG
fields.text: Set while the SWTRIG write is being synchronized across clock domains; cleared once it is done. Reads 0 on the client ADC while CTRLA.SLAVEEN=1.

fields.name: OFFSETCORR
fields.text: Set while the OFFSETCORR write is being synchronized across clock domains; cleared once it is done.

fields.name: GAINCORR
fields.text: Set while the GAINCORR write is being synchronized across clock domains; cleared once it is done.

fields.name: WINUT
fields.text: Set while the WINUT write is being synchronized across clock domains; cleared once it is done.

fields.name: WINLT
fields.text: Set while the WINLT write is being synchronized across clock domains; cleared once it is done.

fields.name: SAMPCTRL
fields.text: Set while the SAMPCTRL write is being synchronized across clock domains; cleared once it is done.

fields.name: AVGCTRL
fields.text: Set while the AVGCTRL write is being synchronized across clock domains; cleared once it is done.

fields.name: REFCTRL
fields.text: Set while the REFCTRL write is being synchronized across clock domains; cleared once it is done.

fields.name: CTRLB
fields.text: Set while the CTRLB write is being synchronized across clock domains; cleared once it is done.

fields.name: INPUTCTRL
fields.text: Set while the INPUTCTRL write is being synchronized across clock domains; cleared once it is done.

fields.name: ENABLE
fields.text: Set while the ENABLE write is being synchronized across clock domains; cleared once it is done. Reads 0 on the client ADC while CTRLA.SLAVEEN=1.

fields.name: SWRST
fields.text: Set while the SWRST write is being synchronized across clock domains; cleared once it is done.

fields.name: DATA
fields.text: Data the DMA writes here is passed on to the first ADC register enabled in DSEQSTAT.

fields.name: AUTOSTART
fields.text: ADC auto-start conversion.

values.text: Once a DMA sequence finishes, a conversion waits for a software or event start.
A conversion starts by itself once a DMA sequence finishes; ignored when EVCTRL.STARTEI=1.

fields.name: OFFSETCORR
fields.text: Includes OFFSETCORR in the DMA sequence.

fields.name: GAINCORR
fields.text: Includes GAINCORR in the DMA sequence.

fields.name: WINUT
fields.text: Includes WINUT in the DMA sequence.

fields.name: WINLT
fields.text: Includes WINLT in the DMA sequence.

fields.name: SAMPCTRL
fields.text: Includes SAMPCTRL in the DMA sequence.

fields.name: AVGCTRL
fields.text: Includes AVGCTRL in the DMA sequence.

fields.name: REFCTRL
fields.text: Includes REFCTRL in the DMA sequence.

fields.name: CTRLB
fields.text: Includes CTRLB in the DMA sequence.

fields.name: INPUTCTRL
fields.text: Includes INPUTCTRL in the DMA sequence.

fields.name: BUSY
fields.text: Sets when DMA sequencing is enabled or restarted; clears when it is disabled.

fields.name: OFFSETCORR
fields.text: Status of the DMA update of OFFSETCORR.

values.text: DMA update of OFFSETCORR finished or off.

fields.name: GAINCORR
fields.text: Status of the DMA update of GAINCORR.

values.text: DMA update of GAINCORR finished or off.

fields.name: WINUT
fields.text: Status of the DMA update of WINUT.

values.text: DMA update of WINUT finished or off.

fields.name: WINLT
fields.text: Status of the DMA update of WINLT.

values.text: DMA update of WINLT finished or off.

fields.name: SAMPCTRL
fields.text: Status of the DMA update of SAMPCTRL.

values.text: DMA update of SAMPCTRL finished or off.

fields.name: AVGCTRL
fields.text: Status of the DMA update of AVGCTRL.

values.text: DMA update of AVGCTRL finished or off.

fields.name: REFCTRL
fields.text: Status of the DMA update of REFCTRL.

values.text: DMA update of REFCTRL finished or off.

fields.name: CTRLB
fields.text: Status of the DMA update of CTRLB.

values.text: DMA update of CTRLB finished or off.

fields.name: INPUTCTRL
fields.text: Status of the DMA update of INPUTCTRL.

values.text: DMA update of INPUTCTRL finished or off.

fields.name: RESULT
fields.text: Conversion result, up to 16 bits depending on setup. A single conversion without averaging gives 12 bits: with CTRLB.LEFTADJ set, the high byte is in [15:8] and the other 4 bits in [7:4], so an 8-bit result can be read from the high byte alone; right-adjusted without oversampling, it is in [11:0]. With oversampling the result spans [15:0] according to AVGCTRL.

fields.name: RESS
fields.text: Result of the last conversion.

fields.name: BIASREFBUF
fields.text: Reference buffer bias scaling. Production-trimmed value; software copies it unchanged from the NVM software calibration row into CALIB to reach the specified accuracy.

fields.name: BIASR2R
fields.text: R2R amplifier bias scaling. Production-trimmed value; software copies it unchanged from the NVM software calibration row into CALIB to reach the specified accuracy.

fields.name: BIASCOMP
fields.text: Comparator bias scaling. Production-trimmed value; software copies it unchanged from the NVM software calibration row into CALIB to reach the specified accuracy.

fields.name: ENABLE
fields.text: Turns the AC on or off, after a synchronization delay. The written value reads back at once and SYNCBUSY.ENABLE sets; SYNCBUSY.ENABLE clears when the change has taken effect. Resetting with SWRST avoids spurious interrupts from enable/disable cycles.

values.text: AC on; each comparator also needs its own COMPCTRLn.ENABLE.

fields.name: SWRST
fields.text: Writing 1 returns every AC register to reset and turns the AC off; other writes in the same access are dropped. Writing 0 does nothing. The reset is synchronized; CTRLA.SWRST and SYNCBUSY.SWRST both clear when it is done.

fields.name: STARTx
fields.text: Write 1 to start one single-shot comparison on COMPx when COMPCTRLx.SINGLE and COMPCTRLx.ENABLE are both 1; otherwise, or if COMPx does not exist, it does nothing. Writing 0 does nothing; reads 0.

fields.name: INVEIx
fields.text: Inverts the incoming event for comparator x.

fields.name: COMPEIx
fields.text: Lets an incoming event start a comparison on comparator x. If several events are connected, any of them triggers the enabled action and the source cannot be told apart.

values.text: Any incoming event starts a comparison.

fields.name: WINEO0
fields.text: Lets the window 0 function produce a peripheral event.

fields.name: COMPEOx
fields.text: Lets the comparator x output produce a peripheral event.

fields.name: WIN0
fields.text: Reads the window 0 interrupt enable; write 1 to turn it off, 0 does nothing.

fields.name: COMPx
fields.text: Reads the comparator x interrupt enable; write 1 to turn it off, 0 does nothing.

fields.name: WIN0
fields.text: Reads the window 0 interrupt enable; write 1 to turn it on, 0 does nothing.

fields.name: COMPx
fields.text: Reads the comparator x interrupt enable; write 1 to turn it on, 0 does nothing.

fields.name: WIN0
fields.text: Sets on the condition chosen by WINCTRL.WINTSEL0 and requests an interrupt if INTENCLR/SET.WIN0 is 1. Write 1 to clear; 0 does nothing.

fields.name: COMPx
fields.text: Comparator x interrupt flag; reads 0 if COMPx does not exist. Sets on the condition chosen by COMPCTRLx.INTSEL and requests an interrupt if INTENCLR/SET.COMPx is 1. Write 1 to clear; 0 does nothing.

fields.name: WSTATE0
fields.text: Present state of the signal relative to window 0, while window 0 mode is on. It may change during start-up and measurement; to poll for a finished sample, use both STATUSB.READYx bits.

fields.name: STATEx

fields.name: FLEN

fields.name: HYST

fields.name: HYSTEN
fields.text: Turns on hysteresis for comparator n; available only in continuous mode (COMPCTRLn.SINGLE=0). Not synchronized.

fields.name: SPEED
fields.text: Must be set to 0x3 for every comparator n. Writable only while COMPCTRLn.ENABLE=0. Not synchronized.

fields.name: SWAP
fields.text: Exchanges the positive and negative inputs of COMPn and inverts its output, which allows offset cancellation. Writable only while COMPCTRLn.ENABLE=0. Not synchronized.

fields.name: MUXPOS
fields.text: Chooses what drives the positive input of comparator n. Writable only while COMPCTRLn.ENABLE=0. Not synchronized.

fields.name: MUXNEG
fields.text: Chooses what drives the negative input of comparator n. Writable only while COMPCTRLn.ENABLE=0. Not synchronized.

fields.name: RUNSTDBY

fields.name: INTSEL
fields.text: Picks the condition on which comparator n raises an interrupt or event. Writable only while COMPCTRLn.ENABLE=0. Not synchronized.

fields.name: SINGLE
fields.text: Chooses how comparator n operates. Writable only while COMPCTRLn.ENABLE=0. Not synchronized.

fields.text: 1 turns comparator n on, 0 off, after a synchronization delay. The written value reads back at once and SYNCBUSY.COMPCTRLn sets; it clears when the change has taken effect. Once 1 is written, the other COMPCTRLn bits are locked until ENABLE is written 0 and that write has synchronized.

fields.text: The 12-bit value DAC0 turns into a voltage: in DATA[11:0] with DACCTRL0.LEFTADJ=0, in DATA[15:4] with DACCTRL0.LEFTADJ=1. With dithering on, whatever LEFTADJ is, DATA[15:4] hold the 12 converted bits and DATA[3:0] the dither bits.

fields.name: DATA
fields.text: The 12-bit value DAC1 turns into a voltage: in DATA[11:0] with DACCTRL1.LEFTADJ=0, in DATA[15:4] with DACCTRL1.LEFTADJ=1. With dithering on, whatever LEFTADJ is, DATA[15:4] hold the 12 converted bits and DATA[3:0] the dither bits.

fields.name: DATABUF
fields.text: Value moved into DATA1 when a START1 event arrives.

fields.text: Sets what the DAC does while an external debugger halts the CPU; a software reset leaves this bit as it is.

fields.text: Interpolated value of the data written to DATA0 or DATABUF0, when the filter runs standalone (DACCTRL0.FEXT=1).

fields.name: RESULT
fields.text: Interpolated value of the data written to DATA1 or DATABUF1, when the filter runs standalone (DACCTRL1.FEXT=1).

fields.name: CAPTMODE0

fields.text: When 1, every overflow, underflow or re-trigger event sets LUPD; not synchronized.

values.text: LUPD left alone on these events.

fields.name: PRESCALER
fields.text: Picks the factor by which the counter clock is divided; not synchronized.

fields.text: Sets whether a stopped TC keeps asking for its clock. In standby with CTRLA.RUNSTDBY=0 it is held at 0. Not synchronized.

On: a stopped TC requests no clock until a software re-trigger command or an event with a start or re-trigger action arrives.

fields.name: RUNSTDBY

fields.text: Picks whether the counter wraps on the following GCLK_TCx clock or the following prescaled clock, and can also reset the prescaler; not synchronized.

notes: Clears CTRLB bits with a single write, no read-modify-write; every change shows up in CTRLBSET too.

fields.name: CMD

notes: Sets CTRLB bits with a single write, no read-modify-write; every change shows up in CTRLBCLR too.

fields.name: CMD
fields.text: Issues a software command, run on the next prescaled GCLK_TCx cycle; 0x0 does nothing and CMD reads back 0 once the command has run. The command needs synchronization: write CTRLBSET.CMD, wait for SYNCBUSY.CTRLB=0, then wait for CTRLBSET.CMD to read 0.

values.name: RETRIGGER
values.text: Force a start, restart or re-trigger.

values.name: UPDATE
values.text: Force an update of the double-buffered registers.

values.name: READSYNC
values.text: Force a read synchronization of COUNT.

fields.name: ONESHOT
fields.text: Writing 1 turns one-shot operation on; 0 does nothing.

values.text: Counter wraps and keeps counting at overflow or underflow.
Counter wraps and stops at the next overflow or underflow.

fields.name: LUPD
fields.text: Writing 1 sets LUPD; 0 does nothing. While CTRLB.LUPD is 1, a hardware UPDATE condition does not copy buffered values into their registers, so all buffers can be loaded before the lock is released. Has no effect with input capture enabled.

values.text: CCBUFx and PERBUF are copied into CCx and PER on a hardware update.
CCBUFx and PERBUF are not copied into CCx and PER on a hardware update.

fields.name: DIR
fields.text: Changes the count direction: writing 1 clears the bit so the counter counts up; 0 does nothing.

notes: Turns interrupts off with a single write, no read-modify-write; every change shows up in INTENSET too.

fields.name: MC0

fields.name: MC0

fields.name: MC1
fields.text: Set one CLK_TC_CNT cycle after a compare match or a valid capture lands in CC1, raising an interrupt if INTENSET.MC1 is 1. Writing 1 clears it, 0 does nothing; when capturing, reading CC1 also clears it.

fields.name: MC0
fields.text: Set one CLK_TC_CNT cycle after a compare match or a valid capture lands in CC0, raising an interrupt if INTENSET.MC0 is 1. Writing 1 clears it, 0 does nothing; when capturing, reading CC0 also clears it.

fields.name: ERR
fields.text: Set when a capture arrives on a channel whose match/capture flag is still set, leaving the new value nowhere to go. Writing 1 clears it; 0 does nothing.

fields.name: OVF
fields.text: Set one CLK_TC_CNT cycle after an overflow, raising an interrupt when the overflow interrupt is enabled (INTENSET.OVF or INTENCLR.OVF reads 1). Writing 1 clears it; 0 does nothing.

fields.name: CCBUFV
fields.text: Bit x shows channel x's buffer holds a new value. Compare channel: set by a write to CCBUFx, cleared by writing 1 while CTRLB.LUPD is 1 or by hardware on UPDATE. Capture channel: set when a capture is stored in CCBUFx, cleared when CCx is read.

fields.name: PERBUFV
fields.text: Set by a write to PERBUF; cleared by writing 1 while CTRLB.LUPD is 1 or by hardware on UPDATE. Exists only in 8-bit mode and reads 0 in 16- and 32-bit modes.

fields.name: SLAVE
fields.text: Set on the client TC (TC1, TC3) when its host TC (TC0, TC2) runs in 32-bit mode; present only in 32-bit mode.

fields.name: STOP
fields.text: Set when the TC is disabled, receives a Stop command, or overflows or underflows with CTRLBSET.ONESHOT=1.

fields.name: WAVEGEN

fields.name: INVENx

fields.name: MC1
fields.text: Writing 1 sets the Match or Capture Channel 1 interrupt enable, turning that interrupt on; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: MC0
fields.text: Writing 1 sets the Match or Capture Channel 0 interrupt enable, turning that interrupt on; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: ERR
fields.text: Writing 1 sets the Error interrupt enable, turning that interrupt on; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: OVF
fields.text: Writing 1 sets the Overflow interrupt enable, turning that interrupt on; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: MC1
fields.text: Set one CLK_TC_CNT cycle after a compare match, or when CC1 holds a valid capture; raises an interrupt if INTENSET.MC1 is 1. Writing 1 clears it, writing 0 does nothing; in capture operation reading CC1 also clears it.

fields.name: MC0
fields.text: Set one CLK_TC_CNT cycle after a compare match, or when CC0 holds a valid capture; raises an interrupt if INTENSET.MC0 is 1. Writing 1 clears it, writing 0 does nothing; in capture operation reading CC0 also clears it.

fields.name: ERR
fields.text: Set when a channel captures again while its Match or Capture flag is still set, so the new capture has no place to go. Writing 1 clears it; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: OVF
fields.text: Set one CLK_TC_CNT cycle after an overflow; raises an interrupt if the Overflow interrupt enable (INTENSET.OVF / INTENCLR.OVF) is 1. Writing 1 clears it; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: CCBUFV
fields.text: Bit x, compare channel: set when CCBUFx is written; cleared by writing 1 while CTRLB.LUPD is set, or by hardware on UPDATE. Capture channel: set when CCBUFx holds a valid capture; cleared when CCx is read.

fields.name: PERBUFV
fields.text: Set when PERBUF is written; cleared by writing 1 while CTRLB.LUPD is set, or by hardware on UPDATE. Present only in 8-bit mode; reads 0 in 16- and 32-bit modes.

fields.name: SLAVE
fields.text: Set on a client TC (TC1, TC3) when its host TC (TC0, TC2) runs in 32-bit mode. Present only in 32-bit mode on the client TC.

fields.name: STOP
fields.text: Goes to 1 on disable, on a Stop command, or on overflow/underflow while CTRLBSET.ONESHOT is 1.

fields.name: WAVEGEN
fields.text: Picks the waveform mode, which sets the top value and frequency or PWM output. Not synchronized. 0x0 NFRQ, normal frequency: top PER in 8-bit mode or MAX in 16/32-bit mode; output toggles on match, no action on wrap. 0x1 MFRQ, match frequency: top CC0; toggles on match, no action on wrap. 0x2 NPWM, normal PWM: top PER (8-bit) or MAX (16/32-bit); set on match, cleared on wrap. 0x3 MPWM, match PWM: top CC0; set on match, cleared on wrap.

fields.name: INVENx

fields.name: CAPTENx

fields.name: ALOCK
fields.text: When 1, every overflow, underflow or re-trigger event sets LUPD to 1. Not synchronized.

values.text: Overflow, underflow and re-trigger leave LUPD alone.

fields.name: PRESCALER
fields.text: Divides GCLK_TCx to make the counter clock. Not synchronized.

fields.name: ONDEMAND
fields.text: Sets whether a stopped TC keeps asking for its clock. Forced to 0 in standby when CTRLA.RUNSTDBY is 0. Not synchronized.

values.text: Off: a stopped TC (STATUS.STOP=1) still requests its clock.

fields.name: RUNSTDBY
fields.text: Keeps the TC running in standby. Not synchronized.

fields.text: Picks whether the counter wraps on a GCLK_TCx edge or a prescaled-clock edge, and can reset the prescaler. Not synchronized.

values.name: PRESC

values.name: RESYNC

fields.name: MODE

fields.name: SWRST
fields.text: Writing 1 resets every TC register except DBGCTRL and disables the TC; it overrides every other write in the same operation. Writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: CCBUF
